*If I attempt in this place to restore, by a new effort as it were, that imperfect and plainly crippled medicine of the ancients—of the Greeks and Arabs as well as the Latins—which was purely invented and written by pagans <note>original: "Ethnicis"</note>, washing it in the waves of truth itself and restoring it with the holy balsam of Wisdom <note>original: "Sophiæ Opobalsamo"; Sophia refers to Divine Wisdom.</note>, I pray it does not seem strange to you (Doctor most skilled in medicine as well as the mysteries of Divine Knowledge <term>theosophia</term> <note>Theosophy: Here referring to the study of God through the works of nature and Scripture.</note>), though it might perhaps seem worthy of wonder at first glance. Like King Ahaziah <note>original: "Azakia"</note>, they consulted Baal-Zebub <note>original: "Balzebubo"</note> or their false prophets for the sake of preserving or recovering health, neglecting Jehovah, the God of gods.*

*Therefore, since I have perceived that the invasions of diseases and the vexation of ailments are to be dissolved and driven away not by the uncertain conjecture or poorly-founded knowledge of these gentiles, but by holy virtue and divine truth, I have at last erased their sterile doctrine in medicine and their famished and uncertain knowledge in the art of healing. Thus, after the seduction of such a cruel and long-lasting error, and the exhaustion found in the series of fables from infidels regarding medicine, I might finally return myself to the longed-for apothecary <note>original: "myrothecio"</note> of truth—the sanctuary of the Scriptures, I say—which is most rich in sacrosanct wisdom. For who can bring forth the naked causes of natural things, if he is not a diligent and sincere investigator of true wisdom? Wisdom [Sophia] teaches us the most noble and profound secrets of medicine, and indeed of the whole of nature; she is the one and only mother of the sciences, since by her (as Scripture witnesses) we are taught all things. Can anything more absurd be devised among mortals not destitute of reason, than to grope in the darkness like the blind, seeking from the dung-heap of that shadowy fiction those things which in truth are to be found only in the bosom of light and truth, and drawn from it? Therefore, let us look first to God with contemplation and immovable faith, He who—with His good spirit assisting—will not deign to indicate and reveal to us Christians the straight line of knowledge and the direct and unerring way of healing and prognostication. ...it belongs to God alone to work all things in all, whether He be the cause of health or of diseases. Since those heathens <note>original: "Ethnici"; refers to the non-Christian Greek and Roman authorities.</note> were ignorant of this Christian standard, they falsely attributed to creatures those things that belong to the Creator alone, according to their own corrupt manner. And hence it was that they—as if submerged in the deep filth of Idolatry or sticking fast in the mud of ignorance—wandered entirely from the path, and thus vanished into their own imaginations. From this it happened that they accepted the creature in almost every work—indeed, even in the very practice of religion—in place of God their Creator. This, therefore, was the origin of universal ignorance, the beginning of the distraction of unity into multiplicity: taking the instrument <note>original: "organum"</note> (I say) which is driven by the internal and eternal acting principle, for the centrally moving and driving principle itself; and consequently accepting the shadow for the subject, and the fiction (I say) for the truth, in an unfitting manner.

Gentile physicians, therefore, recorded in writing that the primary cause of diseases is either heat or cold, or moisture or dryness, considering with a far-from-serious mind that God himself (as Scripture holds) effects and produces all these in the heaven or the air by His breath. Sometimes they posited either fire, or air, or water, or earth, but more frequently bile <term>cholera</term>, phlegm <term>pituita</term>, corrupt blood, or melancholy as the effectors of infirmities. Occasionally they imagined some of the macrocosmic <note>The "macrocosm" refers to the great world or universe, as opposed to the "microcosm" or the human body.</note> winds, or the inclemency of the air, or the evil influences of unfortunate stars, or their most wretched aspects (or some of them, speculating even more deeply) to be a striking angel, or some evil spirit dealing a blow, as the primarily efficient cause of diseases. Meanwhile, they failed to perceive that there is none among all these creatures that can bring either health or disease to another by itself, but only God, the one Jehovah, the creator and operator of all things, whose part it is (by means of His instrument, whether it be angelic, stellar, elementary, or windy) to act from the center, when and where He wills.

For the angel does not move or work, but God through the angel; nor the angel upon the star, but God by means of the angel and through the angel upon the star: and so in the rest. Whence it is certain that, according to the blameless testimony of the Apostle, God works all things in all, as He who, by the witness of the Prophet, does His will as much in the powers of heaven—that is, the angels and stars—as in the inhabitants of the earth, and there is no one who can resist. Finally, from Him, in Him, and through Him are all things: but from the creature, nothing; except by the operation of Him who said: *I make all things, I alone stretch out the heavens, I establish the earth and no one is with me.* This is to say: with no creature assisting, but I alone make and bring to completion all things that exist.

But what need is there for more words to one who is so well-versed in the controversies of scholastic Theology, and the secrets of medicine and Philosophy—indeed, who is hardly to be placed second to anyone? I know that you (most worthy Knight and most excellent Doctor) are not only most refined in all these things, but are also able to bring to light and put forth into public view things far higher than these. Indeed, not a few of the most learned men eagerly expect and gape for the desired fruit of your labor, which is (as I hear) ready for printing. Therefore, I have freely dedicated this treatise of ours to you, not for the sake of instructing you, but so that you might judge directly concerning it; for I have perceived your mind to be so fortified and enriched by a nature and virtue so generous and noble, that (the stings of calumny, the chara- <note>The text breaks off mid-word; likely "character" or "charactere."</note>

I pray, therefore, that you receive this **Medicine** of ours (whatever its worth may be) in good part, and run your vigilant eyes over it with your usual judgment. Its entire intention is to publish to the world, and to announce to everyone—Gentile and Christian alike—that God Himself, the creator of all things, is the one and only author, actor, and prince of life and health as well as of death and disease. It aims to show that not only we, but all creatures, exist in His hands, since it is His alone to wound and to heal, to strike and to make whole, to kill and to give life. Once this is explained to worldly Christians and diligently weighed by them—contrary to the doctrine of the Heathens—they might fear and venerate this unique author, actor, and worker of all things with a more sincere heart. # THE SUBJECT OF UNIVERSAL MEDICINE.

<note>original: "Medicinae Catholicae"; "Catholic" here is used in its original sense of "universal" or "all-encompassing."</note>

<image-desc>A large ramified diagram (scholastic tree) using curly brackets to outline the contents and structure of the work "Universal Medicine." This Universal Medicine is divided into two Volumes: Of which
* The First gives an account of health and diseases: and is divided into two Treatises. Of which
    * The First is organized into two Sections. And of these
        * The First discusses the origin of life and health.
        * The Second teaches the universal method of guarding and preserving well-being.
    * The Second has three Sections: Of which
        * The First treats the different kinds of diseases or morbid meteors. <note>original: "meteororum morbidorum"; in 17th-century science, diseases were often compared to atmospheric "meteors" or disturbances within the human body’s internal environment.</note>
        * The Second describes their courses.
        * The Third explains the various ways of prognosticating <term>prognosticating|predicting the likely outcome or end of a disease</term> regarding both recovery and death.

    * In the first Section [of the first treatise]

    * In the various Sections of the second [treatise], through medicines:
        * Divine and super-celestial.
        * Celestial.

# The Emblem

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'I' depicting a figure in a landscape with buildings in the background.</image-desc>
AT the peak or summit of the described Emblem, the head or root of all things is expressed, both in the simplicity of its unity and in the twofold nature of its most general property. One (I say) God, one supreme Being, one essence, or divine Mind, either willing or not-willing <note>original: "vel volens, vel nolens." In this philosophy, "not-willing" refers to God's state of contraction or withdrawal, rather than an active desire for evil.</note>. In its property of "not-willing," it contracts itself into itself and does not wish to send itself forth. For example: a single divine mind is present in man, yet its property is twofold; for at one moment a "willing" is observed, and at another a "not-willing." And although His refusal or negation might perhaps seem a great evil to the person seeking it, yet to the one who denies, it will be not an evil, but a good. For no one, moved from the very root of the mind, either denies or affirms except insofar as such a negation or affirmation is judged by them to be good, advantageous, or fitting. Thus, indeed, whatever God either wills or does not will is good, because in Him there is no evil. His "not-willing" <note>original: "noluntas," a technical term for the divine refusal to act or the withdrawal of light.</note> is therefore explained in many ways, both by grave philosophers and in the sacred writings. <margin>Pymander</margin> And first, *Hermes Trismegistus* <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the "Corpus Hermeticum," a collection of texts on philosophy, magic, and religion.</note> seems to explain this matter to its very core thus: *The Monad generates a Monad and reflected the ardor <note>original: "ardorem," heat or divine passion.</note> back into itself;* that is, it shone back upon itself and not upon others. This property of the *Pymander* <note>The "Shepherd of Men," the first book of the Corpus Hermeticum.</note> or of the divine mind, he called *divine power* <term>potentia diuina: the latent potentiality of God before taking action</term>, which is opposed to the divine act (not otherwise than darkness is opposed to Light). But in the property of "willing," He does not contract Himself into Himself, but from that region, He sends forth the rays of life and illuminates all things. We find these two properties in a single essence best explained in the sacred Text:

<margin>Psalms 104:29; Deuteronomy 31:17; Psalms 13:1, 11:16, & 31:6</margin>
> When God sends His spirit forth to the creatures, they are renewed by good; when He hides His face, they are troubled; when He takes back their spirit, they expire and return to their dust.

<margin>Job 10:12; Psalms 17:29.</margin>
> God leaves the wicked and hides His face from them, so that many evils befall them.

> How long will you hide your face from me? says David. Gladden me with your countenance; show your face to your servant. Your visitation preserves my spirit. If you light my lamp, O Lord my God, you make my darkness shine.

And we could bring forth infinite other testimonies from the sacred writing concerning this subject. The reason why "not-willing," or the hiding of the face, or the contraction of the divine ray into itself, will be the worst thing for creatures is this: Because the malignant spirits of darkness are stronger in those places where the presence of God is absent.

<margin>Psalm 139.</margin>
We conclude, therefore, that although God may seem to be darkened when contracted into Himself, yet Darkness and Light are the same to Him. For (as the Prophet testifies) *Darkness is not darkness to God; for they cannot be so darkened that He does not see through them. For to Him, the day and the darkness are as light itself.*

->B.<-

B. is the effect of divine power, or "not-willing"; in which state all things were unformed and existed only in potential for action before the creation of the world. Indeed, B. is the hieroglyphic image of God simply "not-willing" as of yet, in the middle of which God is in His true essence—luminous in Himself, but not sending Himself out of Himself. Such was the primordial Chaos, from whose depths the worldly matter originally arose. <margin>Pymander 3.</margin> Hence Hermes says: *There was an infinite shadow in the abyss; but water and a thin spirit were within the abyss.* So also:

<margin>1 Chronicles 6:1.</margin>
> The Lord confessed that He dwells in thick darkness.

<margin>Daniel 2.</margin>
> God reveals the deep and hidden things; He knows what lies in darkness, and the light is with Him.

<margin>Psalm 18:11.</margin>
> He made darkness His secret place; and with the darkest waters and thick clouds, He surrounded His tabernacle, so that they might serve Him in place of a veil.

<margin>Genesis 1.</margin>
> Darkness was upon the face of the deep.

We conclude, therefore, that of such a kind is the divine power—namely, the seat of God retaining His rays in Himself before creation, and contracting His act into potential after the creation of the world, and during the creation of the world; which power...

[...divine] power, or the contractive property, there follow darkness, chaos, formlessness, stillness, coldness, privation, death, diseases, sadness, fear, and melancholy: and its more primary root in the world is the Northern wind, and less so, the Western wind, the effect of which is to thicken nature into an earthy or watery state.

### C.

On the other hand, we have property **C**, which is entirely contrary to property **B**: just as the former was placed in will and potential, so indeed this one consists in will and act. Therefore, as **B** was the hieroglyph of the hidden God, or (to speak with the Kabbalists) the **Dark Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph tenebrosi." In Kabbalah, Aleph represents the beginning or the unity of God; the "dark" aspect refers to God in a state of withdrawal or hidden potentiality.</note>: so indeed **C** is the character of His glorious emanation for the creation of the world. This emanation is **Wisdom** itself, whose source (as the Scriptures testify) is the **Word**. Concerning which the sacred Text says:

<margin>1 John 1. Wisdom 7.</margin>
->God is Light, and in him there is no darkness at all.<-

<margin>Wisdom 8.</margin>
*She is the brightness of eternal light, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty God: a spotless mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. She is more beautiful than the Sun in her splendor, and being compared with the light, she is found prior to every arrangement of the stars: whence in her action she is more mobile than any thing; she reaches from end to end mightily, and orders all things sweetly.* <note>These verses are from the Book of Wisdom, traditionally attributed to Solomon.</note>

Therefore, just as the divine potential provides the "potential matter" for the creation of the world, so indeed this divine act provides the **form**, by means of which the said matter is shaped and adapted into the arrangement of the world sweetly and with ineffable harmony.

We conclude, therefore, that this **Emanation** is the **Word of God**, the true spiritual **Christ** filling all things: an incorruptible spirit in every thing, in which alone is life. **Eternal Wisdom**, created or sent forth before all things. The radical affirmation, position, or act of God: the central and radical light of things, day, life, form, the bond of harmony, pure love and benevolence, peace, the source of health and the sole preserver, **Jesus**; seeing as he is sent not to destroy, but to save the world. Finally, it is his work to thin what is thick, to purify the impure, and to make the deformed beautiful. This we have expressed in these few verses regarding the subject matter and the threefold explanation of that Almighty name:

### D. E.

## Emblem.

<margin>Pymander 3.</margin>
From the radical power of Being <note>original: "Entis radicalis potentia." This refers to God as the root of all existence.</note> and from its very act, union and the same number proceed while the Being itself remains: thus indeed, out of those two opposites, one World is forged according to the radical Exemplar of the creator. Hermes says: "There was an infinite shadow in the abyss. Moreover, water and his spirit were within the abyss. But a holy splendor flourished which, beneath the sand and the moist nature, led forth the elements; and heavy things, submerged in darkness, settled beneath the moist sand." <note>This is a paraphrase from the *Pymander*, the first book of the *Corpus Hermeticum*, describing a mystical vision of creation.</note>

<margin>2 Peter 3.</margin>
<margin>Wisdom 11:18.</margin>
<margin>Job 12:22.</margin>
Saint Peter says that the Heavens and the Earth were previously of water and through water, with the Word standing by. And the Wise Man says: "God created the world out of formless matter." Finally, Job says: "He reveals the foundations out of the darkness and brings the deadly shadow into the light."

<margin>Asclepius 10.</margin>
From this, therefore, Hermes concludes: that the World is moved within the vitality of Eternity, and that the place of the world is within that very vital eternity. For (he says) the world is itself quickened from without by eternity, and it quickens all those things that are within itself, distinguishing all things by established and prefixed numbers and times. For which reason he says elsewhere that "all mundane things are in the world, and the World is in God." From this he concludes that the place of the world is uncreated, but the world itself is partly created and partly uncreated: it is "born" if we look at the workmanship of the creation, but "unborn" if we look at the maker. For that reason, he says elsewhere that the Father of the World is God; but of those things which are in the World, the Father is the *Cosmos* <note>original: "Cosmus." In this context, it refers to the ordered universe as a secondary creative force or "Second God."</note>. Finally, he concludes elsewhere: "The first God made the second God (the World) according to his own image; but He made Man according to the image of the World."
<margin>Asclepius 7.</margin>
<margin>Pymander 9.</margin>
<margin>Pymander 8.</margin>

Finally, it is right to gather that this divine light is the Cornerstone of both the Heavens and the Earth. For He placed a Tabernacle in the sun of the earths. Whence Jehovah said to Job: *Who laid the cornerstone of the Earth?* Therefore, if we are able to open the Earth in a discreet manner, we may beyond doubt find in it that shining cornerstone, which is the foundation of every creature, so that by this method we may apply it to our salvation.

->F. G.<-

According to the mystic theology of Orpheus, Hesiod, Euripides, and Aeschylus (who involve in fables those mystical things which they learned from divine persons), they acknowledge a Divine Sun in the Archetype, from which is derived all ornament and numerous beauty encompassing the harmony of life. In its right hand is piety and benevolence; in its left hand is severity and punishment. They ascribe the mystery of this divine sun to the visible and created sun, which they call Apollo; they assert that he carries grace, life, and health in his right hand, but a bow and arrows in his left. Similarly, in another respect, they call him Bacchus and Dionysus, insofar as he is believed to tear himself and other creatures made by him to pieces during the night: but they say that in the daytime he is called Apollo, or Phoebus, who has dominion over the day and life; he composes those things which he tore to pieces and destroyed in the night under the name of Dionysus, and that in the sevenfold number <note>The "septenary number" refers to the seven planets or the seven stages of creation/destruction in alchemical and Pythagorean thought.</note>. For through the same number, Apollo proceeded in composition by his own nature. From this, it is argued that the same God is the author and actor of both destruction and composition—that is, of both corruption and generation—and that just as he composes through the number 7, so conversely he destroys through the number 7. For the number 7 is attributed to the author of life.

In the night, therefore—that is, in his privative and dark property, or when he is unwilling—he dissipates the members of the generated or composed thing under the name of Dionysus. But in the day—that is, in his positive, bright, and benign property, when he is willing and granting—the nature of the creature is created, generated, and preserved. Hence it is that the Athenians called Apollo *Alexikakon* <note>Greek: Αλεξίκακος, "The Averter of Evil."</note>, the driver away of evil; and the ancients used *Apellin* in place of Apollo, as a dispeller of evils; and Homer called him *Ulion* <note>Greek: Οὔλιος, "The Healer."</note>, that is, the author of health. This is according to that saying of David: *All creatures look to God in expectation. When God gives to them, they gather; when he opens his hand, they are satisfied with good; when he hides his face, they are troubled; when he takes away their spirit, they expire and return to their dust; when he sends forth his spirit, they are recreated, etc.* And Job says: *God placed man upon the earth, applying his soul to him; if he should take back or draw to himself his spirit or breath or soul, man would fail and...* <note>The text cuts off here, continuing the quote from Job 34:14-15: "...and return to dust."</note>
<margin>Psalm 104:29.</margin>
<margin>Job 34:13.</margin>

# Emblem.

<meta>The catchword "SANI-" at the bottom of the previous page would have completed a word like "sanitas" (health) or "saniret" (would heal), following the flow of the biblical paraphrase regarding God's power over life and death.</meta>

...would perish and all flesh would expire at once, and man would return to ash, etc. <note>original: "ret & expiraret omnis caro simul, & homo in cinerem reuerteretur &c." This is a reference to Job 34:15: "All flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust."</note>

From these things it is clear that it belongs to the **one God**—either by willing life through His presence (for He is life itself) or by not willing it through His absence (since His absence is death itself and privation)—to both kill and make alive, to wound and to heal, to strike with evil and to bless with good. For it belongs to Him, by His will and presence or act, to generate and preserve; just as by the withdrawal of His act into Himself, He deprives and destroys.

Moved by this line of reasoning, I have established the twin feet of this <term>Hieroglyphic Emblem</term><note>A "Hieroglyphic Emblem" in this period referred to a symbolic image meant to be "read" like a sacred mystery, often combining art and philosophy.</note>: namely, Day and Night, Light and Darkness, Good and Evil. Finally, we have established them as the various <term>Tabernacles</term><note>Dwellings or containers; here referring to the different "houses" or states of existence.</note> of life and death within the single World. 

Of these, we have fashioned—along with the aforementioned poets—the Prince as God Himself, transformed from one nature into another according to the arrangement of Light and Darkness. In the daytime <term>Hemisphere</term><note>One half of the world or the celestial sphere.</note>, we call Him **Apollo**, **Phoebus**, and the bright **Sun**, who works within it to fuse, create, and generate Man from a union of seven parts <note>A reference to the belief that man is composed of seven distinct physical or spiritual layers corresponding to the seven traditional planets.</note>. In the nocturnal hemisphere, however, we appoint Him **Dionysus** and the Prince of Darkness, following the well-conceived invention of the ancient poets. Indeed, the union of these two is nothing other than the **one God**, whether willing or not willing, who (as the Apostle <note>Saint Paul, in 1 Corinthians 12:6.</note> testifies) *works all things in all.*

<header>Hieroglyphics of the mystical fortress, page [blank]</header>

<margin>Wisdom 1:14 <note>original: "Sap. 1, 14. v."</note></margin>
He created the nations of the world, and there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor is the kingdom of the underworld upon the earth, etc. He concludes, therefore, that there would be neither disease nor death on the part of Divine Justice, since it gave eternal being to all things: for that Justice is the Word of God, of which not even one iota ever perishes. figment of Darkness which is in every way opposed to justice (which is that true daughter of Light). Hence the Wise man says in the following verse: *But injustice is the acquisition of death: The ungodly have summoned it with hands and words, and thinking it a friend, they have melted away, etc.* For this reason, it is necessary that he who desires to live in a healthy manner in this world

must live justly before his God, and according to the Apostolic rule, never cease to pray: that is (according to the sense of the Royal Prophet <note>King David</note>) *he should delight in the law of the Lord, and meditate upon it day and night; he should sincerely fear Him, and abstain from sin or injustice; he should contemplate in silence upon his bed, and sacrifice the sacrifices of innocence, and hope in the Lord.* Moses expressed this thus: *Worship Jehovah, your God, who will bless your bread and your water, and will take away every sickness from your midst, etc.* For this primary cause, therefore, we have imagined Man to be enclosed in a certain rocky fortification or bulwark full of
<margin>Ephesians 6:12.</margin>
Angelic power against Diabolical enemies, for the sake of protecting his health. *Put on* (says the Apostle) *the armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the snares of the devil, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against princes and powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places: therefore, take up the armor of God, that you may be able to resist, etc.* By this speech, he intends not only spiritual invasions, but also physical ones.

Therefore, let this Davidic petition always remain fixed in the soul of the just and God-fearing man—not only in a time of a raging plague, but also at every hour and moment let it be imprinted and revolved in his heart and memory; indeed, let it be uttered aloud with the highest humility of body and spirit, namely:

->Make your face shine upon your servant: Save me by your kindness,<-

<margin>Wisdom 7. Deuteronomy 30:10. Psalm 30:6. Psalm 36:9. Psalm 90:14. Psalm 10:12. Psalm 4:7. Psalm 15:29. Psalm 27:1. Psalm 80:4. Psalm 84:12. Psalm 106. Proverbs 3. Wisdom 16. Psalm 91:4.</margin>
For as the Word or divine wisdom is the *brightness of the emanation of the Almighty and the radiance of divine light:* so indeed Health and the preservation of life will be present by its presence. Hence Moses says, *Jehovah your God himself is your life, and the length of your days.* And David: *Life is present in the benevolence of Jehovah. The fountain of life is with you. And I could bring forth many other places from the sacred Text, which (for the sake of brevity) I omit.

Now, as to who those four Princes are, who are the leaders of the *Cardinal Winds*, we have explained above according to the opinion of Rabbi Tedaci Levi <note>Likely referring to a medieval Kabbalistic source or commentator</note> in the place cited before: namely, *Michael* of the East, *Raphael* of the West, *Gabriel* of the North, and *Uriel* (or *Noriel*) of the South. And although there are certain harmful angels—as the Revealer <note>The author of the Book of Revelation</note> witnesses—in whose power the forces of the winds lie, nevertheless these good princes are placed over them in power and dominion by divine will. This is because the Dragon, with his evil Angels, was conquered by them under the leadership of Michael. Therefore, the harmful evil ones can do nothing if these good princes are unwilling and do not permit it; for *the Angel ascending from the east commanded them not to harm until...* etc., and they were immediately obedient. 

Johann Reuchlin <note>A famous German humanist (1455–1522) and scholar of the Kabbalah</note> explained this best from the doctrine of the Kabbalists <note>Jewish mystical tradition</note>, saying that just as there are angels among us mortals, so the Devils have their own banners and standards. In the army of God, there are four Standard-bearers: Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael. They are like the four Elements according to the four directions, or according to the four spiritual enumerations <note>original: "numerationes spirituales," likely referring to the Sephirot or divine emanations in Kabbalah</note>, just as formerly the children of Israel set out with four banners: to the East <margin>Numbers 2</margin> was the banner of Judah, to the South was Reuben, to the West was Ephraim, and to the North was Dan. Likewise, in the army of *Satan*, the vengeful standard-bearers carry the widest veils: *Samaël, Azazel, Azaël, and Mahazael* with their troops and hellish legions.

Wherefore it is evident that the *good leaders* are those of the God of light—or the <term>divine act</term> <note>The manifest, active energy of God</note>—who is the Light of the World and the life of every Creature; in which (as John witnesses) *there is no darkness at all*. The others, who are called evil in respect to us, are those of the God who is hidden and contracted within Himself—that is, the emperor of darkness. This refers to the divine power which, from our perspective, appears opposed to the divine act in no other way than darkness itself is opposed to light.

Therefore, just as one attribute of God seems to contradict another, so also the nature of the spirits of light is most opposite to those of darkness: for the latter are destined by the God of light for disease and death, or privation and corruption; while the former are for health, life, generation, and establishment.

And although these properties seem to us who suffer to be entirely contrary, nevertheless, in the eternal root of God and the primordial Unity of the divine essence—whose nature it is both to hide Himself by contracting into Himself, and to manifest Himself by expanding out of Himself—these are nothing but one and the same source from which all things come.

# Hieroglyph of the Mystical Fortress, Leaf 88

<margin>Psalm 139</margin>
For what difference is there in the essence of my spirit <note>original: "mentis meæ"</note> when it grants or denies a petition? From this it follows that although God, by contracting Himself into Himself, makes all things dark and dead, He likewise shapes the universe with a most joyful light by emitting a ray of His countenance. And yet, to Him, Darkness and Light are the same; night and day are one. Therefore, Darkness is not dark to God, because things cannot be so obscured to Him that He does not see them beforehand, as the royal Psalmist <note>Referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> testifies. It is not, then, by their radical unity that the spirits of darkness are harmful to the children of light; rather, they are as "good" as the spirits of Light themselves, since both serve Him in ministry. However, to us who suffer, they are thought to be either good or evil. For the dark angels are as necessary to God in His property as **Dionysus** <note>original: "Dionysii." Here representing God’s hidden, severe, or "dark" aspect of justice.</note>—that is, in His severity—as they are in His property as **Apollo**, which is to say, in His mercy. In the property of mercy, He sends forth a benevolent spirit to the creature; and these spirits of light shall have dominion there. In His wrath or severity, He turns away His face and countenance, contracting Himself into Himself, and plunges the creature into darkness, leaving it in the power of dark and cruel spirits. In this act, the Ancients used to call Him **Dionysus**. Hence it is that we, who are children of life and light, are taught by the God of light—that is, by eternal wisdom or emanation—to walk in the light and avoid the ways of darkness, so that we may live strictly apart from the Prince of Darkness, the Devil, and the evil or dark Angels. Otherwise, we may be numbered among the children of darkness and be evilly tormented by those dark ones when the Lord hides Himself from us.

In this Emblem, therefore, we see in each Bulwark <note>original: "Propugnaculo"</note> of the square Fortress, arranged toward the cardinal points of the wind, a good and principal Archangel. These archangels, with drawn swords, drive back the wicked and malignant spirits—the greatest enemies of human life—who are sent from the four winds by the four harmful angels. To these four angels who have power over the winds, the wiser Teachers of the Hebrews have given names consistent with their natures. For the angel having power over the East wind, they named the East, or **Urient**; the West wind, **Paymon**; the North, **Egyn**; and the South, **Amaymon**. At their blast, those Demons who are princes of the Elements and leaders of those legions are moved and stirred with their cohorts to harm the earth, the sea, and the fruits or trees, and to turn the air into their own nature. These are the four who carry the wide sails of Satan: namely, **Samael**, who with his fiery spirits (insofar as he is held by the Hebrews to be the leader of the element of fire), when **Urient** slackens the reins of the East wind <note>original: "Euri"</note>, rides upon a **Dipsas** <note>A mythical serpent whose bite was said to cause an unquenchable, burning thirst.</note> and turns the Air back into his own fiery nature. We have depicted him riding upon the **Dipsas** because that species of serpent generates an immense thirst and intolerable heat in the one it wounds. Thus, he is observed to bring with him fevers, thirst, and burning, dry diseases during his lengthy dominion in the Air. He is resisted by **Raphael**, who is of the opposite nature, having his dominion in the West. Furthermore, **Michael** prevents him and his followers from entering the Fortress of the salvation of the righteous, according to the following sacred Texts:

<margin>Deuteronomy 28</margin>

### Description.

From this it is clear that God makes the air burning, feverish, and dry by means of the East Wind's blast <note>original: "Euri afflatu"</note>; for the Sun alone was not enough, but it was the hot and scorching Wind, which others interpret as the East Wind.

The second Standard-bearer of Satan is called **Azazel** by the Hebrews. Insofar as he is the Leader of the moist *Air* Element, he attacks the Southern bulwark of the health-bringing fortress with his airy, moist, and corrupt spirits, while the Angel **Amaymone** <note>One of the four kings of the cardinal directions in Renaissance magic; here associated with the South.</note> loosens the reins of the South Wind. He is depicted riding upon a **Basilisk** and surrounded on all sides by other venomous creatures. We have made him ride the Basilisk because, just as the Basilisk is said to infect and kill with its gaze alone from a distance, so do plagues and pestilential diseases affect us in the same manner. From this source come the plague, measles, smallpox, consumption <term>phthisis: a wasting disease of the lungs, typically tuberculosis</term>, and so on. This is confirmed by the following sacred texts:

<margin>Psalm 91:10</margin>
> "Do not fear the plague that walks in the darkness, nor the destruction that wastes at noon," or as Jerome <note>Saint Jerome, the 4th-century translator of the Latin Vulgate Bible.</note> interprets it, "from the attack of the **Noonday Devil**."

<margin>Deuteronomy 28:22; Habakkuk 3:5</margin>
> "The Lord shall strike you with fever, heat, and parching thirst, and with corrupt air until you perish. (Jehovah shall come from the South; His glory covered the heavens; before His face shall go death, or as Tremellius <note>Immanuel Tremellius, a prominent 16th-century Hebraist.</note> interprets it) **Plague** and the **Devil** are before His feet."

From these it is clear that the root of pestilential diseases is in the south; a fact which Hippocrates, in his *books on Epidemic diseases and Aphorisms*, and Galen in his commentaries upon them, seem to expressly acknowledge.

The third Standard-bearer of Satan is called **Mahazael**. Insofar as he is said to preside over the Element of Earth, he directs himself with hostility toward the Northern bulwark of the fortress of health. He brings with him his cold and dry spirits (while the Angel **Egyne** loosens the reins of the North Wind <note>original: "Boreæ"</note>), which constrict the air on all sides and tighten the waters. We have depicted him ascending upon a **Salamander** <note>In ancient lore, the salamander was believed to be so cold it could extinguish fire; here it represents the "freezing" of the body's natural heat.</note> and surrounded everywhere by his light-shunning spirits because, by his coldness, he extinguishes natural heat through mortification or freezing. He is also the author of melancholic and contagious diseases, especially from the direction of the North wind: see Leprosy, the Itch <term>Psora: a skin disease causing extreme itching</term>, Baldness <term>Alopecia</term>, mange, the scab, etc. From this come melancholic, numbing, and sorrowful diseases, according to these testimonies of Holy Scripture:

<margin>Job 27:9; Psalm 147:17; Deuteronomy 28; Job 37:9</margin>
> "By the breath of God, frost is given, and the waters are frozen. Who can stand against His cold? The Lord shall strike you with cold and blight until you perish, etc. The northern winds bring forth cold."

The fourth Standard-bearer of Satan is called **Azael** by the Hebrews. As the prefect of the Element of Water, he affects the air with moist and watery spirits and produces thick, cold, and humid rains, while the Angel **Paymone** relaxes the reins of the West Wind. He manfully and maliciously attacks the western bulwark of health, which the good Angel **Raphael** (with God’s assent) bravely defends. To this one are attributed Catarrh, running of the fluids, Dropsy <term>Hydrops: swelling caused by excess fluid in the body's tissues</term>, Epilepsy, Apoplexy, etc., about which the Sacred Page speaks everywhere.

->Biblical Testimonies of the moisture of this Wind in the Macrocosm <note>the universe/nature</note>, from which comes the Microcosm <note>the human body</note>.<-

<margin>Psalm 77:26; Exodus 10:13; Psalm 77:26; Numbers 11:13; Job 37; Proverbs 26; Genesis 41:6; Exodus 14:21; Exodus 15:8, 10; Psalm 10:3; Psalm 14:8; Ephesians 2:1</margin>
He brought the South Wind out of heaven and by His power He brought in the Southwest Wind <note>original: "Africum"</note>, and rained upon them, etc. How God truly works in the air by means of this wind; how He works through the East and North winds; and that the winds are called the "breath of Jehovah’s nostrils"; and for what reason God made the winds His Angels by His own breath; and that through these most powerful Angels He carries out His will both severely and mercifully—whence the Prophet says: *Stormy wind fulfilling the word of God*—is demonstrated copiously in the sacred writings. ### Hieroglyph of the Mystic Fortress, folio

<margin>Psalm 139</margin>
For what difference is there in the essence of my mind between granting a petition or denying it? It follows, therefore, that although God—by contracting Himself into Himself—renders all things dark and dead, so too by emitting a ray of His countenance, He informs the universe with a most pleasant light. Yet, to Him, Darkness and Light are the same; night and day are the same: *Therefore, Darkness is not Darkness to God, because things cannot be so obscured to Him that He does not foresee them, as the royal Psalmist <note>Referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> testifies.* Thus, the spirits of darkness are not harmful or "evil" by their fundamental unity [with God], but are as "good" as the spirits of Light themselves, since both serve Him in His ministry; it is only to us, who suffer their effects, that they are thought to be either good or evil. For the angels of darkness are just as necessary to God in His "Dionysian" <note>original: "Dionysii." The author uses Dionysus to represent God's hidden, dark, or "severe" aspect, contrasted with the solar "Apollonian" aspect.</note> property (that is, in His severity), as they are to Him in His "Apollonian" property (that is, in His clemency). For in the property of clemency, He sends forth a benevolent spirit to the creature, and the spirits of light will hold dominion there; but in His wrath or severity, He turns His face and countenance away—contracting Himself into Himself—and plunges the creature into darkness, leaving it in the power of dark and cruel spirits. In this act, the Ancients repeatedly called Him **Dionysus**. Hence it is that we—who are children of life and light—are taught by the God of Light (that is, by eternal wisdom or emanation) to walk in the light and avoid the ways of darkness, so that we may live strictly apart from the Prince of Darkness, the Devil, and his evil or dark angels. Otherwise, we may be numbered among the children of darkness and be evilly tormented by the dark angels of the Lord who hides Himself from us.

Therefore, in this **Emblem** <note>A symbolic illustration common in Renaissance books; here referring to an engraving of the "Mystic Fortress."</note>, we see in every Bulwark of the square fortification, arranged toward the cardinal points of the winds, a good and principal **Archangel**. These Archangels use drawn swords to repel the wicked and malignant spirits—those most hostile to human life—who are sent from the four winds by the four harmful angels. To these four angels who have power over the winds, the more sagacious Doctors of the Hebrews have given names consistent with their natures. For the angel of the **East** wind, who has the power of burning, they named **Orient** or **Urient** <note>meaning "The Burning One."</note>; the angel of the **West** wind they named **Paymon**; the **North** wind **Egyn**; and the **South** wind **Amaymon**. At the blasts of these four, those Demons who are the princes of the Elements and the leaders of those legions are moved and stirred up, along with their cohorts, to harm the earth, the sea, and the fruits or trees, and to convert the air into their own [harmful] nature. These are the four previously mentioned who carry the wide sails of Satan. See **Samael**, who with his fiery spirits (insofar as he is held by the Hebrews to be the leader of the **Element of Fire**) rides upon a **Dipsas** <note>original: "Dispada." A mythical serpent whose bite was said to cause unquenchable, burning thirst.</note> while the Eastern Urient loosens the reins of the East Wind. He converts the **Air** into his own fiery nature. We have depicted him riding upon the Dipsas because that species of serpent generates an immense thirst and intolerable heat in the victim it has wounded. From this, it is observed that he brings with him fevers, thirst, and burning, dry diseases during his prolonged dominion in the Air. **Raphael** resists him, for he is of the opposite nature, having his dominion in the **West**. Furthermore, **Michael** prevents him from entering the Bulwark of the salvation of the just with his followers, according to the following sacred texts:

### Description

From this, it is clear that God makes the air burning, feverish, and dry by means of the blast of the East Wind <note>original: "Euri." In classical wind lore, Eurus is the East or Southeast wind, often associated with drought.</note>; for the Sun alone was not sufficient, but rather the hot and scorching Wind, which others interpret as the East Wind.

The second Vanguard of Satan is called *Azazel* by the Hebrews. Insofar as he is the Leader of the moist element of *Air*, he—along with his airy, moist, and corrupt spirits—attacks the Southern rampart of the fortress of salvation. This occurs when the Angel *Amaymone* <note>Amaymon is frequently cited in grimoires as one of the four kings of the cardinal directions, usually ruling the East or South.</note> loosens the reins of the South Wind. We have depicted him riding upon a Basilisk and surrounded on all sides by other venomous creatures, because just as the Basilisk is said to infect and kill from a distance with its eye alone, so too do the plague and pestilential diseases affect their victims. From this source come the plague, measles, smallpox, consumption <note>original: "phthisis," a historical term for pulmonary tuberculosis.</note>, and so on. These following sacred texts confirm this:

<margin>*Psalm 91:6*</margin>
> Do not fear the plague that walks in the darkness, nor the destruction that wastes at midday—or as Jerome <note>Saint Jerome, the translator of the Vulgate Bible.</note> puts it, from the attack of the *Noonday Devil*.

<margin>*Deuteronomy 28:22*</margin>
> The Lord will strike you with fever, heat, and thirst, and with corrupted air until you perish.

<margin>*Habakkuk 3:3*</margin>
> (Jehovah shall come from the South; His glory covered the heavens; death shall go before His face; or as Tremellius <note>Immanuel Tremellius was a 16th-century Hebraist who produced a famous Latin translation of the Bible.</note> interprets it) *The Plague and the Devil are before His feet*.

By these passages, it is clear that the root of pestilential diseases is in the South; this is something that even Hippocrates (in his books on Epidemic diseases and Aphorisms) and Galen (commenting upon them) seem to expressly acknowledge.

The third Vanguard of Satan is called *Mahazael*. Insofar as he is said to preside over the element of *Earth*, he directs himself in a hostile manner toward the Northern rampart of the fortress of salvation. He brings with him his cold and dry spirits (while the Angel *Egyne* loosens the reins of the North Wind), which constrict the air on all sides and tighten the waters. We have depicted him ascending upon a Salamander and surrounded on all sides by his light-shunning spirits because, by his coldness, he extinguishes natural heat by mortifying or freezing it. He is also sometimes the Author of melancholic and contagious diseases, especially from the direction of the North wind that approaches the "Caecias" <note>The North-East wind.</note>; for example: leprosy, the itch <note>original: "psoram."</note>, mange <note>original: "alopeciam," referring here to hair loss or skin disease.</note>, scabies, the "itch," etc. From here come the melancholic, senseless, and sorrowful diseases, according to these testimonies of Holy Scripture:

<margin>*Job 27:9, Psalm 147:17, Deuteronomy 28, Job 37:9*</margin>
> By the breath of God, ice is formed and the waters are narrowed. Who can stand before His cold? The Lord will strike you with cold and blight <note>original: "rubigine," literally "red rust," often used for crop blight.</note> until you perish, etc. The Northern winds produce cold.

The fourth standard-bearer of Satan is called *Azael* by the Hebrews. He (being the prefect of the element of *Water*) affects the air with moist and watery spirits and produces heavy, cold, and humid rains when the Angel *Paymon* relaxes the reins of the West wind. He manfully and maliciously attacks the Western rampart of salvation, which the good Angel Raphael (by God's command) stoutly defends. To this entity belong catarrh, "the flux" <note>An excessive discharge of bodily fluids.</note>, dropsy <note>Edema or swelling.</note>, epilepsy, apoplexy, and so on, concerning which the Sacred Page speaks throughout.

# THE BEGINNING, OR PROLOGUE, IN WHICH
## The author, in a rigorous investigation of the eternal Monad <term>Monad: derived from the Greek *monas*, meaning "unity" or "one." In Hermetic and Pythagorean philosophy, it represents the first principle, the indivisible source of all numbers and the entire universe—God.</term>, explains its difficulty and depth in the manner of a hymn; he implores the help of the Divine Word and Wisdom to unlock such a great mystery; and finally, he invokes the aid of the paternal Monad, sings of its omnipotence with awe, and gives immense thanks for its blessings.

*Pay heed, O World, image of holy eternity; hear, O heaven and earth, adorned with the splendor and glory of divinity; listen, you precious members of the Cosmos, and let all creatures within it be struck with wonder. For I begin to sing and trumpet forth to you the immense existence of the Creator before all time, and before the ages had received their beginning, from the very point of eternity. For who can reach the hidden knowledge of the Father—what He is, of what nature, and where He may be—unless it be His Son, and he to whom the Son has chosen to reveal Him?*

*O, how deep and hidden are the things I now prepare to make known to the world! With what amazement and fear do I feel myself shaken and trembling, considering the smallness of the spark of my own mind as I set about unfolding and explaining this immense, incomprehensible, and abstruse work. And had I not seriously considered the nobility of the human mind; had I not diligently reflected upon that mind being contained within the Word—as the Word or eternity is contained within God; had I not contemplated somewhat more accurately His immense virtue and power in the subtle investigation and revelation of hidden things; and had I not understood that Divine Wisdom (whose role it is to teach all secrets) finds delight, familiarity, and conversation with the sons of men (through the mediation of the mind itself); I would have considered it ill-advised and otherwise too reckless to plunge and cast myself into an Ocean of such depth and into so high and hidden an abyss of darkness. *Behold then, O Eternal Father! Led by Your luminous Son, I humbly desire to bring the rays of my mind to Your exalted majesty, imploring above all Your remarkable grace and mercy in so difficult an undertaking. For though You are One, Your Unity nevertheless exists in all things and in everything. There is nothing in all of nature which You Yourself are not; and yet, You can nonetheless be called "Nothing," <note>This refers to the concept of "Nothingness" in mystical theology (the *via negativa*). You, immobile and remaining stable, compel all things to move within Your manifest property; yet in that hidden property, You constrain and bind them by the secret link of rest (contracting the infinite power of Your Monad into itself). ### Preface on the Vastness of the Monad.

*...the same, you, the simple one <note>In this context, "simple" means "not made of parts" or "indivisible," a key attribute of the Divine in philosophical theology.</note>, in yourself, through yourself, and around yourself remain full, perfect, and eternal, thereby clearly proving to your creatures that you are infinite, incomprehensible, and wonderful. Although you embrace all existence—beyond which there is nothing—you nevertheless extend the power of your essence even beyond that "nothing."*

*From your unity, therefore, as from a single and sole principle, all things depend; and yet you, one and the same (never receding from the degree of unity), are accustomed to excel. For in your manifest nature, you strive to act and perfect all things at every moment of time: namely, in the heaven, in the air, in the earth, in the sea—in short, in the whole world and in every tiny part of it. For this reason, you alone are the sole Monad <term>Monad: from the Greek *monas*, meaning "unit." You are the source of both darkness and light, just as the number two <term>binary: in Pythagorean thought, the "dyad" or number two represents the first step away from unity into division and plurality.</term> took its birth and beginning from unity. Thus, at last, with a clearer vision, I may proceed to the manifest and open laws of your character, and to the ineffable acts of creating the world and adorning it with honor and beauty, to be published and made known to the world. For yours alone is the kingdom, the act, the power, and the wisdom forever.*

### CHAPTER I.

->*In which the Divine disposition, hidden and lurking in darkness, is discussed, and the rise and origin of darkness is presented.*<-

<image-desc>A decorative square woodcut initial 'V' containing floral and leaf patterns.</image-desc>

Just as those most skilled in Arithmetic could conceive of nothing prior to or more ancient than Unity <note>original: *Vnitate*</note> (from which they recognized it to be the simple and sole root of number and multitude), so they noticed that Unity, taken absolutely in and of itself, has no relation to any specific number, nor is it limited by any size or dimension, nor included in any number, nor divided into any parts, nor, finally, defined by the "whatness" <note>original: *quidditate*, a scholastic term for the essence or "what-it-is" of a thing.</note> of its substance. From this, with a slightly more accurate gaze and observation, they perceived it to be the primary and most ancient principle of all things, encompassing within itself all things—whether substantial or quantitative, and indeed even the qualities themselves—in their proper proportion. It is no different from how we see the point of Geometry considered in its naked and pure nature: indivisible, barely perceptible, and terminable as almost nothing. Yet, it nonetheless exists as the infallible beginning and origin of any line or other mathematical dimension, insofar as the point itself embraces and contains all magnitudes, while being encompassed by none of them.

These two things, then—the Principles of all Numbers and Dimensions—those wiser in Mathematics <term>Mathesi: a term encompassing the quadrivium of arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy, seen as the keys to understanding the structure of the universe.</term> found to be most worthy in order and most ancient in duration, fashioned after the imitation or image of the internal and most central point of the Divinity, or the most Holy and Radiant Monad <term>Monad: from the Greek *monas*, meaning "unity" or "the one." In this philosophical context, it refers to the singular, indivisible source from which all reality flows.</term>, in which there is no darkness at all, which was contracted and hidden within itself before the creation of the World, and in its absolute Unity...

Volume I, Treatise I, Section I, Part I, Book I.

...[immensi]ty and Simplicity, remaining without any consideration for the creation of things or for a creature brought into being. In this state and condition, He cannot be considered "God," insofar as He has not yet produced a creature by whom He might be adored as God; nor can He be called "Father," since He has not yet seemed to think of any offspring, whether ideal and archetypal <note>The "archetypal" world refers to the divine blueprint or idea of the world existing in the mind of God before physical creation.</note>, or typical and worldly. Nor is He to be judged as "Good," insofar as He has not yet tasted of the dark or hidden Goodness of the World’s matter or dark <term>hyle</term> <note>original: *hyle*. A Greek term used by ancient philosophers and later alchemists to describe "prime matter"—the raw, formless "stuff" of the universe before it is given shape.</note>. Neither could He be called "Beauty," because He has not yet decorated anything with His beauty; nor "Eternity," because He has not yet seemed to exist to human understanding, and consequently He was seen to be associated neither with eternity, nor an age, nor time, nor did He claim the name of "Beginning," because He was recognized as having no relation yet to anything that has a beginning. Finally, the nature of this most holy Monad, hidden within itself, is so secret and obscure—its essence so unknown in order and antiquity, and so imperceptible and incomprehensible—that it appeared to be neither a "what," nor a "how much," nor a "what kind." Rather, it was conceived as a certain transcendent Being, reserved within itself and consisting only of itself, in whose power all these things existed, as if located in a Place. Wherefore, those most skilled in the laws of true Wisdom concluded that this Infinity, since it was contracted in an abyss of darkness and remained idle—or (as they say) looking toward nothing—was therefore called <margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*.</margin> איין <note>original: *Ayin*</note>, that is, "Nothing," or "Non-Being," and "without end." This is because we, being punished with such a meager poverty of intellect regarding divine matters, judge those things which do not appear in the same way we judge things that do not exist.

*Hence, it is for this reason that, just as this indivisible Unity led those things which now exist through creation into the light by its manifest property, so indeed by its secret and hidden disposition, it hid within itself those things which are not.* By this, it seems clearly enough declared that this stupendous and never-sufficiently-admired unique Power, or this central Nature, is accustomed to turn what exists into nothing by the contraction of its rays into itself—that is, to leave them dark and deformed. Nevertheless, the divine power remains within them, through which it is possible for them to be brought back into action according to the will of that Power that hides itself. But in truth, they are called "nothing," "darkness," "empty," and "void" <note>This refers to the *Tohu wa-bohu* of Genesis 1:2.</note> insofar as they are not yet formed or enriched by divine light; for form is said to attribute a name and being to any thing. *God (says Job) stretches out the North over the empty and void; and hangs the earth upon nothing.* And Moses calls such a thing *an empty and void earth.* And Solomon says, *The World was created from unformed matter; or as Jerome interprets it, invisible matter.*

From these things, it is clear that just as this Imperial Monad embraces, uncovers, creates, and forms all existence by its manifestation—or by the dilation and emission of its rays—so indeed, outside this existence, there is nothing; just as outside of "nothing," this Unity is pure. Therefore, from these points, the incomprehensible and infinite Excellence of this Nature seems more clearly declared than by the Sun: though it is One, it is capable of all things; though it exists within all things, it nevertheless rules outside all things. And finally, though it is the supreme Divinity of light and lives, it is nonetheless the one and only ruler and Emperor of the darkness. Thus (according to the sentiment of the Royal Psalmist), *as is its darkness, so is its light.* By these words, he seems to prove the Monad to be the most hidden of all things, and yet again the most manifest of all. And this is why men skilled in the Kabbalah called that primordial monad or unity, in its abstruse and hidden disposition, the "dark *Aleph*." Now, the Hebrews used *Aleph* to signify arithmetical unity, which they called "dark" when, by immersing itself in gloom—that is, by contracting its rays into itself—it seems to look toward almost nothing. Conversely, when it emits its light, they called it the "bright *Aleph*," asserting then that *Aleph*...

We perceive, therefore, from what has already been said, that darkness itself is nothing other than the contraction of the light—or the rays of the simple and uncreated Monad—into itself; namely, when it pleases the Creator to withhold or turn away His bright face from the act of recreating and giving form. In this act of His, Darkness is seen to hold dominion over the entire face of the rough Abyss. Therefore, just as in this contracted disposition of the Monad, it is said to rest within itself, having regard for nothing and acting in no thing, but being present only to itself: so indeed that deformed disposition of <term>hyle</term> <note>original: *hyle*. A Greek term for "prime matter" or the raw, formless substance of the universe before God gave it shape.</note>—which for this reason is called darkness and gloom—is seen to acquire a similar inclination. Being deprived of light, it is covered over with gloom and darkness; for due to the absence of the divine light itself, darkness and gloom are produced and are said to have been "upon the face of the Abyss." Furthermore, while the Monad’s act rests within itself—that is, while it is contracted and its rays are contained within—that same deformed matter or dark *hyle*, being utterly destitute of bright and active form, is inclined toward a certain natural appetite for rest and stability. For just as it is devoid of heat (which is the effect of light), so it lacks the actions by which it might be stirred to motion through heating. Indeed, in this it imitates the nature of the radical Monad, insofar as the Monad is always immobile, stable, and fixed within itself <margin>Wisdom 7</margin> <note>A reference to the Book of Wisdom, Chapter 7, describing the nature of Divine Wisdom.</note> and constantly remaining within itself, even though in its dilated condition nothing is more mobile or swift than it, as will be shown more extensively below. Finally, this mass of darkness is seen to enjoy coldness and to embrace it as its innate quality; for that quality is recognized to have chief dominion where heat is observed to be absent. Why then should we be moved by further doubt in this matter? Since we have received from the <term>Tetragrammator</term> <note>The author likely means God, the author of the *Tetragrammaton* (the four-letter name of God, YHWH).</note> himself—from the Oracle of that holy Monad, I say—that *he dwells in thick darkness.* <margin>1 Chronicles 6:1</margin> <note>The Latin text cites 1 Chron. 6:1, though this passage is traditionally found in 1 Kings 8:12 or 2 Chronicles 6:1: "The Lord said that he would dwell in the thick darkness."</note> Or what is more absurd than to think that He (who can do all things) cannot, according to His good pleasure, send forth the holy emanation of His will out of the darkness, and that it (at the command of the radical Monad) cannot emerge from the gloom? Since it is decreed by the holy page and committed to eternal memory that darkness cannot so overshadow Him that He does not see through it; for to Him, black and dense obscurity and the dark night are as light and the noonday sun. For although this root of Divinity is said to have been able to make a hiding place in His circuit, yet He was not so hindered or enveloped by darkness that, before the brightness in His presence, the gloomy clouds were not kindled into coals of fire. <margin>2 Samuel 22:12</margin> <note>The text cites "2 Reg. 22. 8," which refers to the Vulgate numbering for 2 Samuel 22:13.</note>

You have here, therefore, the one of the two Extremes, namely the dark one; whose author, power, and supreme Empress is the radical Monad, the most ancient of all things, hidden and stored away within itself in the most abstruse manner. Thus, darkness of this kind is not impertinently or incorrectly called by the sanctuary of Truth the vehicle of God, His dense cottage, and His covering, <margin>Job 22:15. Psalm 104. Psalm 105. Pimander.</margin> <note>The author cites various biblical Psalms and the *Pimander* (a core text of the *Hermetica* attributed to Hermes Trismegistus).</note> as if one were to say with the divine Philosopher: *that the Monad, before the beginning of the World, shone for itself and not for others.* In which state, nevertheless, we shall prove that it is able to do all things in its simple Nature; that it comprehended all things, both created and uncreated, within itself; and this clearly, by the following demonstration. For we are taught by the diligent observation of <term>Cossic numbers</term> <note>original: *numerorum Cossicorum*. "Cossic" comes from the Italian *cosa* ("thing"), an early term for algebra. It refers to the study of roots, powers, and unknowns.</note> that *all things whatsoever exist as either Roots, or Squares, or Cubes, or are composed from them.* By "Roots" are meant the *principles of all things*; by "Squares," *simple and spiritual things derived from principles*; and by "Cubes," *composites of simple derivatives (such as are corporeal things).* By the same reasoning in a Geometric respect: the *Line*, which is the beginning of triple dimension, corresponds to the *Root*; the *Surface* to the *Square* (which the parts of a line multiplied by themselves are accustomed to produce); and the *Body* to the *Cube*, produced by the multiplication of the Square by the Root. Now indeed, if one considers the nature of the Monad, or Unity, contracted into itself...

## CHAPTER II.

### *Concerning the Archetypal or Intellectual World, and how it was ordained from the Monad and within the most sacred Monad through the number three.*

<margin>Asclepius 12. <note>Refers to the *Asclepius*, a famous Hermetic text from late antiquity.</note></margin>
Therefore, so that before all things that luminous and purely formal source might have had its Existence in and from itself—as it remains and stands eternal in itself, from itself, and through itself—it follows as if granted that it is the only and unique simple and absolute Principle, from which, in which, and through which all other things are derived, whether they be principles or things originating from principles. For that this Monad is the Root, origin, and beginning of all principles is chiefly explained by the fact that without a true principle, there is nothing: for there is no beginning of an absolute principle, but only of that which is created from it. Truly, the Monad or Unity is also declared to be that principle which comprehends every number within itself, and is comprehended by none. The same privilege the geometric point seems to claim for itself in the threefold dimension of Quantity. <note>Just as a point has no dimensions but defines the line, surface, and solid, the Monad defines all reality without being divided by it.</note> For this reason, that which...

it is increased, whether in Quantity or in Quality, by the power of the Monad; and <margin>Pimander, Book 4</margin> vice versa, it seems to vanish by its own weakness when it can no longer contain the Monad. From this, therefore, it follows that neither the raw and undigested mass of darkness, nor that created light, can rightly be called absolute Principles in their most opposite disposition: insofar as they themselves have an origin from which they arise, no less than the binary number <note>The number two.</note> has its own origin, insofar as it is derived from unity. Hence, this binary number is called a "confusion of Unities" by Pythagoras, and not without reason. <note>Pythagoras viewed the number 2 as the beginning of differentiation and conflict, moving away from the perfection of the 1.</note> And yet we call both darkness and light "Principles" in a comparative or relative sense, insofar as they seem to participate in the twofold property, nature, and varying quality of the Unity or Monad (namely, that which consists in the expansion and contraction of the radical Monad). Thus, we see that the entire diverse force of these two beginnings, and their strength striving in opposition, is comprehended in one. For this reason, the highest Father of things is absolutely called the "only and sole Good," in whom all things are good; completely beautiful and perfect. Other things, namely created things, which arise from the perfection of this Monad, are called good, beautiful, and perfect only comparatively and through participation in His formal goodness and beauty.

In this way, many principles are established in the nature of things, proceeding from a single, pure, and truly simple and radical origin: namely, Light, Darkness, and the Waters, flowing as if immediately from the fountain <term>Ensoph</term> <note>original: *Ensoph*. In Kabbalah, this refers to the Infinite, the divine origin of all things before they take form.</note>. Similarly, the four Elements can be called "secondary" principles, which proceed from the Monad medially (through an intermediary) and from the secondary sources immediately; and so it is with the rest. Since all these are creatures, it <margin>Pimander, Book 10</margin> certainly follows that it is necessary for the Creator to precede them in the order of His Eternity and be presupposed for their existence. This Creator is neither born (insofar as He comprehends Eternity itself), nor does He admit anything before Himself, or anything equal to Himself—whether in time, age, or eternity, or in dignity, goodness, and the excellence of beauty. From this, therefore, it follows that just as He is called the principle and head of all principles whatsoever, so it is necessary that He comprehends within Himself both the principles and those things derived from the principles. Wherefore both Hermes and the Apostle <note>Likely St. Paul, whom Renaissance thinkers often compared to Hermes Trismegistus regarding the nature of the divine.</note> himself, <margin>Pimander, Book 5</margin> agreeing with Hermes in this matter, seem to coincide in this single sentiment, namely: *That God is all things, not only those which are, but also those which do not yet exist.* "Shall I sing," he says, "your praises in those things which you have brought forth from darkness into light? Or in those things which still lie hidden, stored away in the secret womb?" <note>original: *Cantabone laudes tuas...* This is a paraphrase from the *Corpus Hermeticum*, specifically the *Poimandres* or *Pimander*.</note>

The Monad, therefore (which is itself Eternity), contains eternity; eternity contains the world, the world contains time, and time contains generation. In these, one may see that just as eternity—or the Word—proceeds from the radical monad like a son from a father, so from that Word (which is itself eternity) proceeded wisdom or the <term>aeon</term> <note>An "aeon" refers to an eternal age or a divine power emanated from God.</note> (which was created before all things); from which the world then drew the power and soul of its life, and time received its ordinations.

To the Wise man, therefore, it cannot be hidden how God, though He is one and the One, is nevertheless said to be in all things, and embraces all things just as a place embraces that which is placed within it. For in time there is increase and decrease, or generation and corruption; in the world, and by the soul of the world, time is established, governed, numbered, and measured. The world exists in the aeon; the aeon in eternity; for the fountain of Wisdom is the Word itself. Finally, eternity consists in the Monad itself, no differently than life consists in the soul. The world itself is the image of the divine Monad, but the Monad is the image of nothing. God the creator is the Monad, purely formal in and through Himself, the wonderful Being of beings; the world is purely material in and through itself, existing by the power of the hidden and formal Monad, from which it has received life, goodness, clarity, and beauty by way of participation.

### On the Supercelestial Origin of Life and Health.

And [the Monad] now at length sends forth the light of its face—which was once hidden and contracted within itself—and reveals it out of the darkness. In this way, the second monad is brought forth; and finally, by the reflection of that emanation back into its own root, the third power is produced. Through this [third power], the return of the triple number into its uniform root is achieved. From this has arisen an inseparable union between the nature of the God who is hidden and the God who is manifest; specifically by the power of the third property, whose role is to confirm the duality within unity through the bond of love. We see, therefore, that these three monads in the Archetype <note>The "Archetype" is the divine blueprint or original model of the universe in the mind of God.</note> constitute only a single monad in their essence, although they appear to vary by the distinction of their properties. This is no different than how we observe the same Unity, when multiplied by itself, claiming the properties of the Square Root and the Cube; yet in the end, we find nothing except a single unity in essence. This is the beginning, the middle, and the end; and consequently, it is everything that exists: the *Alpha and Omega*, the *Circle including all things*, whose nature it is to return into that which it was, and nevertheless always remains within itself everything that was, is, and shall be. For this Monad, insofar as it is Eternity itself, contains within itself the three times of Eternity <note>Past, present, and future.</note>, as well as the plurality of persons within the unity of nature. This was the reason 
<margin>Exodus 3</margin>
why, when Moses asked Him what His name might be, God replied: 
<margin>Malachi 3</margin>
*I am who I was, who I am, and who I shall be.* <note>original: "Ego sum qui fui, qui sum, & qui ero." This is an expanded mystical interpretation of the Vulgate's "Ego sum qui sum."</note> For which reason He said elsewhere, *I am the Lord and I do not change.* From this, therefore, He is called <term>Ehieh <gloss>אהיה</gloss></term>: a name which, in the mystical fashion, encompasses within itself all the different tenses of the substantive verb "to be"—*I am, I was, I shall be*. In this way, it declares the everlastingness, stability, and permanence of God, and consequently proves the mystery of the Holy Trinity itself; which, in its Essential root, is nothing but one God, one supreme mind, 
<margin>Synesius</margin>
one principle, and one head. By these things, according to that sentiment of Synesius <note>Synesius of Cyrene (c. 373–414 AD), a Neoplatonist philosopher and bishop.</note>, it is clear *that this divine and unique nature is a principle born and arisen from itself and by itself alone.* We conclude, therefore, from what has been said, that *this Monad is the Principle without any other preceding beginning, the holy unity of unities, prior to unity itself,* 
<margin>Synesius</margin>
*the first monad of monads, the father of all, the simplicity of immense simplicity, which, sitting constantly as hidden glory above the peaks of the potential heavens,* brought forth the simplicities of the summits by a super-substantial birth, and joined them to itself by reflecting them back. For this very Unity, leaping forward through the primary form, diffused in an ineffable manner, has attained a triple power or property. This super-substantial source is therefore crowned by the beauty of a most bright and formal offspring, which flowed out from that very point (or unity, or center of darkness) and revolves around that point and center. One source, therefore, one root from which the illustrious son shines forth—the manifest birth from the secret inward parts—wisdom, the maker and reconciler of both worlds, the light of the Holy Spirit. A trinity in one, the root of darkness and the matrix of the waters, the root of light, the root of the intellectual world, the root of the sensible world, the root (insofar as Eternity is within it) of present, past, and future things which are in both worlds; the origin of divine numbers, the type of worldly things, and the perfection and existence of all. Indeed, it is truly all in all, just as every number is in reality nothing other than Unity, insofar as Unity is the beginning of any number, unity its middle, unity its end, and finally, unity its Whole.

But since all things consist of Unity, it follows that Unity is everything that is; for from it, through it, and in it are all things which are considered by number, weight, and measure. From the monad (I say) as the efficient cause through the power which is appropriated to the Father; through the monad as the exemplary and disposing cause through the Wisdom which is appropriated to the Son; and in the Monad itself as the final and preserving cause through the goodness which is appropriated to the Holy Spirit. And nonetheless, this is mediated by the single, unique monad alone (since it is indivisible and always remaining within itself)
