...external [property], which is a dense and smoky Spirit rising out of the darkness and resisting the action of divine heat; by constricting the heat's expanded power, it causes it—contrary to its essential and simple nature—to destroy and burn. <note>The author is describing how the "contractive" property of God, when it meets the "expansive" heat, creates a destructive or burning effect rather than a life-giving one.</note>

Therefore, it can by no means remain hidden from people endowed with a sound mind how both properties of God are radically involved in man and around man’s composition. Furthermore, this will seem not at all strange to those who consider man's free will in the choice of good or evil. For although Adam, before his fall, was "one," and focused only on the One <note>That is, Adam was in a state of pure unity with God.</note> (which "one" could neither be called "good" by him, insofar as he did not know evil—for "good" takes its name from its opposition to the evil contrary to it—nor "evil," since he was directed toward only one root, namely the luminous God and author of his life). Although (I say) before his fall he was one in his contemplation, yet after he had tasted of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, he perceived that he was composed of two opposite principles or contrary properties. Thus, while the eyes of his mind were closed, his bodily eyes were then opened in a moment. Having now recognized the two extremes and neglected heaven and his internal nature, he then began to look upon his external self. He knew himself to be naked, and above all, he attempted with great effort to cover and hide his private parts <note>original: "pudenda"</note>. And so, it was imposed upon him—by the divine will so ordering it—to know both earth and heaven, both body and soul, both darkness and light, both good and evil, both vice and virtue, and to distinguish between them.

From here, therefore, is the source and origin of **free will**; from here the rise and beginning of justice and iniquity; from here the confusion of life with death, of generation with corruption, and of health with sickness. For he who could not previously contemplate bodily and earthly things because of the elevated and illuminated clarity of his mind—not looking downward at all (for his earthly part was entirely subject to him because of the abundance of his luminous portion)—that man (I say), through the loss and lessening of his light within himself by his reckless fall, allowed bodily darkness to gradually creep in. This happened so that the darkness of the body might step by step prevail over the clarity of the mind and strive to defeat it by obscuring it. 

Therefore, it has come to pass that both the passions of darkness and those of light are recognized as having greater or lesser dominion in man at various times, according to the condition of the individual. From this, the rewards due to each of them are assigned by the Holy Scripture; for through it we are warned to abstain from the works of darkness if we wish to be considered and numbered among the chosen children of light. From here, therefore, comes **Christ’s Triumph** over sin, death, and Hell <note>original: "Gehennam"</note>; from here the Devil’s dominion and power in this world over the children of disobedience. From here (I say) the effects of each property of the eternal **Monad** <term>Monad</term><note>A term from Pythagorean and Platonic philosophy referring to the "One" or the first source of all things; here used for God.</note> are clearly depicted in human nature after the fall of the first Adam. 

But indeed, that "second Adam" <note>A common theological title for Jesus Christ.</note>, setting aside the chains and darkness of the first falling one, showed us the way by which—by closing our exterior or bodily eyes—we may open again the interior and mental ones. By this, we may gaze upon, adore, fear, and pursue with the highest reverence and love all the hidden Mysteries and Secrets of the Divinity—indeed, even God Himself as He is—and finally, that we ourselves, firmly clinging to Him, might become one with Him and at last be transformed into that same image.

Here, then, you have one argument for the operation of the two properties of God in a single subject [the human being]; by which he is sometimes submerged in darkness and sometimes, by a contrary reasoning, is illuminated by a new rebirth and finally emerges from the abyss of darkness.

It acts like a radical **Monad** <term>Monad: A term for a fundamental, indivisible Unity or "The One," often referring to God.</term> or a divine mind, the "principle of principles," at whose imperial command all the Microcosmic heavens and spheres are known to move in a circle. This is no different than how the "First Mover" <note>The 'Primum Mobile' in ancient astronomy, the outermost sphere that moves all others.</note> of the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm: The "Great World" or the universe at large.</term>—driven by eternal Wisdom, which is more mobile than any other thing and the source of all act and motion—rotates the lower heavens and spheres. This human or Microcosmic mind (which is a spark of divine wisdom within the Microcosm) is the "First Mover" in its human organ, and it has its chief seat in man's intellectual heaven [the brain].

From this, I say, both philosophers and physicians have concluded that voluntary motion comes from the brain or the "intellectual heaven." However, they have designated the movement of the "lower heavens" as involuntary—namely, the movement of the celestial, spiritual, or vital region (whose solar vessel or treasury is the **heart**), and the elemental, airy, or natural region (whose treasure chest is the **liver** <note>original: "Hepar"</note>). These move as if depending on the will of a single Monad. We shall now show how the two properties of God exercise themselves in the movement of this vital region.

First, it must be noted that life consists of "innate heat" and "radical moisture." <note>These were the two essential components of life in medieval and Renaissance medicine; heat provided the energy, while moisture provided the "fuel."</note> This heat comes from the luminous principle—the mind and the ray of Wisdom itself—while the moisture comes from the nature of the "created spirit" leaping out from the source of the moist nature (which is the image of darkness). From the mixing of these two—as **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of alchemy and Hermetic philosophy.</note> testifies—life or the vital soul was made, about which we will speak more extensively below. 

Therefore, just as it was said of the vast soul of the Macrocosm that it consists of watery matter (the offspring of darkness) and divine light, in exactly the same way and for the same reason, the matter stands in the constitution of the human soul. From this it follows that the soul contains within itself the effect of the property of God, both as the "hidden and contractive" Monad and as the "manifest and dilated" one. 

Through the **contractive nature**, the soul draws in light and spirit from the open air into the dark left sinus of the heart; it thickens and contracts it through "inspiration" (breathing in). Then, the smoke thus contracted—or the air thus thickened—is again breathed out in the form of dense smoke by the act of internal heat. This smoke, dispersing itself again into the expanded air, is rendered invisible through "rarefaction" <note>The process of becoming less dense.</note>. Physicians call this act of contraction and expansion **Systole** and **Diastole**; we have spoken of these at length in our booklet *On the Mystical Anatomy of the Heart*.

Therefore, just as we see in the Macrocosm that the "middle heaven" (which they call the **aether**) participates in both extremes—the upper or empyrean heaven and the lower or elemental/airy heaven—so indeed in the vital action, air is expelled and emitted by the light of the super-celestial region. Meanwhile, air is attracted and thickened by the dark and corporeal [nature] pertaining to the air and the earth (the body), and this is done solely for the necessity of life and living. 

But (as **Galen**, **Avicenna**, and other physicians testify), there are very many "passions" <note>In this context, "passions" means emotions or states of mind that "act upon" the person.</note> familiar to the Microcosmic heart which participate in these two extreme properties. For just as it is the nature of the hidden and dark property to contract and bind, to condense and submerge in darkness, so it happens that by the contraction of the heart alone, many various passions and afflictions—the "daughters of darkness"—arise. 

For these authors say that by the contraction of the heart alone, horrible effects come upon a person: namely, **sadness, fear, despair, melancholy, horror, distrust, anger, stupor, anxiety, and cares**, as well as infinite other effects (the daughters of darkness) which are most hostile to the human race. For the dark property, by constricting and contracting the organ of the heart, so blinds its spirits and overwhelms them with darkness that, as the super-celestial vision disappears, the false, chimerical <note>original: "Chimæreæ"; referring to the Chimera, a mythical beast, used here to mean "imaginary" or "illusory."</note> figments of the body and of dark spirits so disturb and delude judgment and reason that the person does not consider himself a creature awaiting salvation, but rather something already damned and rejected. 

Conversely, they conclude that good passions—the "daughters of light"—follow the expansion (dilatation) of the heart. For the human spirit, dilating itself by the opening of the heart, [beholds] with the vision of the mind...

### On the Supercelestial Origin of Life and Health

...is seized by the divine mind: from which it is affected by gladness and joy, nourished by love and hope; with fear and distrust driven out, a pious boldness and certain faith are fostered. It is guided by patience and temperance, filled with mercy and piety; it contemplates celestial things and despises terrestrial and worldly things. It is affected by many such good "passions" <note>In this period, "passions" refers to any emotional or physical state that acts upon the soul.</note>; all of which happen to it because of the **dilation of the heart** and the emission of the **Spirits of Life** <term>Spirits of Life: In vitalist medicine, these were subtle fluids or vapors that carried life-force from the heart to the rest of the body.</term> toward the "highest good," and the fixation of the "intellectual eyes" upon the mind itself. These, therefore, are the effects of the movements of the heart; which movement, in this respect, the Ancients distinguish into the "voluntary" or "Imperial," and the "involuntary" (or that which is effected by the Supreme Mover). They say the involuntary motion of the heart consists either in **dilation** alone—which they believe these passions follow: namely, joy, hope, confidence, love, mercy, humanity, etc.—or in **contraction** alone, the effects of which are: sadness, despair, fear, hatred, envy, anger, fury, shame, etc. Or, it consists of contraction and dilation together, as in that pulse which moves in **Systole** <term>Systole: The contraction of the heart.</term> and **Diastole** <term>Diastole: The expansion of the heart.</term>. This is attested by Galen in *On Affected Parts* and *On the Differences of Symptoms*; Avicenna in the first book of the *Canon*, doctrine 6; Galen in *On the Differences of Symptoms*, chapter 7; Avicenna on the heart; and Galen in *On the Pulse*, book 1, and *On the Differences of Pulses*; and Avicenna in the second book of the *Canon*, doctrine 3.

<margin>Job 12.</margin> Furthermore, Holy Scripture likewise explains the opposite operations of these properties in the same subject <gloss>the same person</gloss> in plain speech: *In the hand of Jehovah is the soul of every living thing and of all flesh: with God (he says) is wisdom and strength: his is counsel and understanding: he destroys, so that it cannot be built up; he shuts a man in, so that he cannot be opened. Behold, he withholds the waters so that they dry up, and he sends them out so that they overturn the earth. With him is strength and power; the one who errs and the one who leads into error are his; he makes counselors go distracted, and makes judges fools; he makes them wander like a drunkard and <margin>Job 5. Psalm 32. Deut. 32. Isaiah 8. Psalm 90:14. Psalm 8:4. Psalm 18:17. Psalm 106. Numbers 12. Deut. 28. Job 6:4. Job 33.</margin> grope in the dark without light; he wounds and he heals, he cures and makes whole; he kills and makes alive; he pursues with tribulation, darkness, dissolution, distress, and gloom; and again, he is present to men with kindness or pleasantness: he preserves them by the light of his face, and illuminates the lamp of life by putting darkness to flight; so that the creature may enjoy health, goodness, and happiness, he affects them with his visitation. Furthermore, in his negative property, Mary <note>Referencing Miriam, the sister of Moses.</note> contracted leprosy; he strikes with plague, burning fever, madness, and blindness; he causes the human spirit to drink the poison of his arrows; he rebukes through pains in the bed and makes all the bones waste away, so that bread is abominable to him in life, etc.* In these things, one may see God affecting man as much with blessings as with curses—partly in his **bright property** and partly in his **dark property**. This will be more clearly explained by us both in this Treatise on health, and in the following volume where, with God's help, we shall speak on the origin of diseases.

<margin>*Epilogue: or the conclusion of this book.*</margin> These things, therefore, which have been explained by us in this book, seem to agree exactly with the intentions and doctrine of the ancient and venerable Philosophers. For their enigmatic speech was of this sort: namely, that just as they fashioned **Demogorgon** <term>Demogorgon: A primordial, mysterious deity often associated with the very beginning of the universe and Chaos.</term> (the supreme God), Eternity, and **Chaos** to have been from eternity, so they announced that Eternity was in God, and Chaos itself was in eternity. Then they made God the midwife of a double birth of Chaos, the first of which was deformed strife or darkness, which (according to Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermetic philosophy.</note>) glided downward in a slanted revolution at the presence of the light, after its fight and resistance with the light, being unable to endure the strong virtue of the enduring God. For thus, with Michael fighting, the **Dragon** was cast down from heaven; and by this kind of struggle and division, the second birth was brought forth, which they called **universal moist nature**, and which they named the god **Pan** <note>original: "Deum Pana"; referring to the Greek god Pan, here used to represent the totality of the natural, material world.</note> by his action. The moist substance of this Pan filled the cavity of the world entirely; and thus we have a single third or middle thing produced between two extremes: which moist middle resurrected, as if from the sepulcher of death or the abyss of darkness, in a "first resurrection." The author of this resurrection from death to life was the **created light** itself, or Wisdom, which in turn has its origin from the Fountain of Life.

...origin, namely, from the **Word** <note>original: "Verbo"</note> or God revealed, which is recognized as differing in every way from strife, because the highest Light is charity and a self-arisen love: whereas **Strife** <note>original: "Litigium"</note> is malice and contention taking its origin from Chaos by the help of **Demogorgon** <term>Demogorgon: In Renaissance mythology, a primordial creator-god often associated with the dark, chaotic depths of the earth and the origin of the pagan gods.</term>; by whose luminous act it is also animated. This strife, therefore, is inclined toward evil with respect to the capacity of mortals, while the light is inclined toward good. Yet in truth, since nothing is evil in respect to the Creator, Demogorgon uses both this and that to fulfill his good will both in the heavens and on the earth. Demogorgon, therefore, was God, or the radical **Monad** <term>Monad: Derived from the Greek "monas" (unity), it refers to the single, indivisible source of all being in Neoplatonic and Pythagorean philosophy.</term> in and through itself, inasmuch as **Pythagoras** called it **Unity**, that is, the nature or mind of the One, and God and the Good itself. And **Socrates** with **Plato** recognized God as that which is One, which is alone, which is good, and which is of its own self a Mind, mixed with no matter and subject to no passion. Whence **Aristotle** makes him the supreme form.

This form, once hidden within itself, by emitting and revealing a part of itself, made the **Word**; by means of which all things were created. Through the emission of the **Word** or **Wisdom** <note>original: "Sapientiæ"</note>, Chaos, having been made pregnant, brings forth deformed and dark strife by means of its penetrative virtue. For darkness was upon the face of the abyss; a gross and dark Spirit, in receiving strife, repels the pursuing and informing rays of light with a perverse and hardened disposition. By resisting, the rays are reflected, and by this reflection **Lucifer** is procreated; who did not stand long in this state, but by strenuously attempting to attack, resist, and extinguish that luminous act of life, he was gradually driven down from heaven by the power of the God of light. Though he lost his acquired brightness, he was nonetheless endowed with a perverse life, implanted in his dark exterior—which is most hostile to the revealed God—from the sparks of the penetrating light. By this perverse life, he is always agile—acting against his dark or external disposition, which is sluggish and given to rest—through the malignant and envious nature of darkness to perpetrate his malice against the children of light. Thus, he is as ready to exercise the "privative" or withholding will of God as his bright wisdom is prepared for His "positive" will, and most practiced in attributing all good things to the children of light.

Hence, therefore, in the world there are *life and death, generation and corruption, health and disease, good and evil, sympathy and antipathy, concord and discord, love and hate, peace and war, joy and sadness, temperance and rashness, confidence and despair, virtue and vice, will and refusal, mercy and cruelty, truth and falsehood, Christ and the Devil*; and finally, **Light and Darkness**. And this was the reason why a certain Philosopher <note>Likely referring to Empedocles, who taught that Love and Strife were the two forces governing the universe.</note> said that "All things were composed of strife and friendship"; namely, from dark matter and light, or divine love. For even though the fertile offspring of Chaos—namely, **Pan** <term>Pan: In this context, Pan represents "Universal Nature" or the "All," the soul that permeates the material world.</term> or the universal moist nature—is rectified by the virtue of light and cleansed from darkness, and is informed and animated by the life-giving light through the union made by the Holy Spirit, yet because he was born of a leprous mother and infected by gloom or strife before any age began, he truly received his origin from death and deformity themselves, no differently than a form receives its origin from life and truth. Thus, he is more inclined toward deformed works in and of himself than toward those of the light. Therefore, the reason for the words brought forth by Christ is manifest: namely, that "wide is the path leading to destruction, but narrow and straight is the way which leads to salvation." And yet the Author of both this and that is God, who is the radical **Monad** of these two opposites, from whose root the **Dyad** <term>Dyad: The principle of "twoness" or duality; the first step away from Unity toward the multiplicity of the created world.</term> arises. Whence it is said, that He Himself has in Himself the power of life and death, and that He leads to the gates of the grave and brings back again, inasmuch as He hides Himself from the creature in His secret property, and then leaves it in the power of the Spirits of darkness and death. But when He emits the light of His face again, the creature is usually restored and liberated from those wicked and impure spirits, and refreshed by good and luminous spirits. Finally, where Pythagoras attributed Unity to God and Duality to the Daemon <note>In ancient philosophy, a "daemon" was a spirit or power, not necessarily the modern "demon."</note>, whom he calls the author of evils: there, by "God," he understands the bright **Wisdom**...

# On the super-celestial origin of Life & Health.

...the **bright** <note>original: "lucidam"</note> author of life, emitted from the radical **monad** <term>Monad: A term for the number one, representing the indivisible source or God in Pythagorean thought.</term>: through the Demon <note>The author likely refers to the "Demogorgon" mentioned on the previous page as the mediator of material darkness.</note>, [comes] darkness itself and worldly matter, which the corporeal mass surrounds, and which he himself calls the World. From this, all the followers of **Pythagoras** incline toward this opinion: that **Unity** is attributed to **Apollo** <note>In this context, Apollo represents the Sun and the divine light of the One.</note>; where, by Apollo, they mean the divine light. They attribute the **Dyad** <term>Dyad: The number two, representing duality, division, and the initial resistance of matter to the divine will.</term> to strife, or audacity, or matter: but the **Triad** <term>Triad: The number three, symbolizing harmony and the resolution of conflict through divine form.</term> to Justice and form, which is the highest perfection. By these things they seem to hint that the Dyad, or contentious matter—which is in itself bold, just like its brother **Strife** <note>original: "Litigium"</note>—is bound by the bond of Justice in a concord of peace and is raised up toward lucid laws. Thus, it is rendered a son of light and not of darkness by this adaptation; and unless it remains rebellious against the Light, it will prepare for itself a crown in the Kingdom of light. Such will be the second life, which no Death shall follow: such will be the renewal of the Heavens and the earth, when all things will be made new; such will be the resurrection of the body and soul, which the Holy Scriptures so faithfully promise.

We conclude, therefore, that the absence of Light is gloom and darkness; and where light is absent, there also motion is lacking, which is the immediate effect of light (which is the **first act** <term>First Act: A philosophical term (Actus Primus) referring to the initial power or presence that brings a thing into being or motion.</term>): and where motion is lacking, there heat is lacking, seeing as heat is the immediate effect of motion. From this it follows that where gloom is present, there stillness is present, which is the absence of motion; and where stillness is present, there also coldness is present, which does not move unless it is urged by motion, and even then it is said to react through resistance. Finally, this whole system depends upon the **One**, and thus from the One all things were made through **thickening** and **thinning** <note>original: "inspissationem & rarefactionem"; these are the physical processes of "densifying" light into matter or "thinning" matter back into spirit.</note>.

->thus the Heavens extended,<-
->thus the Earth created.<-

# BOOK TWO

## ON THE METAPHYSICAL PRINCIPLE OF LIFE AND HEALTH.

### CHAPTER I.

->*What the Soul of the World is. That it is the source of life for all creatures.*<-

<image-desc>An ornamental woodcut initial 'M' decorated with intricate vine and leaf motifs.</image-desc> Therefore, the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "Mundi Anima"; the vitalizing spirit that permeates all nature.</note> is nothing other than the union of immortal light—emitted from the ray of Eternity—with the most subtle and worthy portion of the humid nature, or the waters, leaping forth from the womb of dark **Chaos**. From this union, according to the pattern of the **Archetype** <term>Archetype: The original "blueprint" or "Intelligible World" in the mind of God before physical creation.</term> (or the Intelligible World), a Trinity was born and produced from Unity (or a "Triune"). For as was declared in the preceding pages, and according to the teaching of the Prophet **Isaiah** <note>Referencing Isaiah 43:7: "Everyone that is called by my name: I have created him for my glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him."</note>, three things are required for the perfection of any individual, whether spiritual or corporeal: namely, **creation**, **formation**, and **making**. "Whatever," says Jehovah through the Prophet, "I have called by my name, I have created, formed, and made."

**Creation**, therefore, is the disposition of matter or of any individual thing, from which the power of the **form** <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "form" is the essence or "actuality" of a thing, while "matter" is its potential.</note> is later drawn out. Thus matter, although it was deformed by darkness, was nevertheless already prepared by the counsel of the **radical monad** <term>Radical Monad: The "Root One" or the indivisible unity of God as the starting point of all existence.</term> and disposed to receive the "act." Then the lucid form flashed forth; it was roused as if out of nothing, yet it was drawn out of the potential of the dark matter by the divine command and will of the Monad. 

The appearance of this lucid principle is called **formation**, because it causes that which previously enjoyed no shape—and was consequently considered as nothing—to appear in some form or species. Finally, the property of **making** <note>original: "faciendi"</note> pertains to the mutual conjunction or union of the flashing form and the humid matter revealed from the womb of Chaos.

And so, the omnipotence or **unity** of God first compels the waters and all other individual things into their own matter (the unity of the individual). This, in respect to divine goodness, is the office or action of the **Father**, as it is more eminent in Him than in the **Son** (or **Wisdom**); for potential matter and the darkness itself existed before the emanation of light. For this reason, these are most rightly referred to the radical and paternal Monad. 

The **Wisdom of God**, or the lucid emanation of the hidden unity (which we call the **Son**, insofar as He arises from the radical Monad as if from a Father), establishes the disposition of the Form. Therefore, we say that "formation" belongs to Wisdom itself, or the **Word**. 

Finally, the highest fiery love of immortality—proceeding from the paternal Monad as "power" and from the filial Word as "act"—is that which, by an ineffable harmony, compels the bond between the matter (now revealed by the presence of light) and the flashing lucid form itself, [drawing them] from the center of darkness into the composition of a single thing.

And indeed, in this triple proportion, all things in the world were made step by step and successively. For just as this Holy Spirit proceeds from eternity, coupling form with matter from the Father (or Power) and the Son (or Wisdom), so

...also one Spirit joins the union of matter, which is from the Father, with the expansion of form, which is from the Son. From these things it must be gathered that the **being** of a worldly thing without its **existence** <note>In scholastic philosophy, "being" (esse) is the potential to exist, while "existence" (existentia) is the actual manifestation in the world.</note> is like potential matter and the origin of those things around which creation revolves. Its **Essence**, however, is like a bright form drawn out from the power of dark matter. God alone is the root or **radical Monad** <term>Monad: Derived from the Greek *monas* (unity); in this context, it refers to the indivisible, singular source of all things—God.</term>, in which being and essence are the same: namely, potential matter and actual Light. Therefore, it is specifically the third person <note>The Holy Spirit.</note> who joins matter with form and is the one who performs the work.

From these principles, the composition of the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "animæ mundanæ"</note> clearly reveals itself, as does the **Worldly Instrument** in which it acts as if in its own proper body. For just as we see that heaven itself (as a universal spiritual creature) was created, formed, and made before the Earth (as a corporeal creature), so it is necessary that the soul precedes the body in both order and time. Furthermore, just as the Soul of the world's Soul is that unique divine **Wisdom** <note>original: "sapientia"; often identified with the Logos or the "Son" in Fludd's system.</note> itself, so the soul of any individual body is a unique spark of that universal World Soul. For we define the Soul of the World as the purer spirit of universal nature, formed and quickened immediately from the eternal Monad by the emanations of divine light, and brought into a living and spiritual nature by the union or "glue" of holy love with those emanations. 

Therefore, it is evident that the **Agent** in the soul is the divine and uncreated light—which is the wisdom of God, and indeed God himself. The **Patient** <term>Patient: The passive recipient of an action; in this case, the spirit that receives the "act" of divine light.</term> is the most subtle and created spirit of the world, filled and, as it were, intoxicated in every way by the eternal rays of Wisdom. Hence it is said that God—or the Light and the Word in which there was life—gives life, breath, and all things to everyone. For from the Father's part, we have prepared matter, or a spirit worthy of such a glorious form; and from the part of the Son, or Wisdom, the form suitable for such matter is given; and by the bond of the Holy Spirit, a union is made into an **Angelic nature**, by which the universal spirit of the world is animated and leads its life. It is clear, then, that Life and Soul are entirely from God, in God, and are as if God himself, inasmuch as He is the life and the "length of days" <margin>Deuteronomy 30; Psalm 27:1.</margin> of all creatures, and especially of Man. And since He is pure light, He informs the spirit and creates a union through a threefold property between those two. Therefore, David calls **Jehovah** his "salvation" and the "strength of his life" (or soul). This is what Saint John calls the **Light**, which he said dwells in the **Word** as if in its primary fountain. Wherefore not only men, but the entire Spirit of the World is said to "live, move, and have its being" <margin>Acts 17; 1 Timothy 6; Ephesians 3:9; John 14:6; Pimander 1.</margin> in Him; for it is His work to give life to all things. Whence **Christ**, or the Word through which God created the world, confessed that he was "the life and the truth." Similarly, **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary sage to whom the *Hermetica* are attributed.</note> says that the union of the Mind of the Father and the Word of the Son (whom he says are not at all distant from one another) is life itself. It is as if he had said: the purest portion of potential matter related to the Father, joined with the measure of clearest light by the union of divine harmony and love, constitutes the soul’s life.

But since I have already written a copious and complete discourse on the confirmation of the universal Soul of the World in our response to the quibbles of **Frater Marin Mersenne** <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648) was a French priest and philosopher who famously accused Fludd of being a magician and heretic. Fludd spent years in a printed "war of words" with him.</note>—who, in an impious and insane manner, attempted to completely remove and deny it—I have not proposed to debate further about it in this place, so that we may hasten more quickly to our current subject of human life and health.

...and immediately fashioned according to His own model. For just as the World was created, formed, and made immediately by God out of the Chaos shimmering in darkness—that is, reigning in the **archetype** <term>Archetype: The original, divine blueprint or ideal pattern of the universe existing in the mind of God.</term>—through the loving union of potential Matter (referred to the Father) and actual Light or form (applied to Wisdom): so in like manner, man was fused together immediately by that same divine **Wisdom**, which fills and gives life to the **Typic World** <note>original: "Mundum Typicum"; the world of forms or types that serves as the model for the physical world.</note> on all sides, and from the moist matter of the world arising fundamentally from Chaos and distinguished into Heaven and Earth by the power of the said divine Wisdom. Therefore, man received his soul, or life and spirit, immediately from God reigning in the typic World; He composed man's internal "Heaven" from a portion of the worldly heaven (which **Synesius** <note>Synesius of Cyrene (c. 373–414 AD), a Neoplatonist philosopher and bishop who wrote on the nature of the soul.</note> calls "a portion of himself") just as He composed his "Earth," or his body and external part, from the heavy substance of the worldly earth.

<margin>Genesis 1. Augustine on Genesis. 2 Peter 3. 1 Timothy 6. Isaiah 42. Wisdom 1. Judith 9. Acts 14. Judith 13. Acts 17. Job 32. Acts 17.</margin>
There was, therefore, a hidden God who, by revealing Himself from the darkness or His own "hidden place," sent forth the **breath of His life** <note>original: "vitæ suæ spiraculum"</note> for the existence of the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm: The "Great World" or the universe as a whole.</term>; hence it is said that the Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters, imparting to them a fiery vigor. From these waters, both the first Heaven and the Earth were then created, with that bright spirit assisting; and then all their powers. For by the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the spirit from His mouth, all their powers: namely, that spirit by which God gave life to all things. This divine spirit was also manifest, ruling a little later in the World, and after its emanation into the world, it fashioned the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: The "Little World," referring to a human being as a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</term> according to the image of the Macrocosm. For God Himself said these things: *I have created the heavens, I have stretched them out, I have established the earth and those things which sprout from it, I have given breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those who walk upon it:* and consequently, it is certain that He Himself gives life to all things by means of His one and only Wisdom. With this Wisdom, He first filled, animated, and gave life to the whole World; from its soul depends the life of all individual things that are in the world. Whence, just as the Sacred Pages acknowledge Him to be *the God of the Heavens, the earth, the sea, the waters, and the creator of all things that are in them, and the Lord of every creature:* so indeed they assert that He spoke, and immediately the creature was made; He sent His spirit, and suddenly all things were created. For by means of that living spirit, He Himself gives life and inspiration and all things to everyone.

But truly, among all other lower creatures fused from the members of the World, Man seems to claim the primary place for himself, because the Creator inspired him with the breath of His Divinity in such a way that He made him only a little lower than the Angels. For just as we read in angelic creatures that one is preferred over another in their internal nature and in the sight of the Creator—so that some of them are closer to God and His light... just as in the celestial bodies, we notice that star is preferred to star, and planet to planet... by the dignity of their light. So indeed man on earth stands in relation to the other creatures of the land, sea, and air, as the Sun itself in the Heavens relates to the other stars; he excels all of them in the dignity of his light, and for that reason, he has dominion over them all. For besides the fact that the strong spirit of God made man, and the breath of the Almighty gave him life as it did all other creatures, yet He gave a still greater gift to man by which he might exceed the others in dignity and illumination: namely, **Intelligence** <note>original: "Intelligentia"; here referring to the highest faculty of the human soul, capable of perceiving divine truths.</note>. *In man (says Job) is the spirit by which he lives, but the inspiration of the Almighty gives him understanding,* from which it is clear that his internal part excels that of other creatures. Although they are imbued with the breath of life just like man—which proceeds from God, whose role it is to give life and inspiration to all things—He nonetheless affected and enriched Man with a greater portion of the light of His Wisdom, and for that reason, He exalted him with a more eminent dignity over the other creatures of the earth.

But setting those things aside, since we have argued more extensively elsewhere concerning the intellectual portion of the internal man, we shall now descend to the arrangement of the "mere life" by which not only he, but also all other creatures live.

### ->On the Super-celestial Origin of Life and Health.<-

We say, therefore, that the life by which every creature exists and lives—forged from the members or elements of the world—is of the same essence as the universal Soul of the World. This is no different than how all drops of water share the same nature with the entire mass of water, or how we observe that all solar rays do not differ in nature and essence from the sun itself. Indeed, we have perhaps thoughtlessly introduced the whole waters and their smallest parts, as well as solar light and its rays, as our examples here, for life itself is forged from a subtle portion of those things and a portion of divine light united together.

The more the proportion of divine light excels in this "subtle spirit," the more noble a thing in dignity it produces. For example: from the Empyrean spirit <note>The highest, most "fiery" or spiritual level of heaven.</note> intoxicated by the power of light, the Angelic and intellectual life is made, in which man participates. From the ethereal spirit—as it is not quite so enriched with light—the fleeting and common life of creatures is composed. As this spirit is equal to light and divine fire in an unequal proportion, their union becomes the life of elementary creatures <note>Creatures composed of the four physical elements: earth, water, air, fire.</note>. For just as the Empyrean spirit, because of its dignity and exaltation, is the soul of the ethereal realm, so indeed that ethereal spirit is the soul of the elementary realm. God, therefore, is the *Author of all*, in whom material spirit and formal light—and consequently, life—exist. The Apostle seems to confirm this in the following sequence of words:

<margin>John 1. 2 Corinthians 8.</margin>
*"There is one God the Father," (he says) "from whom are all things, and we in Him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him,"* etc. In this speech, by "the Father" he seems to indicate matter (both spiritual and corporal), which is assigned—according to the reasoning previously cited—as the subject *from which* all things come. By "the Son" or Jesus Christ, he intends the Light or Wisdom of the world; the form *through which* the said matter is shaped and quickened. Finally, St. John and Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetica, a body of mystical and philosophical texts, are attributed.</note> called the union of these two, mediated by the Holy Spirit, "Life."

<margin>Pimander 1.</margin>
The passive portion of this is the *Spirit*; the active portion is *Light*. The connection of these two is called the *Soul*. From this kind of action and passion arise **Systole** <note>The contraction of the heart and arteries to push blood through the body.</note> and **Diastole** <note>The expansion of the heart and arteries as they fill with blood.</note> in the pulse. And this is the reason why the Soul is sometimes called "Spirit" and the "breath of life" in the Holy Bible, and sometimes "Light" and "Lamp"—taking its name sometimes from the formal light, and sometimes from the material spirit. This is no different than how we observe the Angelic composition itself being called sometimes an *Angel* (in respect to its matter) and sometimes *Jehovah* and *Wisdom* in the same chapter of the holy scripture, as is often found in the Book of Exodus.

Here, then, you have the beginning of the <term>radical moisture</term> <note>The essential, life-sustaining fluid believed by medieval and Renaissance physicians to be the fuel for the body's life-force.</note>; here is the principle of the <term>innate heat</term> <note>The natural, vital warmth of a living being, which "cooks" the radical moisture to produce life.</note>. By the union of these two, the life of a creature is made, and by their power, it exists. Thus indeed we observe the order of the Holy Trinity through the entire course of nature. For from the **Monad** <note>The number one; used here to represent the indivisible Unity of God from which all multiplicity flows.</note> first flowed Light from one side; and from the other, a dark condition was revealed by the appearance of that light. Here, then, is the Trinity of the **Archetype** <note>The original, divine blueprint or ideal pattern of the universe.</note> in unity on one side; then potential matter and actual Light concur for the consistency of the world on the other: and there, according to the pattern of the Archetype, the **Typic World** <note>original: "Mundus typicus"; the conceptual or ideal model of the universe that bridges the divine mind and the physical world.</note> is procreated. Then afterwards, the subtle part of the moist matter and the essence of the light-filled form are gathered by a subordinate bond into the one Soul of the World. Again, this Soul distinguishes itself into three regions according to the dignity of their location: the Empyrean or intellectual portion of the worldly soul was produced; the ethereal or life-giving portion; and the elementary and aerial, or natural and vegetative portion. Again, this tripartite soul expands itself into the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms. And thus we see all things formed in the image of the Trinity by this life-giving power, distinguished into three different parts.

You see here, therefore, what is first the Soul and Life of the World, and then the soul of every creature in the world. It is clearly to be drawn from the above that it takes its origin from God "revealed"—that is, in His positive property. Now, however, it remains to show how, through His opposite or privative property—namely, not by giving and emitting through benevolent expansion, but by receiving and contracting into Himself not only from the world, but from any particular...

Indeed, the Holy Scripture seems to declare this clearly in various places and in express words: for first, the **Royal Psalmist** <note>King David</note> speaks thus: <margin>Psalm 104:29.</margin> *Every creature looks to God, that he may give them their food in its season, etc.* By which he denotes that the preservation of life is performed by God. These two parts of David’s discourse, therefore, regard the preservation of creatures in this life. And it is from this that the sick are tormented more in the night-time than in the day. Which <margin>Job 30:17.</margin> Job also confirms thus: *In the night my bone is pierced with pains, and my nerves do not rest, my pulses are not quiet, etc.*

Furthermore, we receive elsewhere from the holy page that <margin>Isaiah 8.</margin> *tribulation and darkness, dissolution and anguish and gloom pursue the wicked,* by the turning away of the Creator’s face from the creature. Finally, the last clause of the Royal discourse is this: *When he sends forth his spirit, they are recreated, etc.* that is, they are affected with both life and health by the kind manifestation of the face of **Jehovah** <note>The Hebrew name for God, often used in these texts to emphasize the Creator as the source of all being.</note>. Nor indeed do we have this verified only by the Royal Psalmist, since Job seems to agree with this opinion in every way, being one who fell into a similar discourse. God (he says) <margin>Job 34:13.</margin> *placed man upon the earth, applying his soul to him. If he should take back or draw his spirit or breath to himself, all flesh would fail and expire, and man would be turned into his own ash, etc.* By which he not only brilliantly confirmed those things uttered by David, but also seems to hint to us that the soul and spirit and all flesh are in the hands of the Almighty, whose role it is not only to give life, inspiration, and being to all things through his benevolent, life-giving, and open property, but also to trouble the creature by drawing it back little by little and by degrees through the contrary property, making it grow sick; or, persisting entirely in his wrath, to cause life to expire totally by taking away the spirit; or, by sending it back and being appeased, likewise to send out the rays of his benevolent countenance and bless it with its former health.

# CHAPTER III.
## On the mystery of health, and how it extends itself both to the soul and to the body.

Just as according to the rule of the **Pythagoreans** <note>Followers of the ancient Greek philosopher Pythagoras, who believed numbers were the fundamental reality of the universe.</note> the **Triad** <note>original: "Trias" — the number three.</note> denotes perfection—since it signifies the giving of form, in which justice is said to provide its work in the bond and union of potential matter (referred to the Father) with the formal light (which pertains to the Son), and from which union the life of the world consists—so indeed does the safety and health of the world, and of every creature in the world, consist in the sincere observation of this kind of justice. For the creature draws its life in and through the **Soul of the World** <term>mundi anima: a vital spirit believed by many ancient and Renaissance philosophers to permeate all nature</term>. For just as the external part of a creature—its "Earth"—is tempered to justice and weight by the union of the very coarse portions of the worldly elements, so indeed its internal part is constituted from their subtle number, weight, and measure. Therefore, as both the elements and the things composed of them are governed, ordered, and arise from the single **Soul of the World**, which is a **Trinity in Unity** (as has been declared), so it is also necessary that they be held together in harmonious peace by its bond and ligament. 

For as duality is animated by unity—or matter by form—so indeed the number four is vivified by the number three. Thus the numbers four and eight are preserved (eight resulting in a cubic fashion from the square of four); that is, the creature composed of elements is preserved by the four elements. These elements, with respect to their origin, are in truth nothing other than the coarse and external form of visible things—a kind of outer soul—whose internal essence is the subtle portion of the Soul of the World. From this it is certain that, just as the Soul of the World is nothing other than the consensus of Unity in Trinity, so the elements which the world establishes as four in number are in reality and effect only three. This is in imitation of the composition of the world and its soul, which consists of three parts: namely, from darkness (or dark matter), formal light, and an intermediate matter. To speak in the Pythagorean manner, these are **Eternity** (or the **Luminous Word**), **Dark Strife**, and **Bread** (or the intermediate matter). 

Thus indeed we have the **Earth**, which is a mass of darkness, the **dead head** <note>original: "caput mortuum" — an alchemical term referring to the useless residue left after a chemical reaction, here meaning the densest part of matter.</note> of the whole mass, and the seat of the principal dark strife. **Fire** is the image of divine light. There is also the sphere of **humidity**, whose coarser part (water) participates in the earth, and whose more subtle part participates in fire. This is after the image of the moist worldly matter, which came forth and arose from the mutual action occurring between the **Darkness** (whose quality is coldness and whose nature is to react through resistance) and the **Light** (which is the primary actor and whose effect is heat).

From these elements, therefore, the body of mortals is fashioned, just as the soul and life are fashioned from the celestial elements. If, therefore, any of these elements should step outside the laws of the fiery bond of love or of divine justice, the temperament of life is corrupted, and the empire of health is violated. For then an **internal war** <note>original: "bellū intestinū"</note> is arisen among the elements that establish the composition of either the body, or the soul, or the life of both. For the elements are in every way opposed to one another by reason of their origin: namely, fire is opposed to the water of the humid sphere (inasmuch as water is the "wife" of earth and darkness, and shares in the coldness of the earth); and Earth is opposed to the **Air** (inasmuch as air is the "wife" of Fire or Light, and shares in fiery heat). If the bond of concord that ties them in peace is violated and loosened, it is necessary that they affect the whole machine with discord and strife. Thus, all justice is excluded from that "economy" <note>Here meaning the organized system of the body.</note>, and consequently, well-being and health lose their privilege when their empire is reduced to nothing. Therefore, the bond of peace is sought, by which every element may again be weighed in the scales of justice by a peaceful proportion of things, and—with the bond of the most ancient love leading the way—each of them may be restrained by stronger bridles in their proper places established for the composition.

## CHAPTER III.
->On the mystery of health, and how it extends to both the soul and the body.<-

Just as according to the rule of the Pythagoreans the Triad denotes perfection—since it signifies the giving of form, in which justice provides its labor in the bond and union of potential matter (referred to the Father) with formal light (which belongs to the Son)—from which and in which union the life of the world consists: So indeed, health and soundness consist in the sincere observation of this kind of justice, both for the world and for every creature in it that draws its life in and through the **Soul of the World**. For just as the external part of a creature—its "Earth"—is tempered to justice and weight through the union of the dense portions of the worldly elements, so indeed its internal part is constituted from their subtle parts, by number, weight, and measure. Therefore, just as the elements and things <term>made of elements <note>original: "elementata" — physical objects or bodies composed of the four basic elements.</note></term> are governed, ordered, and arise from the unique *Soul of the World, which is the Trinity in Unity (as has been declared)*, so also it is necessary that they be held together in harmonious peace by its bond and ligament.

For just as duality is animated by unity, or matter by form, so indeed the number four is quickened and preserved by the number three. This results in the <term>quaternary <note>The number four, associated here with the physical elements.</note></term> and <term>octonary <note>The number eight; here referring to the cubic stability of matter, where 2 cubed is 8.</note></term> numbers, which result in a cubic manner from the square of four—that is, the material thing is formed from the four elements. These elements, with respect to their origin, are truly nothing other than the dense and external form of visible things, acting as a kind of soul whose internal essence is the subtle Soul of the World. Whereby it is certain that just as the Soul of the World is nothing other than the consensus of unity in the trinity, so the elements, which the world counts as four, are in truth and effect only three. This is in imitation of the composition of the world and its soul, which consists of three parts: namely, from darkness (or dark matter), formal light, and intermediate matter. That is, to speak in the Pythagorean manner, from *eternity* (or the *shining Word*), *dark strife*, and *Pan* <note>In this context, Pan refers to the "All" or the universal intermediate matter that connects the extremes.</note> (or intermediate matter). Thus we have the Earth, which is a mass of darkness, the <term>dead head <note>original: "caput mortuum" — an alchemical term for the inert, lifeless residue remaining after a chemical process.</note></term> of the whole mass, and the seat of the primary dark strife. Fire is the image of divine light, and the sphere of humidity (whose denser part, namely water, belongs to the earth, while its more subtle part belongs to fire) participates in the image of the worldly moist matter. This humidity emerged and arose from the mutual action between darkness (whose quality is coldness and whose nature is to react through resistance) and light, which is the primary actor and whose effect is heat.

From these things, therefore, the body of mortals is forged, just as the soul and life are forged from the celestial elements. If, therefore, any of these elements should stray outside the bonds of harmony of fiery love or the laws of divine justice, the <term>temperament <note>original: "temperies" — the specific balance of the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that maintains health.</note></term> of life is corrupted and the domain of health is violated; for then an internal war has arisen among the constituent parts. For just as the elements are in every way opposed to each other by reason of their origin—namely, Fire to that portion of the aqueous sphere of humidity which serves as a "wife" to Earth and darkness and shares in Earth’s coldness; and Earth to Air, which serves as a "wife" to Fire or Light and shares in the fiery heat—if the bond of concord tying them in peace be violated and loosened, it will be necessary that they affect the whole <term>machine <note>original: "machinam" — the physical body or the universe seen as a complex structure.</note></term> with discord and strife. Thus, all justice is excluded from that <term>economy <note>original: "Oeconomia" — the ordered management and balance of the body's systems.</note></term>, and consequently well-being and health will lose their privilege, as their empire is reduced to nothing. Therefore, a bond of peace is sought, by which every element may once again be weighed in the scales of justice with a peaceful proportion of things, and held in its proper place for the composition of the whole by stronger reins, guided by the bond and tie of the most ancient love.

## CHAPTER III.
### On the mystery of health: how it extends both to the soul and to the body.

Just as according to the Pythagorean standard the **Triad** <note>The number three, which Renaissance philosophers viewed as a symbol of perfection and the divine.</note> signifies perfection—inasmuch as it signifies the "informing" or shaping of matter—so too is justice found in the connection and union of **potential matter** (attributed to the Father) with **formal light** (which pertains to the Son). This union works to provide the life of the world, and it is within this union that life consists. Thus, from the sincere observation of this kind of "justice" or balance, the well-being and health of the world consists, as does that of every creature in the world who draws its life in and through the **Soul of the World** <note>original: *anima mundi* — the vital force that philosophers believed permeated all nature.</note>. 

For just as the external part of a creature (its "Earth") is tempered toward justice and weight through the union of the very coarse portions of the worldly elements, so too is its internal part constituted from their subtle **number, weight, and measure**. Since both the elements and the things made from them are governed, ordered, and born from the single **Soul of the World**—which is the **Trinity in Unity**, as has been declared—it is likewise necessary that they be held together in concordant peace by its bond and ligament. 

For just as duality is animated by unity (or matter by form), so the number four is vivified by the number three; thus the numbers four and eight are preserved (eight resulting in a cubic fashion from the square of four). This represents the "elemented" creature made from the four elements, which, in respect to their origin, are truly nothing other than the coarse and external form of visible things—a kind of soul whose internal essence is the subtle World Soul. From this it is certain that, just as the World Soul is nothing other than the consensus of **Unity in Trinity**, so the four elements which the world establishes are in truth and effect only three, in imitation of the composition of the world and its soul. This composition consists of three things: namely, darkness (or dark matter), formal light, and intermediate matter. To speak in the **Pythagorean** fashion, these are **Eternity** (or the **Radiant Word**), **Dark Strife**, and **Bread** (the intermediate matter). 

Thus we have the **Earth**, which is a mass of darkness, the **dead head** <note>original: *caput mortuum* — an alchemical term for the inert, worthless residue left after a chemical reaction; here used to describe the most solid, lifeless part of matter.</note> of the entire mass, and the seat of the principal "dark strife." **Fire** is the image of divine light. The sphere of **humidity** (moisture) has a coarser part, **Water**, which partakes of the earth, and a subtler part, **Air**, which partakes of fire. This mirrors the moist matter of the world which emerged from the mutual action between **Darkness** (whose quality is coldness and whose nature is to react through resistance) and **Light** (which is the primary actor and whose effect is heat).

From these elements, therefore, the body of mortals is forged, just as the soul and life are forged from the celestial elements. If, then, any of these elements should step outside the bonds of the harmony of fiery love or the laws of divine justice, the temperament of life is corrupted and the empire of health is violated. For then an internal war has arisen among the elements that establish the composition of the body, the soul, or the life of both. 

By the very nature of their origin, the elements are opposites: Fire is opposed to the Water portion of the moist sphere (which acts as a "wife" to the earth and darkness and shares in the earth's coldness), and Earth is opposed to the Air (the "wife" of Fire or Light, which shares in fiery heat). If the bond of concord tying them together in peace is violated and loosened, they will necessarily affect the entire machine with discord and strife. All justice will be excluded from that **Economy** <note>original: *Oeconomia* — the organized system or "household management" of the body's health.</note>, and consequently, health and wellness will lose their privilege as their empire is reduced to nothing. Therefore, the bond of peace must be sought, so that every element may again be weighed in the scales of justice by a peaceful proportion of things, and so that each may be held in its proper place within the composition by stronger reins, guided by the bond and tie of the most ancient Love.

These two small parts of David's discourse, therefore, regard the preservation of creatures in this life. # On the Supercelestial Origin of Life and Health.

### CHAPTER III.

### On the mystery of health, and how it extends to both the soul and the body.

Just as, according to the Pythagorean rule, the **Triad** <note>original: *Trias* — the number three, which many ancient philosophers saw as the first "perfect" number representing beginning, middle, and end</note> signifies perfection—since it represents the imposition of form—in which **Justice** <note>original: *iustitia* — here used in the sense of "right proportion" or "harmonic balance"</note> is seen to offer its work in the binding and union of **potential matter** (associated with the Father) with the **formal light** (which pertains to the Son), and in which union the life of the world consists: so indeed, from the sincere observation of this kind of justice, the well-being and health of both the world and every creature within it depends—drawing its life in and through the **Soul of the World** <note>original: *anima mundi* — the divine spirit that animates all of nature</note>. For as the external part of a creature (its "Earth") is tempered toward justice and weight through the union of the coarse portions of the worldly elements, so its internal part is constituted from their subtle aspects, by number, weight, and measure. Therefore, just as both the elements and the things made from them are governed, ordered, and arise from a single **Soul of the World**, which is **Trinity in Unity** (as has been declared), so it is necessary that they be held in harmonious peace by its bond and fastening. For as **Duality** is animated by **Unity** (or matter by form), so the number **Four** is given life by the number **Three**, and the numbers four and eight are preserved (the latter resulting cubically from the square of four). That is to say, the thing composed of elements is preserved by the four elements, which, regarding their origin, are truly nothing other than the coarse and external form of visible things, acting as their soul—while their internal part is the subtle Soul of the World. From this, it is certain that as the Soul of the World is nothing but the consensus of Unity in Trinity, so the four elements established by the world are, in truth and effect, only three—imitating the composition of the world and its soul, which consists of three parts: namely, from darkness or dark matter, formal light, and intermediate matter. To speak in the Pythagorean manner, these are **Eternity** (or the **Bright Word**), **Dark Contention**, and **Bread** <note>original: *Pane* — likely a reference to Pan, the god of nature, or a play on the word for bread as sustenance</note> (or intermediate matter). Thus we have Earth, which is a mass of darkness, the **dead head** <term>caput mortuum: a term used in alchemy and chemistry to describe the useless residue or dregs left over after a process</term> of the whole mass and the seat of the chief dark contention. **Fire** is the image of divine light, and the spheres of moisture (of which the coarser part is **Water** from the earth, and the subtler part participates in **Fire**) are formed in the image of the worldly moist matter, which emerged and arose from the mutual action between **Darkness** (whose quality is coldness and whose nature is to react through resistance) and **Light** (the primary actor, whose effect is heat).

From these, therefore, the body of mortals is fashioned, just as the soul and life are fashioned from celestial elements. If, then, any of these elements steps outside the bonds of the harmony of fiery love or the laws of divine justice, the temperament of life is corrupted and the dominion of health is violated. For then an **internal war** <note>original: *bellum intestinum*</note> arises between the elements that establish the composition of the life of the body, the soul, or both. For since the elements are in every way opposed to each other by reason of their origin—namely, Fire to the moisture of the watery sphere (as if to a wife of Earth and Darkness, sharing in the coldness of Earth), and Earth to the Air (as if to a wife of Fire or Light, sharing in fiery heat)—if the bond of concord that ties them in peace is violated and loosed, they must necessarily affect the whole machine with discord and strife. Thus, all **Justice** will be excluded from that **Economy** <note>original: *Oeconomia* — the organized management or vital balance of the body's systems</note>, and consequently, health and well-being will lose their privilege, as their rule is reduced to nothing. Therefore, the bond of peace must be sought, so that each element may again be weighed in the scales of justice with a peaceful proportion of things, and—with stronger reins in their places established for composition—each of them may be held back, led by the bond and fastening of that most ancient Love.

Health, therefore, we see from these things is not life itself, but the fulfillment <note>original: *complementum*</note> of a perfect and unimpeded life; that is, it is that state of life which exists in the **justice** or the proper weight of the **temperament** <term>Temperament: The specific balance of the four humors or elemental qualities in the body that determines a person’s physical and mental nature.</term>. If life, by decreasing, passes beyond this boundary, it is then said to languish and to wander and stray outside the limits of health, and the composite being <note>the human person, made of body and soul</note> is usually said to be sick in that state. Furthermore, it is a most certain principle that the author of health is the same as the author of life... since health is nothing other than the momentary perfection of life. Indeed, it was declared previously that life itself drew its origin from the **Word** <note>original: *verbo* — referring to the Logos or Christ</note> and the **Spirit**. From this it follows that health is created and preserved by the benevolent emanation and breath of the divine light. Conversely, by the contraction or turning away of the greater or lesser rays of life from the living being, one is seen to wander more or less from the limits of health, and is said to live miserably and "to eat his bread with bitterness."

"He rebukes him" (*says Job*) "with pain on his bed, and makes all his bones waste away; bread becomes abominable to him in his life," etc. Truly, the way in which God takes away health is best described by Moses, namely: by leaving men and hiding His face from them, so that many evils and distresses come upon them. And David says: "When He sends forth His spirit, He restores them with health; when He hides His face, He troubles them with sickness," etc. Therefore he says elsewhere: "Jehovah is my light and my salvation; whom should I fear? Jehovah is the strength of my life," inasmuch as salvation <note>original: *salus* — meaning both physical health and spiritual salvation</note> itself is in Him. For this reason, there is no one just and saving except Him; for His visitation is what preserves the spirits of men, and His kindness and pleasantness are the prolongation of life. For by the light of His face, one shall be saved; and he whom He has visited with His salvation shall enjoy good and happiness. Finally, the fountain of life and consequently of health itself is with God. For on one side, the **passive spirit** comes from the fountain of potential matter, which is attributed to the Father; and on the other side, the **formal and active light** comes from the Word or the Son, who is the emanation of delights and joy from the radical source. The union of these two is life itself, as **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many mystical and scientific texts were attributed</note> testifies.

From these things, therefore, it is most clearly evident that health is the act or effect of life exalted to the boundary or measure of justice and perfection; while, on the contrary, the effect of an impeded, imperfect, decreasing, or weakened life is disease or infirmity itself. *What then can harm creatures—among whom I name man the chief—when the kindness of Jehovah is present? "If God," (says David) "is with us, who or what can be against us?" For He will be a guardian to him, so that the Sun shall not strike him by day, nor the Moon by night. He will preserve him from all evil, so that neither heaven nor earth, nor sea nor anything in them, shall harm him. He Himself will preserve his soul or life; He will preserve his going out. For he shall not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that invades in the darkness. No scourge shall approach his tent; for He will give His angels charge over him, and will preserve him even unto a just and praiseworthy old age. For the God of Israel said: "I am even to old age itself; I myself even to gray hairs; I will carry, I have made, I will bear, I will carry and I will save."* All of this the Creator is accustomed to provide by benevolently showing the life-giving face of His countenance to creatures, and by leading them into the way of truth, so that they may have dominion over the malignant spirits. It is the role of these spirits—when the God of light withdraws—to afflict His creatures with evil, infirmity, and disease; a thing they cannot do as long as the benevolence of God is present with them. *"Lift up the light of Your countenance upon us," (says the Royal Prophet) "and it will cause us to see good."* For God is the rock of the righteous, their fortress and deliverer, and their health. In His mercy and kindness, He gives men the power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, so that they may not be harmed at all. But conversely, by the turning away of His face, He leaves the creatures troubled and renders them subject to the malignant power of the enemy. These enemies, though they are strong in the privative <note>referring to a state of lack or the absence of God's light</note> property of God, are weak and powerless in His manifest and open disposition.

**A**CCORDING to the testimony of the Prince and High Priest of Philosophers <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary father of Hermetic philosophy.</note>, **Man is therefore called the son and image of the world**, since he is composed of the parts of the world—namely, heaven and earth. From this it follows that the nature of his heaven is most aptly adapted to the disposition and image of the worldly heaven. For just as the universal <note>original: *Catholicus*, meaning universal or all-encompassing in a physical/metaphysical sense rather than denominational.</note> Heaven or Spirit of the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: The "Great World" or the universe as a whole, which Renaissance thinkers believed was mirrored in the human "Microcosm."</term> is that whole which is divided into three parts or regions distinct in nature and dignity: namely the **Empyrean**, which is the seat of God and the Saints; the **Ethereal**, which is the shrine of Life and the kingdom of the quintessence <term>Quintessence: The "fifth element," a pure, celestial substance superior to the four earthly elements (earth, water, air, fire).</term>; and finally the **Elemental**, which is the lowest of all: so indeed is the heaven of man—namely, the universal Spirit of the Microcosm itself—divided into as many regions differing in dignity from one another. In the **Highest** of these, the divine **Mind** <note>original: *Mens*</note> and angelic **Reason** hold their dominion, whence it is said that **man is the temple of the Holy Spirit, and the kingdom of God is said to be within him.** In the **Middle** region, the <unclear>....</unclear> of life rules, and it is the vital Spirit. The Spirit of these two regions is in itself pure and incorruptible, because elemental corruptibility and change are removed from it; not otherwise than in the starry heaven, where we perceive neither dark clouds, nor lightning, nor comets, nor chasms, nor mists, nor other such things happening beyond the nature of the world. And we have the cause of this matter at hand: namely, because **Strife and the Devil** <note>original: *Litigium & Diabolus*</note> are cast down and expelled from the higher heavens into the lowest, called the elemental realm. Whence he is called the **prince of darkness**, who has dominion in the air <margin>Ephesians 2:2</margin>, whose nature it is, according to his power, to disturb all sublunary things, and to bring in darkness, and clouds, and lightning, and chasms, and fire-brands, and whirlwinds, and typhoons, and earthquakes, and marine tempests, and floods, and pestilential diseases, and constant changes both to the elements and to things made of elements. But truly, into the higher, more divine sanctuaries, he cannot move even a finger (as they say), nor undertake anything: because he has been banished from those places into eternal exile. By the same reasoning, just as in the universal spirit of man, the mind with its empyrean vehicle sits upon the spirit of life, and that in turn is carried in the air of the inner or celestial man: so indeed the prince of darkness with his companions can, by the turning away of the creator’s face, disturb the external spirit of the inner man, and procreate fearful and horrendous meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note> contrary to the laws of human life: and thus he is accustomed to afflict the human spirit with various false apparitions, no differently than to nature...
