...pertaining to man, just as clouds, or lightning, or winds, and other such things pertain to the nature of the world. Through these, **Jehovah** is accustomed to work—sometimes using his dark angels and sometimes his bright ones—to the benefit of those in the world or to their harm. Yet, whatever occurs in this region, or the elementary heaven <note>The "elementary heaven" refers to the atmosphere where weather happens, as opposed to the "celestial heaven" of the stars.</note>, it neither disturbs nor in any way moves or hinders the superior heavens. Those higher spheres nonetheless proceed in their motion without any obstacle, casting their lights in every direction and pouring their influences into the lower regions without distress, even if those lower parts may at times be poorly affected.

The same principle undoubtedly applies to the **Microcosmic** <note>Microcosmic: relating to the human being as a "little world" that mirrors the structure of the entire universe.</note> heavens. For although their lowest part may be hindered and disturbed by various "meteors" <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning.</note> against the laws of nature by dark spirits, in truth, the intellectual heaven of the inner man suffers no internal assault. Nor is the internal Essence of life affected, which we have called the union of the purest Spirit and divine light. Indeed, this essence cannot die, notwithstanding the dissolution of the body; it is only the lowest region of the world, or the airy portion of the world, that suffers such alterations.

From this, the Microcosmic heaven is afflicted and tortured by "febrile lightning," "catarrhal rains," "hypochondriacal winds," "vaporous clouds and mists" (which cause vertigo and scotoma <note>scotoma: a darkening of vision or a blind spot.</note>), thunderous rumblings, and infinite other such morbid symptoms. This, therefore, is the reason why the health of a tranquil life is so often taken away, and the action of life is sometimes rendered most miserable—and this occurs through the hiding of the divine face. But truly, if God again, out of his grace and mercy, sends forth his face, the obstructions of the human "air" are chased away, so that it is rendered serene and clear again, and customary health is granted. We see this just as in the Macrocosm, where the appearance of the Sun dissipates the clouds, chases away the darkness, illuminates the air, and frees the entire elementary region from its disturbances.

So also, when God emits his light and grace into the Microcosmic air, the malignant spirits of darkness—who were strongest and most ferocious in the hidden property of the **Monad** <note>Monad: A term for God as the ultimate, indivisible Unity.</note>—are now rendered weak in his manifested property and are defeated by the spirits of light, and the former health is restored. For unless God is present and favorable to the sick person, neither herb nor poultice can bring any remedy. For it is written,

> that neither herb nor poultice healed them, but the mercy of God, which heals all things. <margin>Wisdom 16:12</margin> <note>original: "quod neq; herba neq; malagma sanavit eos, sed misericordia Dei sanans omnia."</note>

Now, as for what concerns the health of the earth (or the Microcosmic body), it must be stated plainly: just as beyond the arrangement of the heaven or the airy expanse, air is also dispersed everywhere through the earth and through the visible water—which, when inflamed, is accustomed to generate typhoons, will-o'-the-wisps, and fire-vomiting blasts—so it is in the earth or the human body. If it is agitated by a vehemently dry Spirit, it produces earthquakes, watery storms, pestilential vapors, mists, whirlpools, marshy floods, lakes, springs, and other such things, all by the impulse of depraved and dark spirits.

So indeed the matter stands in the earth, or the human body, in which the air is sometimes seen to take on a "Protean" <note>Protean: Ever-changing in shape, named after the Greek sea-god Proteus.</note> fiery nature by the agitation of the prince of darkness. This creates burning diseases in the body, such as <term>gutta rosacea</term> <note>Rosacea: a condition causing redness and visible blood vessels in the face.</note>, <term>erysipelas</term> <note>Erysipelas: a bacterial skin infection once known as "St. Anthony's Fire."</note>, <term>Phlegmona</term> <note>Phlegmon: a spreading inflammatory mass or abscess.</note>, <term>herpes</term>, <term>Wildfire</term> <note>original: "Ignis saluaticus."</note>, and <term>St. Anthony's Fire</term>, <term>Buboes</term> <note>Swollen lymph nodes, often associated with the plague.</note>, and all other inflammations in the fleshy mass.

If, however, the air is coagulated by way of cold condensation, it is changed into <term>Oedemata</term> <note>Edema: swelling caused by excess fluid in body tissues.</note> and thick, viscous, and raw humors. Sometimes, by thickening into a dropsical humor, it converts the mass of the Microcosmic body or earth—either entirely or in parts—into a marshy nature or a land [flooded] everywhere with waters... If it is condensed into hardness, it produces <term>tophi</term> <note>Tophus: a deposit of uric acid crystals, common in gout.</note>, <term>scirrhi</term> <note>Scirrhus: a hard, cancerous tumor.</note>, <term>nodules</term>, and <term>warts</term>, and other such excrescences in the body. For that the flesh itself is almost nothing other than "potential air" is declared by this: that if [exposed to] the cruelty of fire... it is reduced almost entirely into air and into nothingness.

From these things, therefore, it shines forth clearly enough that the **Prince of Darkness**, who has power in the air both above the earth and upon the earth, is most ready to work his wicked effects in the "air" of both the **Microcosmic** <note>Microcosmic: pertaining to the human body and soul as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note> body and soul—provided that God, in His **privative property**, permits this, and as long as he is not prohibited in his malignancy by the contrary property of God. By this reasoning, the Prince of Darkness is accustomed to corrupt the laws of life and health, both in the outermost portion of the internal man and in his innermost depths. We say that health is present in the human body when its elements are arranged in equal proportion and measure according to justice, or at least according to weight, and are bound together in a mixture by a strong bond of the **Spirit of fiery love**. In this state, man is preserved and maintained by a benevolent and manifest God through the ministry of bright and good spirits. But indeed, when God hides His face and dark spirits serve the body, man falls from the state of health into the misfortune of pains and diseases.

From this, therefore, the Wise Man concludes that God has power over both life and death, and consequently over both health and disease; for it is He who leads down to the gates of hell and brings back again. It is He who kills and makes alive; He who strikes and He who heals. It is He who pursues with tribulation, darkness, dissolution, and gloom. And again: He alone is the one who saves from all evils and tribulations: for there is no other God who can save besides the God of Israel. Finally, it belongs to Him to be indignant in His wrath and **un-will** <note>original: "noluntate" — a technical term meaning God's "negative" or "withholding" will.</note>; yet in His will, He gives life. For He takes away life by contracting Himself—or His truth—into Himself, and He gives life by giving the inspiration of life to all. In Him, therefore, we live, move, and have our being; in Him also we die, rest in our dust, and cease to be. Finally, this is He who works in all things; wherefore, this is that **God of peace**, who fits men for every good thing, that they may do His will. This is the giver of life to all, this is our savior, who wants all men to be saved; and here again, He is the **Consuming Fire**: the God of wars and armies, rebuking through pain upon the bed, making the soul of the sick man draw near to corruption and his life to the bringers of death.

<margin>Psalm 104:29.</margin>
We conclude, therefore, that God in His one property—namely, the **positive** one—not only effects and preserves full life but also the balance of health. In His other property—the **privative** one—He not only removes the dominion of health but even causes life itself to waste away and languish in pains and infirmities. This is according to the words of the Royal Psalmist: *When God sends forth His Spirit, creatures are created and satisfied with good* (that is, they enjoy health and the happiness of life); *when He hides His face, they are troubled* (that is, health being lost, they are afflicted by diseases and pains); *when He takes back their Spirit, they expire and die.*

<margin>
Psalm 4:9.
Hebrews 13.
</margin>
By these things it is explained clearly enough: that God Himself is the one and the same author of both life and health, and death and disease—but in a different "property." In the former property, the positive, He is called the **God of peace, light, and life**; in this sense, David speaks of Him thus: *Whom God alone has placed in safety, he shall lie down and sleep in peace at the same time* (that is, in health and the happiness of life). Hence also, the Apostle called Him the **God of peace** in express words in the place cited before. In the latter property, the privative, He is called the **God of wrath, vengeance, terror, and the Terrible One**, as you have declared in many places of the Holy Scriptures.

# CHAPTER V.

->On Salvation: and the difference between health and salvation; and that the ancient Heathen Sages understood nothing certain regarding the Savior of the world.<-

We shall perceive that a certain difference is made between health—or soundness—and salvation in various places of the Scriptures, if we look at the matter with a slightly more authoritative gaze: even though in certain places they seem to signify the same thing.

<margin>Exodus 25.</margin>
<margin>Exodus 23.</margin>
<margin>Daniel 3.</margin>
<margin>John 3:16.</margin>
<margin>Matthew 13:43.</margin>
<margin>Luke 19:9.</margin>
<margin>John 6:39.</margin>
<margin>Ephesians 2:1.</margin>
<margin>John 12:35.</margin>
We define health, or wellness, as the breadth or effect of the fullness of the momentary—or primary and present—life; or, we say health is the absence of diseases and infirmities in this life. Whence Jehovah said, *I will remove every disease from the midst of you*. And elsewhere: *You shall serve your Lord, and He will bless your bread and your water, and will take away infirmity from your midst.* But indeed, **salvation** properly intends the highest and eternal blessing in the second life, even though it is sometimes accepted for "safety" <note>The Latin word *salus* can mean both "health" and "safety/salvation." Fludd is distinguishing between the physical state of being healthy and the spiritual state of being saved.</note> in this life. In this sense the Prophet speaks: *There is no other God who can save besides the God of Israel, etc.* Thus, in this sense, salvation was, for example, the liberation of Daniel from the lions' den, and of the three children of Israel from the fiery furnace.

However, he understands salvation properly accepted where he speaks in these words: *He who believes in him does not perish, but shall have eternal life: in which the just shall shine like the Sun, in the kingdom of their Father.* But this is that true and eternal salvation, through the mediation of which the Son of Man is accustomed to make safe <note>original: "salvum facere," meaning to save or make whole.</note> that which had perished, by raising it up on the last day, so that it may have eternal life: in which there is neither disease nor infirmity, but perpetual health. For he is said to quicken men with a new life at that time when they were dead in sin, according to the prince of the power of the air <note>A reference to Ephesians 2:2, implying the devil's influence over the physical atmosphere.</note>. And this was done by the **multiplication of light**, while the light is held, which is achieved through faith in the true light: through the mediation of which, the children of eternal light are made, glowing with splendor and shining like the Sun. In this way, true salvation is completed and perfected, which is never subjected to morbid impediments or evil passions: because it is entirely free from the assaults of darkness; because in a divine act of this kind, the light is seen to prevail.

This whole matter is clearly shown by Christ himself through the parable of the multiplication of the **talents** in tenfold and fivefold: where by the **golden talent**, that **living gold of life** <note>original: "aurum illud vitæ vivum." In alchemical philosophy, "living gold" refers to the purified spiritual essence within a person.</note> to be bought from Christ is understood: which is the sole truth of man. This truth ought to be multiplied by a true Christian in this life: for that light of truth was given and committed to each person on this condition: that by his own industry, and by the magnetic virtue of that luminous mind, he might attract rays or sparks similar to himself, whereby he may increase in the weight of his essence and the measure of his virtue: so that by his own increase, once regeneration has occurred, he may have dominion over the darkness. But this work is deeply mystical, and was signified to us by Christ and the Apostles in a copious, though sufficiently enigmatic, manner: and explained through the "light of the world," "hidden wisdom," the "talent of gold," the "kingdom of God" multiplied from a grain into a great tree like a grain of mustard seed of faith, "the truth," and other such names.

We say, therefore, that **salvation** properly so-called occurs when the incorruptible spark of God's Spirit in man is multiplied by the life-giving and illustrious power of the **uncreated light** in the world (which is Christ himself in spirit); by whose preceding power the whole man, in a true resurrection—death, darkness, and ignorance having been conquered—is transmuted into the image of Christ: and is said to become one with him. From the consequence of this, it will be clear what a **Savior** is: namely, *That uncreated Light: or the holy Emanation sent forth from the face of the Father: through the mediation of which, man lives not only a temporal life, but also an eternal one; for this is the life-giving Spirit of the world, which, by the testimony of the Apostle, gives life to all things: this is that eternal Christ, who fills all things: This is the incorruptible Spirit, which (by the testimony of the Wise Man) is in every thing. This is that Spirit, which makes friends of God and Prophets: this...*

That Spirit, with whose assistance Christ—though a mortal man—was made not only a Prophet, but a Prophet far greater than all others, and because of the abundance of that Spirit within him, was called the Son of God, anointed from on high, and filled with the Holy Spirit. From this comes the *Word in which was life, through which and by which all things were made: the light of the world, by which all men who come into this world are, shall be, and have been illuminated.* <note>original: "Verbum in quo erat vita..." quoting John 1:4-9.</note> This does not mean these things were made by Christ the man, but by Christ the uncreated Spirit, who existed before all things. By means of this Spirit, Christ the man, through his actions, left us the hope of a true resurrection. Hence, all who possess that anointing from on high are called "Christs" <note>The word "Christ" means "Anointed One." Fludd is arguing that any holy person "anointed" by God participates in this spiritual nature.</note>; it is in this sense that we should understand David, where he speaks in the person of God: *touch not my anointed ones* <note>original: "nolite tangere Christos meos." From Psalm 105:15.</note>; where by "Christs," the Anointed Prophets are understood. This light, therefore, is the root of temporal life, and this same light is the Author of eternal life. By losing a portion of this light, the first Adam fell into the sphere of darkness and ignorance; and by the recovery of that same portion (lost in the first man) in the "second Adam" (whom the holy scriptures therefore call *life-giving* and *spiritual*), man emerged again from the abyss of darkness. From this arose *Jesus*, or *Soter*, or the *Savior of the world*, the light emitted by the Father before any creature existed, so that those in the world submerged in darkness and dead in sin might be led back again to life and health, and be guided from the paths of error into the way of truth.

By these words, it is clear enough that it was not Christ the mortal man who saves, but that eternal and spiritual Spirit, filling all things, who is truly God, and who filled Christ the man with His essential power. He attributed the name JESUS to him in respect to the life-giving and eternal Word—concerning which <term>Reuchlin</term> <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a German humanist and scholar of Hebrew. Yet at other times he spoke in his fleshly nature, according to the flesh. It was, therefore, this God-formed Spirit that caused him to rise from death to eternal life, even though, on the other hand, he had died in his human nature. *What does it matter* (says the Apostle) *that Christ died for us, if he had not risen from death? Our hope would be in vain.* From this has arisen the error of many mortals, who look upon the external creature itself instead of the internal Creator: so much so, that they place no distinction at all between the flesh and the Divinity within the flesh. Hence their senses are so dull and blunt that, by accepting and worshiping the creature instead of the Creator, they commit an abominable idolatry. Even the Heathen, who sensed something of a Savior of the world, accepted this or that man as the Creator; they did not perceive that it is not the sensible man, but the intellectual and truly divine nature within the man that saves—which also reigns everywhere outside of man in the world, both the Typical and the Archetypal, sent forth by the Father for the existence of all things, and yet not at all separated from the Father's bosom.

### Volume I. Treatise I. Section I. Part I. Book II. ###

Some of these people, therefore, looked for **Aesculapius** <note>The Greek god of medicine and healing.</note> as the one who was to come into this world as the Savior. For as it is recorded in Plato's *Phaedo*, Socrates—when he was about to drink the poisonous and lethal cup and was close to death—ordered a cock to be offered to Aesculapius, as if to his father **Apollo**, that is, to the first and incorporeal Sun, the dispenser of eternal life. He did this so that he might return the soul of a man dying peacefully with a shout of joy and a hymn of praise. For the cock is sacred to Apollo (who is called the Sun), being the joyful herald of the hours and the day. Moreover, Aesculapius was called by the ancients "Jubilation, Victory, and Triumph," which is named a **Paean** <note>A song of triumph or thanksgiving, usually addressed to Apollo or Aesculapius.</note>. Hence, Orpheus sang:

> Aesculapius, healer of all, Lord Paean,
> Come, blessed Savior, granting a noble end to life.
<note>original Greek: "Ιητὴρ πάντων Ασκληπιὲ, δέσποτα Παιάν, Ἕλθε μάκαρ Σωτήρ βιοτῆς τέλος ἐθλὸν ὀπάζων."</note>

->This is:<-

->*Aesculapius, Healer of all things, Lord Paean,*<-
->*Come, blessed Savior, granting a good end to life.*<-

Furthermore, the Emperor Julian <note>Julian "the Apostate," the last pagan Roman emperor, who wrote "Against the Galileans" to refute Christianity.</note> says in his *second book against the Galileans* that Jupiter begat Aesculapius from himself among his "intelligible beings" <note>In Neoplatonic philosophy, these are divine realities perceived by the mind rather than the senses.</note> and destined him for the earth through the life-giving power of the Sun. He claims that Aesculapius, making his progress from heaven to earth, appeared in human form around Epidaurus. Having grown through his successes, he extended his saving right hand over the entire earth to restore ill-disposed souls and weak bodies. Indeed, this Emperor seems to assert in another place that he knew many people who were helped by Aesculapius in the greatest dangers, and he recounts that he himself, when laboring in sickness, often escaped safely through his healings.

Others believed that Hercules, the son of Jove and Alcmena, was that *Soter* or Savior of the world, so often predicted by the divine oracles. The Thasians <note>Inhabitants of the Greek island of Thasos.</note>, among others, defended this strenuously; for which reason they inscribed this on their public coins: *Hercules, Savior of the Thasians.* <note>original Greek: "Ἡρακλεὺς Σωτῆρ Θασσίων"</note>

Furthermore, even among the Celts, he was held and worshiped as such: because he was the shaper of morals and the teacher of every noble discipline in all parts of the world.

But the Egyptians and certain others regarded their King **Ptolemy** as the Savior of the world, just as the Romans did **Curtius** <note>Referring to Marcus Curtius, a legendary Roman hero who sacrificed himself by leaping into a chasm to save the city.</note>—since he, by his own death, saved the land when it was suffering from a vast opening in the earth. And so, many others, raving in their own fashion and announcing nothing certain, accepted the Savior predicted by the ancient prophets, but they mistook external men for the Savior of the world, rather than the internal Spirit descending immediately from God into man. In a similar respect, **JOSEPH** is called by Pharaoh "Savior of the World."
<margin>Genesis 41:45 and 47:25.</margin>

But which of these men was so filled with the Holy Spirit as was that true Savior and *Soter* of the world? Not without reason was he called **Christ** and **Jesus** because of his actual works. He was not a fiction in the manner of Aesculapius or Hercules, the gods of the Heathen; but the **true son of the true God Jehovah**, of whom it was written that he was *most full of the Spirit of the living God.* Was either Aesculapius, or Hercules, or Ptolemy, or any other "Pseudo-Savior" of the Pagans ever so filled with divinity as He who, besides the vast miracles performed in the world, rose from the dead in a true resurrection? Or does it seem likely, according to Julian’s observation, that Aesculapius, descending from heaven, appeared in human form at Epidaurus to restore souls, when it is handed down by trustworthy historians that in his own life he did nothing...

# On the Super-Celestial Origin of Life and Health #

...is anything notable, other than that he healed Hippolytus? <note>In Greek myth, the physician-god Aesculapius restored Hippolytus to life, which angered the gods of the underworld.</note> Indeed, if this one is worthy of being called the son of Jupiter or Apollo, why was he eventually struck by a thunderbolt from his great Father and died such a horrific death? <note>Zeus/Jupiter killed Aesculapius with a lightning bolt to prevent him from making all men immortal.</note>

But in truth, all these figures, through their fictions, seemed to prefigure the truly real Savior. Where they argue for Aesculapius—arisen from Apollo or born of Jupiter and descending from heaven—they are pointing toward the **Luminous Emanation**, the life and health of the world sent forth from Jehovah Himself, the source of eternal light. This emanation later clothed itself in flesh and was said to "become flesh"; yet it did not do so in a way that it ceased to fill all things or exist everywhere, but in Christ the Savior, it abounded through super-eminence... bestowing upon him the name of the Son of God himself, as was said above.

Therefore, this **Divine Wisdom** <note>original Latin: *Sapientia diuina*</note> is that cornerstone which is able to perform all miracles, raising men from death to eternal life through a true resurrection and transferring them into the divine nature. Neither Aesculapius nor Hercules, but that true **Savior** <note>original Greek: *Soter*</note>, the true **Jesus**, first demonstrated to us the way of this miracle—more wonderful than any miracle—through the power of His eternal Spirit. Having conquered death, and acting as the true intelligible splendor or emanation of Apollo, He killed the dark serpent **Python** <note>The author allegorizes Apollo's slaying of the serpent Python as Christ's victory over the devil or death.</note>—which was procreated from the slime and dregs of the earth—by His own power. That is to say, by overcoming the Dragon and the Underworld <note>original Latin: *Orcus*</note>, He caused His dead body to rise from death to eternal life in a glorious and magnificent form. He did this so that we, following His example, might have a more certain hope through the power of that eternal Spirit to have a similar resurrection and a similar life through the **Spiritual Jesus**. This is that **Universal Spirit** <note>original Latin: *Spiritus Catholicus*</note> **which gives life to all things; for in Him alone (and in no other) is life, and that life is the light of the world**, <note>A reference to John 1:4.</note> from which the world and all things in it were fundamentally made, brought to life, and preserved in a state of salvation by an admirable reason and ineffable harmony. Therefore, through the mediation of this spiritual Christ, or life-giving Jesus, regeneration has been accomplished in this world; whence the Wise Man said:

<margin>Wisdom 9</margin>
> *Who can know the things that are in heaven? Or who understands the things that please you, unless you have given wisdom and sent your Spirit from the high heavens? Thus were the paths of the Fathers corrected, etc.* <note>Quoting the Wisdom of Solomon 9:16-18, a book of the Apocrypha/Deuterocanon.</note>

Furthermore, with this Spirit assisting, the Resurrection will be accomplished in the world to come. Indeed, through His mediation, all things will be made new; for by His operation, the heavens will be renewed, and the earth itself set right.

Here, therefore, you have the Spiritual Christ filling all things, as the Apostle testifies. Thus you understand the true Jesus, the unique **Savior** <note>original Greek: *Soter*</note> and Deliverer of both worlds: to whom alone it belongs to cure both the soul and the infirm body, and to establish a sound mind in a sound body <note>Adapting the classical ideal of *mens sana in corpore sano*.</note>. That we might find Him, that Light—dwelling in the human body or "house of clay"—commands us to knock so that it may be opened to us, and to seek so that we may find.

But now let us proceed to the Kabbalistic <note>A reference to Jewish mystical tradition, which the author integrates into his Christian Neoplatonist worldview.</note> demonstration of the same, in which we shall begin to clarify and explain the properties or emanation of life and mercy, according to the opinions of the ancient Sages.

### CHAPTER VI.

### How the two divine properties—namely, the privative and the positive—are signified by the experts most skilled in the Kabbalah, through the natures and conditions of the ten divine names contained within the Sephirotic Tree.

In Chapter 10, Section 1, Part 4, Page 2, Book 4, Member 1 of our *History of the Meteorology of the Macrocosm*, you have a description of the nature of the **Sephirotic Tree** <note>The *Arbor Sephirotica* or Tree of Life is a central symbol in the Kabbalah, representing the ten attributes or "emanations" through which the Infinite God reveals Himself.</note>, as well as the reason why a different name of God presides over each numeration or Sephirotic branch. There, you also have it demonstrated that in the essence of God there is no diversity, since it is a single identity within itself. For this reason, we declared there that only a single **Essential Name** <note>original: *nomen Essentiale*</note> should be attributed to Him: and that is the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH (יהוה), often rendered as "Jehovah" or "Lord."</note>. This is His inseparable name, appropriated to Him alone, which, according to the opinion of **Rabbi Moses** <note>Maimonides (1138–1204), the famous Jewish philosopher known as "the Egyptian."</note>, includes and argues for the substance and being of the Creator in a pure sense, without any participation with or respect to created things. Other names assigned to Him denote God Himself in relation to participation—that is, with regard to created things—and consequently, they are recognized by the effects of His works.

Hence, it was for this reason that His essential name was never uttered except in the Sanctuary by the holy Priests of the Lord, and specifically in the Priestly blessing by the High Priest on the day of the fast <note>Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement.</note>. Therefore, according to the opinion of the Egyptian Rabbi Moses, the level of this name is so holy that it was not to be uttered rashly by the mouth; for it denotes that God is and was above all Essence, insofar as He existed before any thing was.

But His other names denote God from His works, and insofar as He works all in all and exists in every thing. And this was the precious name of God that Moses desired to understand from God, from whom he is said to have received this response: **יהוה**, that is, *my name forever*. This name is indeed so pure and simple that it cannot be articulated or composed by the human voice.

But in truth, the divine nature exists in and works within created things just as much as it does outside them. To the extent that the **Tetragrammaton** is the common agent in every branch of the Sephirotic tree, it holds dominion throughout the entire trunk of that tree; by its power and dominion, all His other ten surnames are subjected to His command, which are merely His properties and the effects of various virtues of that single and indivisible Essence. Thus, among the various surnames of God inscribed on the Sephirotic tree, **Ehieh** <note>Hebrew: אהיה, meaning "I Am" or "I Will Be," from Exodus 3:14.</note> signifies the fountain and origin of all creatures, the foundation of sincere mercy and clemency, full of all graces, sparing all, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation. Christ teaches us to pray to Him in that formula for paternal benefits: *Our Father, who art in heaven, etc.* And from this, it is said that *the Father judges no one*. Furthermore, it is appropriated to the Father, because it is the office of a Father to always act with clemency and benevolence toward his children. How the Father has mercy on his children is declared by David in Psalm 103. Therefore, this name—acting as the President of the entire Sephirotic order—is assigned to the numeration, or the gate of light, or the chief branch of the Kabbalistic tree; which branch, or numeration, or gate of light, or most holy Emanation, is for this reason called **Cheter** <note>Keter (כתר), meaning "Crown," the topmost Sephira representing the Divine Will.</note> or the **Crown**. For just as the Crown is the root, as it were, of the whole tree, so indeed is *Ehieh* the Father and Root of all creation. By these things we are reminded that this Emanation is the first degree of the whole disposition or positive and life-giving property of God, and consequently it is occupied with clemency and mercy, insofar as He is seen to delight in creation and in the quickening of His creatures.

Furthermore, as the second surname of God in the Sephirotic order is **Iah** <note>Yah (יה), a shortened form of the Tetragrammaton associated with the second Sephira, Chokmah (Wisdom).</note>; which, in the formation of the world and the extraction from the womb of the moist nature and Chaos, is exercis...

-># On the super-celestial origin of Life and Health.<-

...so indeed this kind of emanation or luminous gate, over which **Jah** <note>original: *Iah*; a shortened form of the divine name YHWH, often associated with the initial flash of creation</note> presides, is called **Chokhmah** <note>original: *Hochma*; Hebrew for "Wisdom," the second Sephirah or divine attribute</note> due to the effect of that divine name’s property. Concerning this, it is written: <margin>Proverbs 8, Job 28</margin> *“When he formed the heavens above, when he strengthened the fountains of the deep, when he set a law for the sea and established the foundations of the earth, I, Wisdom, was with him as a foster-child, arranging all things. When he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters, when he set a law for the rains and a path for the sounding storms, then he saw Wisdom.”* Furthermore, because of its kindly disposition, Wisdom is said to be <margin>Wisdom of Solomon 7 & 9</margin> *“a mild and kind spirit, loving what is good.”* Elsewhere it is said that Wisdom is granted by God to humanity to show them His will. Nevertheless, as it is observed, this emanation is placed between **Keter** <note>original: *Cheter*; the first Sephirah, "The Crown," representing the infinite source</note> and **Binah** <note>The third Sephirah, "Understanding"</note>. While Keter signifies mercy, Binah signifies severity. Thus, the divine name **Jah**, whose influence is Wisdom itself, sometimes appears to involve punishment and severity, although this is quite rare; hence Jehovah said, speaking of the Angel or of Wisdom: <margin>Exodus 23</margin> *“Do not provoke him, for he will not bear your rebellion, because my name is in him.”*

Here, therefore, you have a double property contained within one and the same luminous gate: namely, a "privative" or limiting property, though in a smaller proportion, and a "positive" or creative property in a much greater measure and stronger respect. Thus, its mercy far exceeds its severity.

The third name is **Elohim**, whose property is clearly explained in the title of the third numeration or emanation, which is **Binah**, or **Prudence** <note>The author uses the Latin *Prudentia* to translate the Hebrew *Binah*, which means "Understanding" or "Discernment"</note>. The Kabbalists maintain that the name *Elohim* indicates fear and terror, insofar as through this property of God, severe accidents, punishments, and slaughters come upon both the celestial and terrestrial worlds. For by means of this disposition, God exercises His power both for sudden alterations in the world and for punishing the wicked. Hence the Wise Man said: <margin>Wisdom of Solomon 11:21</margin> *“The spirit of the power of God sifts and justice pursues the unjust.”* and elsewhere: <margin>Jeremiah 30:23</margin> *“Behold the whirlwind of the Lord, a fury going forth, a rushing storm; it shall rest upon the head of the wicked.”* So Isaiah says: <margin>Isaiah 29:9</margin> *“Be amazed and stagger, for he has mixed for you a spirit of deep sleep,”* and infinite other examples of the effects of this property are to be found in the Holy Page, which I will not detail here for the sake of brevity. But as the Teachers of Wisdom testify: God, as *Elohim*, uses Angels as His instruments in this property. For this reason, they are called **Bene Elohim** by the Hebrews—that is, the **Sons of God**. Those skilled in the Kabbalah hold that the quarter of the world from which these kinds of demons or turbulent spirits are sent is the **North** <note>original: *Aquilo*; the north wind. In biblical tradition, the north was often the source of judgment or "evil" coming upon the land</note>, since from there all evil or punishment is expected. To the action of this property are attributed all elementary changes and alterations, such as the constriction and condensation of air into thick clouds, snow, hail, ice, frost, and all cold blasts that are enemies to life. This is the reason why the influences of **Saturn** are so adverse to the life-giving nature, because they flow from this source or "luminous gate" into the sphere of Saturn, from which they are later poured out into the elements, as will be discussed more clearly in the appropriate place.

You see, therefore, that the entire power of the **Kabbalistic Tree** depends on these three primordial branches, just as the **Typical World** <note>The physical world as a "type" or reflection</note> depends on the **Archetypal World** <note>The world of divine ideas and blueprints</note>, which consists of a triple property related to the persons in the Holy Trinity. For the number "three" in the intelligible world denotes and implies the same thing that "seven" does in the Typical world. For "two" is the root of **Matter**, just as "three" is the root of **Form**. Moreover, just as "one" is the formal root to "three" and the material root to "two," so "two" is the material root to "four," and "three" is the formal root to the same. These, when united, constitute the number **seven**, from which the entire Typical world was formed.

Indeed, just as through the triple property—that is, through the prudence of the radical **Monad** <note>The "One" or Unity</note>—a strict union was made between the three and the four, so that prudence makes an inviolable bond between strife and friendship. By this bond, both dark matter and luminous form are joined into one; sometimes they clash and act in a tumultuous manner, especially where dark matter holds dominion in the elementary kingdom, as appears in Thunder, where

### Volume I. Treatise I. Section I. Part I. Book II.

Just as fire, when compressed within a thick and dark cloud, breaks forth with a tumultuous roar, so it is established that in the first part of the threefold property <note>The "ternary property" refers to the first three Sephiroth: Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah</note>, sincere mercy is demonstrated through a positive arrangement. For the hidden God now stands open solely for the creation of the world, according to the words of the Wise Man:
<margin>Wisdom 1.</margin>
> God did not create death:
> but made all things that they might exist, etc. <note>original: "Deus non creauit mortem: sed fecit omnia, vt essent." from Wisdom of Solomon 1:13</note>

In the final part <note>referring to Binah/Understanding</note>, severity and disturbance are declared through a privative, contractive, and restrictive arrangement. Finally, the intermediate part <note>referring to Chokhmah/Wisdom</note> participates in both mercy and severity; yet truly, because His mercies are to be preferred far above His severity, this intermediate state is a thousand times more concerned with mercy than with vengeance or terror.

Here, therefore, you have the two properties of the one Monad <note>The "Monad" represents the unified Godhead before differentiation</note> expressed in the Archetype: namely, that which is open on one side and that which is hidden on the other. And just as both of these were potentially in the radical Monad, so they are also potentially present in the divine name **Jah** <note>original: *Iah*</note>. These three relate to the works of the first three days of creation, in which the world was completed. However, the seven following **Sephiroth** <note>original: *Sephirotæ*; the divine emanations or "numbers"</note> pertain to the various alterations in the already completed world, both fortunate and favorable as well as unfortunate.

For the name of God **El** presides over the fourth **Sephirah**—that is, the fourth numeration or luminous gate and emanation. Because of the benevolent effects of this name, it is called **Chesed** <note>Hebrew for "Mercy" or "Loving-kindness"</note>, or clemency; its inflows are grace, life, and full of goodness. Experience has proven that its influences, when poured into the sphere of **Jupiter**, cherish lower life-forms and assist those endowed with life through the highest piety and mercy. From this numeration, therefore, the seeds of life, grace, health, and preservation are rained down into the lower worlds through its channel or luminous gate.

**Elohim Gibbor** <note>Hebrew for "God of Might" or "Strong God"</note> presides over the fifth numeration. From the violent effect of that property, this luminous gate is called **Geburah**, which is to say, Power and Strength. In this property, God is said to have brought forth the elements from the bowels of turbulent Chaos. This gate denotes violence, severity, wrath, judgment, and the punishment of sinners. Through its mediation, and by way of the sphere of **Mars**, there flow into the lower world plagues, famines, wars, robberies, desolations, thunders, comets, and things of this sort.

Hence it is clear that just as the name **El**, through its numeration **Chesed**, promises every good from the Creator, so on the contrary, **Elohim Gibbor**, through its gate **Geburah**, sends forth into worldly creatures malevolent seeds or influences by way of the sphere of **Mars**. For this reason, Mars is called by astrologers the **Lesser Malefic** <note>original: *Infortunium minus*; a traditional astrological term for Mars as a source of minor hardship</note>, just as **Saturn** is the **Greater Malefic** <note>original: *Infortunium maius*</note> due to its malevolent, cold, and freezing effects.

The luminous gate of the sixth order is called **Tipheret** <note>original: *Tephereth*; Hebrew for "Beauty" or "Adornment"</note>, which denotes grace, ornament, beauty, and delights. It received this splendor from the property of the divine name **Eloah**, which presides over it. From here, through the influence of this channel, the celestial Sun is formed and decorated with its admirable clarity and life-giving virtue, so that the heavens are adorned by its brilliance, according to the words of Job: <margin>Job 28.</margin> *By His spirit He has adorned the heavens.* <note>Job 26:13</note> It is from here that the vigor of both life and clarity is cast down from the Sun into the lower realms, by which the mineral, vegetable, and animal kingdoms grow and multiply.

The seventh order is filled by the numeration **Netzach** <note>original: *Netzeth*; Hebrew for "Victory" or "Endurance"</note>, which implies Triumph and Victory, and also charity, justice, and love. From this follow the influences of multiplication and generation, which descend into the sphere of **Venus**. For this reason, Venus is called the **Lesser Benefic** <note>original: *Fortunium minus*; a source of minor good fortune</note>, just as **Jupiter** is the **Greater Benefic** <note>original: *Fortunium majus*</note>. The name of God from which such effects proceed is **Jehovah Sabaoth** <note>original: *Iehova Sabaoth*</note>, the Lord of Hosts, and the God of Jubilation and Perfection.

The eighth luminous gate is called **Hod**, signifying Praise, honor, and beauty. Over this presides **Elohim Sabaoth**, or the God of Hosts, in which He works His changeable influences according to His will within the sphere of **Mercury**.

# On the Supercelestial Life and the Origin of Health.

The ninth title of God is **El chai**, which is to say, the **Living God**; or **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai"</note>, as if to say the **Almighty God**, or He who is self-sufficient. His Sephira <note>original: "Numeratio", referring to the ten Sephiroth or divine emanations in Kabbalah</note> is called **Yesod**, meaning **Foundation**, Basis, redemption, or rest; it sends its influences into the sphere of the Moon.

Finally, the tenth Sephira is called **Malkuth**; that is, the **Kingdom**, the Empire, or the Temple of God. Here, it pours its free influences into the elements of both the world and of man. The Name of God presiding over this is **Adonai**, or **the Lord**, and this Sephira carries with it severity and a sense of servitude toward God Himself when His wrath prevails over mortals.

When these things are rightly considered, it is clear to see that in all the properties or operations of the Divine Essence in the world—whether they lead to punishment and the lash, or to benevolence—God is more inclined toward clemency and mercy than toward severity: for

In the property of His first name, He extends His charity out of the darkness into the world, like a father to a son; hence **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy</note> calls the World the "son of God."

<margin>Numbers 14.</margin>
In that second property, by means of His wisdom, He is more inclined toward creating things than toward afflicting the human race for its sins, as can be seen from these words to the Israelites:
> *The Lord God is long-suffering and of great kindness, forgiving iniquity and transgression, who by no means clears the guilty, etc.* <note>original: "Deus Iehoua est longanimis multus benignitate..." citing Numbers 14:18</note>

Furthermore, we shall declare elsewhere that the Angel who preceded the Israelites in the desert was Wisdom itself, <margin>Exodus 23.</margin> of whom it was said:
> *Behold, I send my Angel before you, to keep you in your way and lead you into the place I have prepared for you. Do not provoke him, for he will not bear my transgressions, because my name is in him.*

In the property of the third title, security, wrath, and cruelty are included.

In the fourth, **El** is the name of mercy; just as in the fifth, **Elohim Gibbor** <note>The "Mighty God"</note> is the name of severity. Thus **Eloah** is filled with clemency, life, and beauty; and so it is with the others.

But lest some **Momus** <note>A classical personification of mockery and harsh criticism</note>—of the same sort as the monk **Marin Mersenne** <note>A French polymath and priest who famously attacked the "occult" philosophies of Robert Fludd and others</note>—be incited against Kabbalistic doctrine, whether by mocking laughter, a thirst for quibbling, or plain malice; or perhaps blinded by ignorance, he might object: "What use to us is this Kabbalistic science of yours, than which nothing in the world is more vain?" (I speak now almost with the voice of that Monk, who attempts to dissuade men from the study of Kabbalistic science with his old wives' reasoning) or: "How is it to be proven that this or that name of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> has this or that property, or various actions in this world—namely, one for clemency and another for manifold severity?" To these I respond according to the observation of the ancient Sages: this is demonstrated to be true by the **effect**, according to the testimony of the holy letters. For example: Moses, in his prayer for the recovery of the health of **Miriam** <note>original: "Mariæ"</note>, who was afflicted with leprosy, uses the name of God **El**, saying, *El na ra-pha.* It is as if he said: *O El (that is, God of grace and clemency), ra-pha (that is, heal); na (I beseech you); her.*

Therefore, through the effects that followed the pronunciation of the divine name in the Sacred Text, the Hebrew Doctors judged the nature and property of the Name. This is no different than judging the nature and property of a temperament by a **physiognomic** <note>The practice of assessing a person's character or health from their outer appearance</note> look, or observing the effects of the signs of the Heavens, as we do with rain, winds, thunder, and other such things. Because such observations in the heavens usually produce certain results, therefore, when those omens appear, we say immediately that such effects will happen in the world.

But we say that Divinity itself is more occupied with its mercy than in the opposite property: because (as has been said) through the fatherly property of the first gate, He made all things; not that they should perish, but that they should exist. Therefore, God's mercy is far greater than His severity, which even the Text seems to acknowledge quite openly

**The sacred text:** where we find that God is clement, merciful, patient, and of much mercy, and forgiving of wickedness. By which the Wise Man seems to hint that God is greatly prone to mercy and clemency, and slow to vengeance; although in His hand are good and evil, life and death, etc., as has been confirmed above by the testimony of the holy scriptures.

**We conclude, therefore,** that all these titles of God, understood as properties in the Sephirotic Tree <note>The "Tree of Life" in Kabbalah, representing the ten emanations of God</note>, whether in clemency or severity, are contained under that single Essential Name **יהוה** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHVH or Jehovah</note>, which by its own virtue fills the entire trunk of the Sephirotic Tree: no differently than He is said to be present everywhere in the World and to fill all things. Whence it is clear that this name retains within itself the dual nature and power of the one radical monad <note>The "monad" refers to the ultimate, indivisible Unity of God from which all plurality emerges</note> from which it arises: namely, both the **positive** and the **privative** <note>In this context, "positive" refers to God's active outpouring of life, while "privative" refers to the withdrawal or contraction of that life, which results in suffering or death</note>; of which the former is more inclined toward clemency. For in His positive nature, by a natural inclination, He is occupied with giving life and imparting benefits to creatures rather than destruction or harm; whence in this property He is said to have mercy on all, to overlook the sins of men, and to loathe nothing He has made, but rather to spare all because they are His and because He loves souls; seeing as He produced them in His benevolence—namely, in His names **Ehieh, El, Eloah, Iah,** etc.

But truly, when He puts on His privative or contractive nature, He is said to pursue His enemies with tribulation, darkness, dissolution, and anguish. He is said to withhold the waters so that they dry up, and by thus condensing the air, to send them forth so that they overturn the earth. It is said that with Him is the one who errs and the one who leads into error; and that He causes counselors to become mad and makes judges foolish, so that they grope in the dark like drunken men when the light fails. Thus, by the spirit of His power, He is said to scatter and pursue the unjust with justice. Thus He gathers the waters of the sea into a heap. Thus, at the vision of an angry God, the waters were afraid and the depths were troubled, and the clouds above gave out a sound; even His small stones <note>Refers to hailstones</note> pierced through. Thus He covers the heavens with thick clouds. Thus He gives snow like wool, scatters frost like ashes, and casts down ice like morsels; He sends out cold so vehement that no one can stand before Him. Thus His whirlwind and fury are said to go forth; a rushing storm upon the heads of His enemies. Thus He sends a spirit of deep sleep and mixes it among men, so that they waver and stagger and are as if intoxicated. Thus He rouses a spirit that puts lies into the mouths of prophets. Thus He sends upon men the wrath of His indignation—anger and tribulation—through evil angels. Thus an evil spirit of God was said to have possessed Saul.

So it is in the **Macrocosm** <note>The Great World or Universe</note>. He bowed the heavens and came down, and darkness was under His feet; and He placed darkness around Him as a hiding place, sifting the waters from the clouds of the heavens. Thus He brought palpable darkness into Egypt; thus at the death of Christ, universal darkness was produced as an argument of an angry God. So too in the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World," meaning Man</note> disturbances and diseases arise, as well as dull and cold infirmities; namely, by the turning away of the face of **Jehovah** <note>original: "Iehouæ"</note>, in whose presence is life. Thus man dies by the withdrawal and contraction of the spirit of life within himself.

Sometimes He exercises His severity in both worlds simultaneously, both by expanding Himself and by contracting Himself. For insofar as the virtue of the Essential Name is everywhere...

### On the super-celestial origin of Life and Health.

It expands everywhere in the Sephirotic or Kabbalistic tree, yet it nonetheless retains the identity of its Monad <note>The Monad refers to the divine unity or the 'One' from which all things originate</note>; thus it is necessary that the same Essence should exercise the effects of both life and death, of both Mercy and Severity, and this through properties that are either positive or privative <note>In philosophy, 'privative' refers to the absence or removal of a quality, like cold being described as the absence of heat</note>. For example: in **Kether** <term>Kether: The 'Crown,' the first Sephirah representing the primal divine will</term>, or the radical crown of His emanation and revelation, through His decree and will, clemency and mercy are shown like a Father toward His children or creatures, insofar as it was His mind to make and create. In **Binah** <term>Binah: 'Understanding,' the third Sephirah, associated here with structure, limitation, and the feminine principle</term>, there is a cold and constrictive property which is opposed to life, inasmuch as darkness reigns within it; for darkness is produced by the condensation of what is subtle. In **Chesed** <term>Chesed: 'Mercy' or 'Loving-kindness,' the fourth Sephirah, representing the expansive flow of life</term>, clemency and the nourishment of life are given. In **Geburah** <term>Geburah: 'Severity' or 'Strength,' the fifth Sephirah, representing judgment and restraint</term>, there is severity and punishment through a fiery and destructive nature. Thus God is called a "consuming fire," and so it is in the rest, according to the number and natures of the planets, which are said to dispose and arrange all lower things according to the multiform properties of the one divine Essence—mediated by angelic messengers and emissaries, whose task it is (as the Royal Psalmist <note>Referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms</note> testifies) to immediately carry out the word and perform the pleasure of God. Whence also the Angels are the mediate instruments of God, because they receive the lights of every shining gate. Just so, it is the nature of the Stars to receive the "seeds" of those luminaries immediately from the Angels; as the winds receive from the stars, the elements from the winds, and animals, vegetables, and minerals (insofar as they are composed of elements) from the Elements.

Finally, how the one God works in both worlds simultaneously in His dual property—and then later in the tenfold property derived specifically from those two—both naturally and in His wrath, we shall declare in the *following treatise*, where, God willing, we shall speak of the primary or essential super-celestial causes of diseases.

Now truly, we shall proceed with a light leap to the second part of this treatise, in which we shall declare how the effects of the primary properties of the Monad proceed immediately from the angelic creatures themselves: and

### ANGELIC METHOD OF HEALTH.
#### CHAPTER I.

*In which it is declared that God works in this world through the mediation of Angelic creatures, both for Health and for infirmity. And how all Angels, or the whole Angelic nature, is included in that great Angel Metatron, whom the Scriptures call Wisdom.*

<margin>Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a pioneering German humanist and scholar who introduced Jewish Kabbalistic thought into the Christian intellectual world.</note></margin>
It was not an absurd assertion of those ancient Sages that **an Angel is a Power acting as a medium between God and nature: in which operations occur in things which their own nature either would not do, or would not do in such a way.** Some say these things arise from a "hidden property," and others simply "because it is of such a nature." For if we correctly observe the disposition of the Angelic nature, we will perceive that it is indeed a medium between the divine unity and the composite creature itself, in the same way we observe the number two <note>The "binary" or number 2 represents the first step away from the absolute "One" (God) toward the complexity of the "Three" (the world).</note> to be the middle between 1 and 3. Therefore, they call the Angel **alterity** <note>original: "alteritatem" — meaning "otherness" or the state of being a reflection rather than the source</note>, just as they call the divine nature itself **identity**. For this reason, they named it alterity because it is composed of two, in the manner of that pillar which preceded the Israelites, which was fused together from cloud and fire. So too does the Angel possess an **Emanation** of divine light for its internal part, but for its external part, the purest and most subtle created Spirit of the world. This serves it as an Organic body, adapted to receive the divine light according to the nature of the "luminous gate" <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for the channels through which divine energy flows.</note> emitting it. Hence it is that the sacred Text sometimes calls an Angel a **Spirit**; sometimes a **Divine Emanation**; and indeed sometimes **God** himself, in respect to the Divinity which it receives and contains within itself. For this reason, it is called by the fathers of Theology a **manifestation of hidden light**: because through the way of influence, it receives the divine light—which in itself is incomprehensible and hidden—and emits and manifests it to the Angels of the lower orders. On this account, it is called a **Mirror** capable of receiving the light of God. From this, others maintain that the more simple this spiritual substance is within an angel, the further it stands from matter, and consequently, the more the likeness or brightness of God shines back within it, more expressly and clearly—not unlike a highly polished mirror. The reverse also follows: just as the influence of divine happiness is more abundant and worthy in the purer Spirits, so it is present more sparingly and in a lowlier manner in the coarser and more opaque spirits; wherefore they are to be regarded as spirits of darkness rather than of light.

From these illuminated Spirits, therefore, bodies both higher <note>Referring to the stars and planets.</note> and lower are adorned with a greater or lesser happiness of light; and consequently, they are more or less liberated from the snares of privation and darkness. For as they receive the power of the luminous life immediately from God, so it is their role to impart it to lower things, by which those things might be refreshed by the divine life and being. This, then, is the reason that the **Cabalists** <term>Cabalists: Practitioners of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that explains the relationship between the eternal, mysterious Infinite and the mortal, finite universe.</term> maintain that there is no animal, herb, or plant, nor any mineral on earth, which does not have a Star in the firmament that strikes it with its influence and says to it:

From this, therefore, it is clear that just as in any kingdom of composite things some are found most opposite to others in nature and condition—so much so that some are more dangerous to others than toxin or poison—so it is certain that Star differs from Star, and Angel from Angel: because the properties of the divine emanation are contrary in nature and condition to other properties. From this arises the occasion of life and death, of health and diseases: and this is the reason why the nature and property of one herb is to cure the effect of that contrary: that is, it is accustomed to remove the morbid influence of the contrary effect.

We say, therefore, that whatever is handed down in the holy writings as being done by God in His creatures: that must necessarily be done through the mediation of His **Angels**: which we prove in this way: namely, because **Angel** in Greek <note>original: "Angelus" from Greek "Aggelos"</note>, **Malach** in Hebrew <note>original: "Mal'akh"</note>, and **Messenger** in Latin <note>original: "Nuntius"</note>, is a name of office and not of essence: for in essence, it is called **Spirit**. And others set him down as the Messiah, or the blessed angel of Christ filling all things: whence Christ is held to be an Angel in many places of the Holy Page. <margin>Isaiah 6, Exodus 23</margin> And his name is called (says the Prophet) the **Angel of Great Counsel**. Similarly, he is called the **Mediator** between God and man. Others take him for that Angel, *in whom Jehovah said his name was inscribed:* that is, **Wisdom** itself: wherefore they made him the prince and leader of the administering Spirits: as much in direction and protection as in the distribution of other goods to creatures: concluding from this that all other administering Spirits are included and comprehended in him (whom others have called **Michael**) as a common name for the angelic species. By these things we are made more certain: that all Angels or Spirits are of the same species: nevertheless, they are made prefects and rulers over the virtues and operations of various bodies, both of heaven and earth: according to the various reasoning of the divine will: not otherwise than we observe that the various rays of one Sun, which are not at all distinct in nature, produce various effects: namely, some dry out, others burn, others bring leafy growth to creatures: some are harmful to others, etc.

This source of the Angelic nature, therefore, is called **Metatron** and the **Active Intellect** <note>original: "intellectus agens" — a philosophical term for the power that makes knowledge possible by "illuminating" the mind</note> by **Rabbi Moshe** <note>Maimonides (Moses ben Maimon), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> and the prefect of the universe: inasmuch as by him all and singular virtues are governed and ruled, and all forms flow in daily. By these words he clearly appears to argue four points: first, that the Angels are so armed and adorned with divine power, and excel with such vigor, that nothing created is able to resist their operations; second, that they carry out the act of the divine word in heaven and on earth; third, that they are the ministers of God, created and ordained specifically to execute the divine will in the world; fourth, that they stand and are present before God, listening to his voice and word, so that they may thereafter bring his pleasure into effect. Therefore, as it is said in the divine numerations <note>A reference to the Sefirot in Kabbalah, the ten attributes or emanations of God.</note>, the first three refer to the Most Holy Persons in the Trinity: namely, **Cheter** <note>Keter</note>, or the **Crown**, to the Father; **Hochma** <note>Chokhmah</note>, or **Wisdom**, to the Son; and **Binah**, or **Prudence** <note>Usually translated as Understanding</note>, to the Holy Spirit. They then pour these lights into the **Olympic Angels** <note>Spirits that govern the spheres of the seven planets.</note> who preside over the seven Planets and are subject to them. These, through various influences—according to the different conditions of their shining channels—fill the glowing globes of the planets, so that from their fountains the elements and all things composed of elements <note>original: "elementata"</note> are copiously watered and given life at every moment. But of this, more elsewhere, at greater length.

Hence, just as these seven Angels received their radiant life immediately from G O D, so the Olympic Angels received it from them, and the Elemental Angels from the Olympic; and yet that divine light is one and the same essence, not divided at all. It is continuous from its starting point to its destination in the same way that the rays of the sun reach from the sun to the earth, with no division coming between them.

<margin>Wisdom 7.</margin>
Here, however, it must first be observed that just as the seat of divine Wisdom in this world exists as much in darkness as in light, as much on earth and in the deep as in the transparent sky: so indeed He is accustomed at times to hide Himself, and sometimes to manifest Himself; sometimes to move in the manner of an invisible wind, and sometimes to reveal Himself like a flash of lightning. In both of His properties, He has prepared for Himself fit and suitable ministers; namely, those of light and benevolence as much as those of darkness and those inclined toward privation <note>In this context, "privation" refers to the absence of good or light, often associated with judgment or the "left hand" of God.</note>: these are merely the Instruments <note>original: "Organa"</note> of the Light or of the holy spirit of Wisdom, in which He Himself acts—what, in what manner, when, and where He wills. Therefore, no one should be led by such vain superstition as to believe that all things are bestowed upon the lower realms from heaven by the Angels alone; rather, we believe those things are done by the divine Majesty itself through the Angels, even within the Angels, according to that saying of Daniel: *He does according to His will in the army of Heaven and among the inhabitants of the Earth.* But the Apostle <note>Referring to St. Paul in 1 Corinthians 8:5-6.</note> seems to explain this more clearly in this thread of discourse: *Indeed there are those who are called Gods in heaven and on earth: yet for us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things and we in Him, and one Lord Jesus Christ through whom are all things and we through Him.* By these words he seems to prove that all things are done fundamentally by Him from whom the Emanation <note>The "outflowing" of divine essence into the created world.</note> was sent forth, through which all things were created; whose infinite rays, sent forth at the will of the primal Monad <note>The "Monad" refers to God as the ultimate, indivisible Unit or One.</note>, are called messengers <note>The word "Angel" (angelos) literally means "messenger."</note>, who have been allotted various names according to the variety of effects or operations which they perform in the world. Hence various names are attributed to them by mortals based on their properties and not their essence; for the Essence of the Angels is the same and unique in the universal Wisdom, as if contained within the root of all Angels. Thus, the spirit of Wisdom was called "simple" by the Wise Man <note>Refers to King Solomon, the traditional author of the Book of Wisdom.</note>, that is, in respect to the one individual Essence; and yet in respect to its various properties, it is called "manifold": *The Spirit of wisdom (he says) is simple, manifold, etc.*

<margin>Romans 11:36. <note>The OCR says 11:32, but the text quotes 11:36.</note></margin>
Therefore we say that although God is said to work all things in all through the mediation of Angels, nevertheless the angels are not accustomed to provide this themselves, but rather the divine rays emanating from the seven luminous gates, or the source of Wisdom; which rays can by no means be divided or separated from the divine Essence: and for that reason the Apostle most excellently concludes that *from Him, through Him, and in Him are all things. To Him be honor and glory forever and ever.*

### C H A P T E R III.

->Who are those Angels who are accustomed to direct the influences of Life and Health from their celestial sources into the lower regions?<-

The Cabalists <note>Scholars of Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition.</note> have frequently called the general Angel of life and preservation Metatron <note>original: "Mitattron"</note>, and the Platonists have made him the Soul of the World <note>original: "Animam mundi", the vital force that permeates all nature.</note>; whom they have established as the author of life and souls: but the Holy Page <note>A common term for the Bible.</note> calls him the "Word sent forth," in whom was life: indeed, the Sacred Writings have recognized that he was the spiritual Christ, who is life itself; and the Savior filling all things, whom they also called the Mystic *Hochmah* or Wisdom; in whose right hand is length of days, and in her left, riches, as she is the Treasury of the kingdom of heaven, which being sought out, all other goods will be added. Truly, the Angels who are subject to his commands by their own healing property are those who proceed from the luminous gate of *Chesed* <note>Hebrew for "Mercy."</note>, and that of *Tiphereth* <note>Hebrew for "Beauty."</note>, and that of *Netzeth* <note>Usually spelled "Netzach," meaning "Victory" or "Endurance."</note>, and that of...

# On the Super-celestial Origin of Life and Health.

**Hod** <note>original: "Hod"; the eighth Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing "Splendor" or "Glory." It is often associated with the planet Mercury and the Archangel Raphael.</note>; they receive the influxes of life and health, and they store them in the sanctuary of the planets Jupiter, the Sun, and Venus, from which they gradually rain them down into the lower realms.

The ancient Sages say that the Archangel **Zadkiel**—one of those seven who stand before the face of God—receives his influences from the bright gate of **Cheter** <note>original: "Cheter" or Keter; the "Crown," the highest Sephirah, representing the divine will or the infinite light of God.</note>, and pours them into that orbicular vessel of heaven which they call the planet of **Jupiter**. From this, it follows that this Jovial planet sends down influences to the lower regions which are always benevolent toward the life of creatures. For just as the nature of life and a healthy temperament is hot and moist, so indeed this kind of influence fosters the **innate heat** and **radical moisture** <term>radical moisture: a vital fluid in medieval medicine believed to be the fuel of life, preserved by "innate heat."</term>, maintaining them in a moderate sweetness. Therefore, such influences are accustomed to produce the effects of mercy and life.

Similarly, that one of the seven whom they call **Michael**, who is said to preside over the celestial **Sun**, receives bright influences from the most beautiful emanation, **Tiphereth** <note>original: "Tiphereth"; the sixth Sephirah, meaning "Beauty." It sits at the center of the Tree of Life and is traditionally linked to the Sun and the balance of the universe.</note>, and pours them into the Solar vessel, from which they are later rained down into the lower realms. Through these, life, generation, and multiplication are observed to flourish on the lands and in the waters.

Likewise, the bright influences emitted from the gate of **Netzeth** <note>original: "Netzeth" or Netzach; the seventh Sephirah, meaning "Victory" or "Endurance," associated with the planet Venus.</note> are received by the Archangel **Hanael**, one of those seven. They are introduced by him into the globe of **Venus**, from which they are then poured downward for the benefit of creatures. For this reason, Venus is called the "Lesser Fortune" by astrologers, as will be discussed more extensively below.

Finally, the reception and guidance of the influences distilling from the gate of **Hod** are attributed to the Archangel **Raphael**, who is accustomed to direct them into the **Mercurial** body of Heaven. From there, in a benevolent manner—unless hindered by malevolent forces—they are sent forth into the elemental region.

Here it must be noted that these principal Angels are said to have as many Angels of their own nature and condition subject to them as there are rays or bright acts emitted by them; all of these are nonetheless no less continuous with their Archangelic source than the rays of the Sun are with the Sun. Thus God, expanding Himself into the Word through the Holy Spirit, creates Unity in Trinity and Trinity in Unity, which Trinity again pours its power in a sevenfold property into the Machine of the World. It is as if **Universal Wisdom** were building her house upon seven columns: these seven bright columns are those seven Archangels who immediately govern the World and the ages of the World through the seven Planets. These planets are said to have dominion over all lower things in the World by divine command, just as the Archangels and intellectual Spirits have dominion over the lower spirits.

<margin>Revelation 1.</margin>
And this seems to be best explained in the Revelation <note>The biblical Book of Revelation (the Apocalypse).</note> in these words: *He who said, I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, was like the son of man, whose eyes were like a flame of fire and his feet like the purest molten brass glowing in a furnace. His belt was golden, and in his right hand he held seven stars, and his face shone like the Sun; his voice was like the murmur of many waters, etc.* In this speech, he seems to denote that great Angel, called **Wisdom**, who placed his Tabernacle in the Sun, which is why he said his appearance was very much like the sun. And just as the Sun has the other planets subject to it—inasmuch as they have their light and life from the Sun—so indeed this spiritual Sun, this Universal Angel, has under him the seven Angels presiding over the said Planets. Of these, John says: *I saw seven Angels standing before God, and to them were given seven trumpets, etc.* <margin>Revelation 8.</margin> Indeed, this is the Prince of all Angels and the head of salvation, whose rays are those seven Archangels who stand before him, pouring out life, form, and being to the lower things. These seven, by multiplying their received rays, produce infinite angels of a lower order, who in effect, however, are only seven. For thus all the angels of Saturn are called by the common name "Saturnine," those of Jupiter "Jovial," those of Mars "Martial," and so on for the rest. Thus also, although Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, etc., are said to stand before God, there is nevertheless no impediment to their being present both on earth and in the heavens, and everywhere according to the divine will.
