### Volume I. Treatise 1. Section I. Part II. Book 1.

...are said to exist to fulfill one whole; and this is not done without consideration. For all subject Angels are, as it were, continuous rays of the same sevenfold angelic root, which in turn is joined to the luminous source in such close kinship that these seven are sometimes called Angels, and sometimes God or Gods. From this it is clear that all Angels are, as it were, branches of a single Trunk or Root, and consequently the lower are rendered obedient to the higher in all things, and matching in nature: so that the good Angels act and work according to their capacity, and are accustomed to act according to the will of their radical light <note>The "radical light" refers to the primary divine source from which the angels emanate, similar to the "root" of a tree.</note>, and are known to hold dominion over the wicked Angels by turns. By the same reasoning, the Angels of severity exercise their unmerciful powers at such times when—by the will of their luminous root—they are permitted to prevail in power and dominion over the good Angels. For example, regarding the mercy of God (who is that radical Light of all lights), it is said: <margin>Psalm 91</margin> *“Do not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague or darkness that stalks in the night, nor the destruction that wastes at noon, nor the noonday Demon. For no plague shall come near your tent: for he will command his Angels concerning you, and he will preserve you in all your ways, etc.”*

By these words, it is manifest that by such a beneficial influx, the good Angels, by divine will, sometimes have the command to repress the assaults of malignant Spirits. Similarly, it is said of that Angel who presides over the safety of creatures: <margin>Rev. 7</margin> *“And I saw another Angel ascending from the East, who had the seal of the living God, and he cried out to the four Angels who were told to harm the earth and the sea, saying: Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have signed the servants of God on their foreheads, etc.”* By this thread of discourse, the Revelator <note>Referring to John the Apostle, author of the Book of Revelation.</note> seems to argue that there is a certain supreme Angel who holds dominion over both the evil and the good Angels, to whom it is given sometimes to send forth the power of this one or that one, and sometimes to suppress it according to his will. But indeed, in the opposite sense it is said: <margin>Job 2:7</margin> *“Satan struck Job with a most grievous ulcer from the soles of his feet even to the top of his head.”* And elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 78:47, Isaiah 29</margin> *“He sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: anger, and tribulation, and evil Angels, etc.”* So a wicked Spirit of Jehovah is said to have possessed Saul. And elsewhere: *“Be stunned with amazement, fluctuate, and stagger, for the Lord has mixed for you a Spirit of deep sleep, etc.”*

Therefore, just as that great Angel of salvation is **Michael**, or (as the Kabbalists prefer) **Metatron** <note>original: "Mitattron"; a high-ranking angel in Jewish mystical tradition, often regarded as the celestial scribe or the "lesser YHWH."</note> and Wisdom itself: an Angel (I say) who saves and does not destroy; so indeed the prince and presiding officer of the harming and destroying Angels is called in Hebrew **Abaddon**, and in Greek **Apollyon** <note>Both names mean "The Destroyer."</note>—that is, "the one who destroys"—as John testifies.

To the care of the thrice-greatest **Michael** belongs the guardianship of the soul, life, and health: which is the subject of this treatise of ours.

To the hostile and litigious disposition of **Apollyon** belongs the triumph of diseases, infirmities, and death; these will be treated in the following Treatise, in which the triumph of Diseases and that final triumph—in which the nature of the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: "the little world," referring to the human being as a reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</term> is dealt with in a counter-natural way, concerning the Trophy of Death—shall be clearly discussed (God willing).

Finally, I shall not say more in this place regarding the origins of the Angels; for regarding their birth and their twofold kingdom (one of which is heavenly, belonging to those of light; the other Infernal and earthly, belonging to the light-shunning and dark ones), I shall speak in the following Treatise. There, I shall (God granting) discuss the causes of diseases, both material and efficient, more clearly and deeply. But now, I shall turn the thread of my discourse to the **Olympic Angels** <note>The "Olympic Spirits" are seven planetary spirits described in Renaissance grimoires, such as the *Arbatel de Magia Veterum*, who govern the spheres of the world.</note>, so that you may see and perceive, as if with the eyes of a Lynx, how the Angels of the lower orders receive divine influxes from the Higher ones.

It was the opinion of all the Platonists that every star in the sky enjoys its own Angelic Presiding officer; indeed, the Peripatetics <note>The followers of Aristotle, known for walking while teaching.</note> themselves are observed to have fallen into this same sentiment: namely, those who attribute to each Heaven, besides its own essential form, an Intelligence which is the mover of its sphere. ### *That the Stars are known to be subject to Angels of the second Order, no differently than they themselves are subject to the Archangels of the first order: What the Cabalists have thought on this matter.*

It was the opinion of all the **Platonists** <note>Followers of Plato's philosophy, who believed in a world of ideal forms and spiritual intermediaries</note> that every star of heaven enjoys its own Angelic Governor. Indeed, even the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle, known for "walking about" while teaching</note> are observed to have arrived at this same conclusion. <margin>Pimander, 3.</margin>
> The stars were numbered according to those who inhabit them, the Gods; the broader circuit, in its course, the airy circle breathing together, was carried by the divine spirit: Each of the Gods, from internal virtue, fulfilled the work assigned to him, etc.

He acts by means of those Angelic organs, which are led here and there in their duties to perfect divine commands in the world; they are led by that divine spirit which exists within them in the form of divine light. For (as has been declared clearly enough by us elsewhere) Angels are like highly polished mirrors receiving the emanation and splendor of divine light either immediately—namely those especially who stand closest to the face of **Jehovah**—or mediately—namely those of the lower orders, who receive their light and action by various influx from the superiors to whom they are subject, according to their dignity.

...one and the same [light] poured into divine vessels by various reflections; nevertheless, in this progression we perceive that there are various degrees of illumination in the aforementioned mirrors. For the light from the Sun, when concentrated in the first mirror, is of a nobler and more dignified aspect than that in the second: and so it is proportionally in the rest. Indeed, the matter is the same in the order of the Angels, of whom those who stand before the face of Jehovah are more dignified in order and light than those who are placed beneath them. But truly, insofar as all these Angels receive their powers and virtues—or rather their acts—from Eternal Wisdom or divine emanation (that is, from the **Word**), it will be safer to call all these virtues "divine acts" rather than to ascribe their effects to the Angelic Organs in that manner. Hence it is that David calls the Angels themselves <margin>Psalm 103:21</margin> *Powers of God*, speaking in these words: *Bless the Lord, all you his Angels, you Powers of God: you ministers of his, who do his will, etc.* If, therefore, they are the virtues of **GOD**, then it follows that **GOD** is in them essentially; and he is to them as a Soul is to a body, whence it happens that in several places of the sacred scriptures, sometimes God (with respect to their internal nature) and sometimes Angels are mentioned.

Therefore, just as **GOD** in his most simple Nature is called *Identity* <note>original: "Identitas"; referring to the absolute oneness and unchanging nature of God</note> by the wise; so indeed the Angel, because of that twofold nature, is called *Alterity* <note>original: "Alteritas"; referring to a state of being "other" or divided, as Angels are composed of both spirit and light</note>; namely, composed of the purest spirit as a body, and divine light as a soul. For this reason, that eternal Wisdom (<margin>Wisdom 7</margin> *which is the breath of the power of **GOD**, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty God, and the brightness of eternal light; and the spotless mirror of **GOD'S** Majesty and the image of his goodness*) has mostly been sent out from its luminous source into the mundane spirit. With respect to its mixing <margin>Ecclesiasticus 1</margin> with that universal spirit, it is called the *first of all creatures*, and that great angel who is the Prince of all other Angels; for in him is the force and power of all Angels. These subordinate Angels are therefore called "Gods" in heaven and on earth for no other reason than that they participate in that divine Unity, which is God himself. Thus, for this reason, the World is called by Hermes the <margin>Pimander 1. 2 Peter 3.</margin> *second God*, yet not God absolutely, but insofar as it participates in the divine form and essence according to this sense explained elsewhere. *The Word* (he says) *stood by the moist nature.* And St. Peter says: *The heavens were of old and the Earth was formed out of water and through water by the Word of God.* Hence it was that the Cabalists <note>Jewish mystics; here the author refers to their traditional naming of the highest archangel</note> called this universal spirit of God *Mitattron* <note>Metatron; often identified in mystical literature as the highest angel or the "Prince of the Countenance"</note>; as if one were to say, the "Gift of God," for of all gifts that was the greatest, by means of which the World and all creatures in it were made into something from nothing, and were brought back from the abyss of deformity into the noblest likenesses of most beautiful creatures. Hence also it was that Orpheus and the Pythagoreans <note>Ancient Greek philosophers and mystics who believed in the mathematical and spiritual harmony of the universe</note> held the opinion that *all things are full of Gods*; all of whom they nevertheless referred back to the one Jove: according to that saying of the Wise Man: *The incorruptible spirit is in every thing;* and yet this Spirit, however much it is expanded into a multitude, is one and simple. The Pythagoreans called these spirits (the rays of the one Universal spirit) *Gods*, insofar as they are truly not to be divided from the Divinity; and again they are called Angels both in Heaven and on Earth, insofar as they are rays of that great Angel, who is truly that internal Soul of the World <note>original: "Anima Mundi"; the spiritual essence that permeates and animates the entire universe</note> of the Platonists, which gives life and inspiration and all things to the Creatures, as is more clearly declared in our Discourse on the Soul of the World.

These things being established, it must be observed that although the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle</note> and Platonists attribute Intelligences to the stars and especially to the Planets, which Hermes calls **GODS**, nevertheless in truth, these are none other than sevenfold influences sent out from the single luminous well of all Wisdom in various ways and manners; to which luminous source all the actions of the world are primarily to be attributed. Therefore, the virtue which rains down from that Orb into lower things is not to be ascribed to the Angelic Governor of Saturn with his legions, but to the source of all Goodness, from which such influences first arise; namely, to divine Wisdom, which is the [Prince] of Angels...

### Volume I. Treatise I. Section I. Part II. Book II.

...to fill all things, and to work all in all: So this Angel is the head and Prince of all lower Angels and Powers in this world.

The first ray emitted from him is **Jophiel**, who receives his rays from the gate of **Wisdom** <note>original: "Hochma"</note>. This Angel, by the etymology of his name, signifies beauty, as one who is filled with the gifts of life. And the reason for this is that he is the receiver of the influences sent from the source of light through the gate of Wisdom, and he is the conductor of these influences into the eighth sphere <note>The sphere of the Fixed Stars</note>. This is why that sphere is filled with an infinite multitude of bright stars and adorned with that celestial belt or zone which they call the **Zodiac**; it is as if it were a living creature, since it is filled with living images.

The third <note>The author likely considers the "Universal Angel/Wisdom" as the first/second source, or follows the Sephirot numbering where Binah is third</note> ray or Virtue of the divine source is received by that Angel **Kaffiel** <note>original: "קפציאל" (Cassiel)</note>, that is, the Spirit of great wrath; because he rains the influences of **God** <note>original: "Elohim"</note> sent through the gate of **Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"</note> into the globe of Saturn, he is said to be the ruler of that same planet.

The fourth ray, sent through the name of God **El**, is received by **Zadkiel** <note>original: "צדקיאל"</note>, which means the Spirit of Justice (who signifies the gift of God), and is conducted into the sphere and globe of Jupiter.

From the fifth name of God, namely **Elohim Gibbor** <note>The Almighty God</note>, through the bright gate of **Severity** <note>original: "Geburah"</note> or punishment, a fifth ray is poured out into the Angel **Hamael**, that is, the Spirit of subsistence (which brings with it a sense of awe), by whom it is received into the globe of Mars.

From the sixth name, namely **Eloah**, through the bright gate called **Beauty** <note>original: "Tiphereth," also translated as Grace</note>, the sixth ray is rained into that mighty Angel **Michael**, whose name means **Who is like God?** <note>original: "Quis tanquam Deus?"</note>, who pours it into the orb of the Sun.

From the seventh name, namely **Jehovah Sabaoth** <note>The Lord of Hosts</note>, through the gate of **Victory** <note>original: "Netzeth" or Netzach</note> or Triumph, the seventh ray is poured into the Angel **Haniel** <note>original: "Hanacelem"</note>, that is, the Spirit of riches and sufficiency, by whom it is directed into the globe of **Venus**.

From the eighth, namely **Elohim Sabaoth**, through the gate or numeration of **Splendor** <note>original: "Hod"</note> or praise, the eighth influence descends into the Angel **Raphael**, that is, the Spirit of medicine, by whom it is rained into the sphere or orb of Mercury.

From the ninth, namely **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai"</note>, through the gate of **Foundation** <note>original: "Iesed" or Yesod</note> or Redemption, the ninth ray descends into the Angel **Gabriel**, that is, the Spirit of power and virtue, by whom it is poured into the globe of the Moon.

Finally, from the name **Adonai** <note>Lord</note>, the ray is poured into the "Heroes" <note>The Ishim or "Souls of the Just"</note>, and from them into the Elemental region; this last ray passes through the gate of the **Kingdom** <note>original: "Malchut"</note>.

By these things, therefore, we see how, according to the intention of the Cabalists, all the angelic rays—like the various Virtues of a single Essence—are derived from the unique source of **Divine Wisdom**. They are directed first to the fixed stars, and then afterwards to the wandering stars <note>The planets</note> through the mediation of the aforementioned angelic spirits. All these spirits, according to the variety of the divine property, differ among themselves in office and quality, and are accustomed to produce various effects in the said celestial bodies.

In this matter, it must especially be observed that every one of these bright influences is subdivided into infinite other rays, which are also said to possess the virtues and actions of Angels, and are called by the name of **Olympic** spirits or Intelligences. Thus, it is established that every one of these globes is filled with spirits of this kind, whose duty it is to care for various things according to the condition of their nature here in the Elements, and especially on the land and in the sea. So much so, that there is nothing to be found in the entire earth or sea that does not look toward a particular Angel in Heaven. This also seems to be what the Pythagoreans intended when they said: **All things are full of gods.** And the Wise Man <note>Solomon</note>, by saying: **that an incorruptible spirit was in every thing.** And all the Cabalists affirm with unanimous consent: **that all lower things are representative of higher things; and as it is below, so it is acted upon from above.** But Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note> seems to confess this in express words, speaking thus: **Whosoever of the gods who inhabit the stars has fulfilled the work assigned to him by internal virtue...**

## CHAPTER II.

->*How these influences, both healthful and destructive, produce their effects by reason of the variety of their properties.*<-

FROM these things, therefore, which are expressed above, it is certain that all lower actions and forms proceed from and are continuous with that bright and eternal fountain: which in itself is the unique, simple, and most holy Origin of all things: from which, in which, and through which, all things were created and made. This deep and also exalted well of Goodness, although it is in itself—that is, in its paternal root—fixed, stable, and permanent: nevertheless, nothing in this world is faster in its emission and emanation, that is, in its rays, and more subtle in its motion. And although this holy Wisdom in its nature is unique and simple, yet in respect to the variety and multiplicity of its rays, it is said to be manifold, and in its property, varied: not otherwise than we perceive the same artificial fire <note>Man-made fire</note>, or rather the solar fire (which also derived its action from that fountain), to be one and the same in its nature: and yet it has in itself the property either of preserving and nourishing with its benevolent heat, or of destroying, burning, and drying out, in a contrary property.

In a similar respect, the Mind <term>Mens<gloss>The higher, intellectual part of the human soul</gloss></term>, or the intellectual soul of man, is unique and simple, and yet, sometimes it acts malevolently with its negative and privative property: just as on the other side, in its positive and affable disposition, it is seen to act benevolently and graciously. Thus also the human mind may harm another by its former property, either by denying and not responding at all to the petition of one who asks: or by the emission of its contracted rays, with violence toward the destruction or damage of the seeker, as may be seen in a man driven by sudden anger. Is not the divine Identity <note>The "Sameness" or "Oneness" of God</note>, from which that human Identity proceeds, held in exactly the same way? Thus also God causes men to wander like drunkards and grope as if in darkness when the Light fails. <margin>2 Corinthians 4.</margin> And elsewhere: *The God of this world blinds the minds of unbelievers, so that the light of the Gospel of the Glory of Christ does not shine upon them.* <margin>Isaiah 8.</margin> And elsewhere: *Behold, trouble and darkness, dissolution and anguish, and a gloom following the wicked from which he cannot fly.* But indeed, where he totally receives back his Spirit, there <margin>Acts 5.</margin> it is necessary that the creature expire, and be reduced to its dust. ...cold and dry and congealing, which is why Saturn is judged by astrologers to be the **Greater Misfortune** <note>original: *Infortunio maiori*; known in astrology as the "Greater Malefic," a planet associated with hardship or limitation</note>. From this it is clear that through this type of property, God contracts His nature within Himself. By this contraction of Himself, He constricts, binds, and thickens the creature, rendering it dark. Consequently, by the contraction of Himself within Himself, He leaves behind darkness in the whole world, or in part, or in some specific creature. Therefore, it is certain that this property is, on His part, negative, and consequently contrary to the "children of light"—that is, those who possess life.

In the severe property of the second Order, God turns Himself: contracting His own bright nature into a consuming fire. In this property, He acts by burning and consuming, just as in the previous property He acts by mortifying and congealing with cold. Hence He is called a *Consuming Fire*, as was declared before. The Angel who receives this type of influence is **Samael**, who leads these forces into the sphere of Mars, which is filled with fiery spirits <note>original: *Dæmonibus*; in this context, the author refers to elemental or spiritual entities, not necessarily "demons" in the modern evil sense</note> who are subject to Samael’s command. For this reason, this planet is said by astrologers to be fiery, hot, and dry, and quite hostile to living creatures. For just as the influences of Saturn extinguish the "innate heat" <note>The vital warmth believed to be the source of life in the body</note> with their cold, so do those of Mars absorb the **radical moisture** <note>The essential fluid or "fuel" of life in medieval medicine</note> with their heat and dryness. Hence this planet is called the **Lesser Misfortune** <note>original: *Infortunium minus*; the "Lesser Malefic"</note>.

Regarding the properties of clemency and mercy, it must be understood that the first of these flows from His name **EL**, which in the Holy Scriptures is always the path of mercy, compassion, and beneficence. For example, when Moses wished to pray for the health of Miriam, he used this prayer: *El na rapha na la*, which is: *El, God of grace: rapha, heal: na, I pray: la, her.* <note>Numbers 12:13</note> Therefore, the "gate" through which this type of outpouring passes is called **Chesed** <note>Hebrew for "Kindness" or "Mercy"; one of the ten Sephirot or divine emanations</note>, meaning clemency. The Archangel who receives this influx is **Zadkiel**, who conducts them into the globe of Jupiter. This planet is by nature temperately hot and moist, and consequently favorable to life and health, insofar as it is the supporter of the radical heat and moisture. Thus, this planet is called the **Greater Fortune** <note>original: *Fortunium maius*; the "Greater Benefic"</note> by astrologers. Therefore, this entire Jovial sphere is inhabited by spirits benevolent toward human nature, who recognize Zadkiel as their leader.

Furthermore, the name **Jehovah Sabaoth** <note>Lord of Hosts</note> produces or sends forth benevolent and peaceful outpourings through the gate of **Metzeth** <note>Likely a variation of *Netzach*, meaning Victory or Triumph</note>, which signifies Triumph. For when creation was complete, Jehovah triumphed and rested on the seventh day, remaining as if in total peace and quiet.

The Archangel **Hanael** receives these bright influences and with them has enriched the world of Venus, which is filled with all sweetness, joy, and cheerfulness. Therefore, that sphere is inhabited on all sides by Venereal spirits.

<margin>Exodus 34.</margin>
Finally, as for the properties that tend partly toward clemency and partly toward severity—such as those that descend through the gates of **Yesod** <note>Foundation or Redemption</note> and **Tiphereth** <note>Beauty or Glory</note>—all these refer to Jehovah Himself, or the Eternal Wisdom, which alone encompasses the "Sephirotic Trunk" <note>The central column of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, balancing Mercy and Severity</note> of the Kabbalists. The Holy Scriptures teach us everywhere that this name of God tends toward both mercy and clemency. Hence it says:
> *Jehovah, the strong, merciful, and gracious, slow to anger and abundant in mercy and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, taking away iniquity and sin, yet visiting the iniquity of the Fathers upon the children's children, unto the third and fourth generation, etc.*
Furthermore, just as His anger is sometimes kindled, so He most often shows His mercy and clemency to mortals according to His good pleasure.

For this reason, Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a pioneering German humanist and scholar of Hebrew and the Kabbalah who argued that Christian theology could be deepened through Jewish mystical traditions.</note> says:

> *My name is in him*, etc. <note>Exodus 23:21. The author is highlighting that the Angel possesses no power of its own, but carries the "Name" or essence of God.</note>

### CHAPTER II.

->In which it is proven that the elements themselves arise from the winds, and not the winds from the elements. Likewise, it treats the four Great Angels who preside over the corners of heaven: and the great Seal of life; and its Guardian.<-

In Section 1, Portion 4, Part 1, Book 2, Chapters 4 and 5 of our *Cosmic Meteorology* <note>original: "Meteorologia nostra Cosmica"</note>: the nature of the air was most clearly explained by us. Now we call the Air the elemental Spirit of heaven: which extends from the Earth and Water up to the concave surface of the Moon. Which indeed does not differ in its substance from the Spirit whether Ethereal or Empyrean <term>Empyrean: The highest, most refined part of the heavens, associated with pure fire and divine light.</term>: except that, due to the lack of formal light, it is perceived to be thicker than those: for it must be understood that both the Heavens and the Earth were first existing out of water and through water by the word of God, as St. Peter <note>original: "D. Petrus"</note> testifies. Wherefore it follows that the imperceptible Spirit of the world is a most subtle Water; and the mediocre visible Spirit is either vapor, a cloud, or water; and that the earth is the thicker part of Water.

Hence it can be hidden from no one that just as simple Water is capable of any impression—namely, it has within itself the power of heating, cooling, freezing, or dissolving—so indeed the air, in the manner of the celestial Mercury <note>original: "Mercurij cœlestis"</note> (who changes his quality and nature according to the disposition of the Planet with which he is joined in aspect), the air (I say) is accustomed to change its nature by reason of the wind, which is observed to blow from some corner of the world. For example: When the North Wind <note>original: "Borea"</note> blows, the air takes on an earthy disposition, namely cold and dry; whence it is seen to be constricted into snows, hailstones, frost, and rime. But when the South Wind <note>original: "Austro"</note>, the South-East Wind <note>original: "Euro-Austro"</note>, and the South-West Wind <note>original: "Austro-Africo"</note> blow, the frozen air becomes liquid, and takes on a moist nature mixed with heat at the same time: whence it is truly reduced to the nature of that portion of moisture in the highest Sphere (which is called the element of air). But if the East Wind <note>original: "Subsolanus"</note>, or the South-East Wind <note>original: "Eurus"</note>, or the North-East Wind <note>original: "Cæcias"</note> blows, it is reduced to a burning and dry condition; hence, that Spirit is exceedingly hot and dry, and in such a nature it withers and consumes fruits and herbs. Finally, if the West Wind <note>original: "Fauonius"</note>, or the North-West Wind <note>original: "Corus"</note>, or the South-West Wind <note>original: "Africus"</note> blows, it reduces the air to a cold and humid nature, either in a lower or more relaxed degree according to the wind that blows; wherefore, in that state, it can be considered as the element of Water. And this is the reason that the air is not ineptly called the Mercury of the Philosophers <term>Mercury of the Philosophers: An alchemical term for a primary, adaptable substance that can take on any quality; here Fludd uses it to describe how air changes based on the wind.</term>: since it changes its nature and condition according to the nature of the Wind observed to blow. Since this is indeed the case, it follows that the Winds are the parents of the elements, and not the elements of the Winds.

From these premises, therefore, we conclude: that the authors and acts of the Winds are the Angels; the God of the Angels, or his Wisdom, is the author of the Angels; and the Winds are the authors of the elements. Which indeed we proceed to prove in this manner: and we shall begin from the North.

Raphael is likewise of the side of clemency. Then Gabriel, in the power of Judgment and severity, is set over the Northern wind during the middle of the night and two measures of the world. These species are then said to exercise and impress their effects upon the lower world when those winds blow under whose governors they are subject.

But just as the leadership of the entire air is ascribed to the Prince of Darkness: so indeed he has his own demons, or Angelic Spirits, whose duty it is—according to the malice of their prince—to afflict the earth, the sea, and its creatures with evil. And yet, their malice is nonetheless restrained by the Archangels, those Standard-bearers of God, who have supreme power over the four regions or hinges of heaven, as well as the malice of their own Prince: as may be perceived from these words of the Revealer <note>The author of the Book of Revelation, St. John.</note>. <margin>Rev. 7.</margin> I saw (he says) four Angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the winds of the earth, that they should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree. And I saw another Angel ascending from the rising of the Sun, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four Angels of the earth, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea: saying, hurt not the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads, etc. In which discourse there are very many things, and as I think, worthy of observation.

First, namely, that there is a certain Imperial Spirit, benevolent and good by nature, who has power over malignant and harmful spirits. Second, that he ascends from the East. Then, that he has the great Sign or Seal of the living God, with which he is accustomed to seal the servants of God on their foreheads. And in the last place, that the Angels who preside over the corners of the earth are harmful and malevolent, even though their rage is suppressed by the goodness and dominion of that great Angel.

When these things are rightly considered, it appears that this is the Imperial Spirit; because the Princes of the air offered obedience to him, who was also that *strong Angel* described in the Apocalypse.

### On the Super-celestial Origin of Life and Health. ###

->...<- whose face was like the Sun; in this he is seen to be confirmed, since that great Michael the Angel is the prince of the Sun, who has his strength in the Light of the East—I speak of the Eternal Wisdom, which made the Sun its dwelling place. This is even more so because he himself is said to have fought with the ancient Serpent for the salvation of souls, and with spiritual weapons defeated Lucifer and his angels, rendering them obedient. Hence, therefore, it is that the Sun is the favorer of life, the author of multiplication, and consequently, the adversary of Saturnian destruction and loss. <note>In Renaissance thought, Saturn was associated with decay, melancholy, and contraction, while the Sun represented life and growth.</note>

<margin>Daniel 7.</margin>
As for the Mystery of the Seal, by which the Elect are said to be marked on their foreheads by the great Angel: I shall endeavor to teach you in this place what that great Seal of Heaven is, which that Angelic Chancellor of the heavenly Kingdom carries with him for the salvation of the Elect, and of those whom it has pleased God to save.

The Hebrew Doctors (among whom Eliezer Hatzlir is named) say that *Emeth* <note>Hebrew: אמת, meaning "Truth"</note> is the Seal of God. This word *Emeth* signifies "The Word" in Hebrew, or "Truth" in Latin. It is the Peace of the Lord, and consequently, through its mediation, the Rest and Salvation of the creature is sealed, granted as if by a firm obligation. Thus, he who has the sign of this great and strong Seal within himself cannot fear the attacks of wicked spirits. For wherever the impression of this spiritual Seal is found, the destroyer understands that the Peace of the Eternal Emperor is there.

Furthermore, as this is the great Seal of the heavenly and spiritual kingdom, it must necessarily be purely formal, or spiritual. Consequently, its impression or "Character" is of such a kind—namely, invisible and not at all to be perceived by mortal eyes.

The place where this Character is usually made, according to the meager capacity of men, is said to be on the forehead, as if on the frontispiece of the entire human structure, and a place more open to the eyes. Therefore, its Character is said to be the *Tau* <note>The Hebrew letter ת (Tav/Tau), which in ancient scripts resembled a cross</note>, insofar as it comprehends all other holy characters, which include and signify all things within themselves. It is as if one were to say: "Alpha and Omega," or "Aleph and Tau" <note>The first and last letters of the Greek and Hebrew alphabets, signifying the beginning and the end</note>. For *Emeth* <note>אמת</note> begins with *Aleph* <note>א</note> and ends with *Tau* <note>ת</note>, and the *Mem* <note>מ</note> in the middle denotes, according to the intention of the Cabalists, the universal waters, which are measured, animated, and filled by the Alpha and Omega, or the Aleph and Tau.

<margin>Revelation 7.</margin>
Wherefore, this word or Seal comprehends within itself the entire power of that great Angel, who in the Apocalypse is called Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End, for it proves (as has been said) Truth and Peace. Whence, without a doubt, this was that great Angel who, ascending from the rising of the Sun and having the sign or seal of the living God, cried with a loud voice to the four Angels standing over the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth so they would not blow—to whom it was given to harm the earth: "Do not harm the earth or the sea until we mark the servants of our God on their foreheads," etc. Concerning which also

<margin>Ezekiel 9.</margin>
<margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Cabala*.</margin>
the Prophet says: *And the glory of God, which was taken up from the Cherub, called to that man clothed in linen garments and said to him: Pass through the middle of the city and mark the sign Tau upon the foreheads of the men who groan and grieve over all the abominations that are in the midst of it. And he said to those who came by way of the upper gate which faces the North, each holding a weapon of destruction in his hand: Pass through the city following him and strike. Let your eye not spare, nor have mercy; kill the old man, the youth and the Virgin, the little ones and the women; but do not kill anyone in whom you see the Tau, etc.* In a typical way, the liberation of the Israelites from the destroyer is also prefigured in this manner, on that night in which every firstborn of the Egyptians was slain—namely, by the symbolic *Tau*, which the Israelites marked with blood upon the doorposts of their houses.

Finally, from the aforementioned testimony of the Prophet, we have it confirmed first of all that *Tau* is the character of all fullness. That great Angel of Salvation, most full of the power of Wisdom, is accustomed to imprint this character upon those whom it is God's will to preserve during a time of contagion. And then, second, we see that the harmful angels, called the *Bene Elohim* <note>Hebrew: "Sons of God," here interpreted as agents of judgment</note> (according to the opinion of the Rabbis), are most frequent in the Northern plague-zone of the world. These can achieve nothing against those whom that most powerful Angel, most affluent in mercy, has signed or noted with the most powerful and precious seal of the kingdom of heaven.

But since we shall explain more about these harmful spirits and their mournful effects in the following volume, we shall leave them out in this place; and we shall treat briefly of the powerful angels governing the four corners of the heaven, as well as the spirits subject to them.

<margin>Daniel 7.</margin>

But this is even better confirmed in another place: *Behold, four chariots coming out from the midst of two mountains, and the mountains were of bronze. The chariot in which the black horses were, went out into the land of the North; the white went out after them; and the dappled went out into the land of the South; but those which were the most robust went out and sought to go and run through all the earth.*

...ra, etc. By which it is clearly indicated through the horses <note>referring to the vision of the four chariots in Zechariah 6 or the Four Horsemen</note> that such Angels with their troops go forth from their regions to execute the divine will; and also by their color the Prophet argues their natures. I say "to execute the divine will," whether benevolent or malevolent; according to that passage in Baruch: <margin>Baruch 6:60</margin> *The wind performs the will of God.* Furthermore, David speaks thus: *Stormy spirits, who perform the word of God.* And elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 148</margin> *Who makes your Angels into winds.* <note>original: "Qui facis Angelos tuos, ventos."</note> And elsewhere: *Angels of God, most mighty in strength, performing his word, his ministers fulfilling his pleasure, etc.*

By these things, therefore, we are taught that there are four Angels who are ruled and governed in their office according to the will of Eternal Wisdom. Her fourfold properties, which encompass the forms of the four Elements within themselves, are assigned to those four Archangels—or great Princes—who always stand before the face of Jehovah. It is their task to send out the spirits of the aforementioned Angels into the evils of the sublunary world <note>The "sublunary world" refers to the Earthly realm below the sphere of the Moon, subject to change and decay.</note>, or to restrain them so they do not harm the earth, the sea, or those who dwell in them. And every cardinal blast of any Angel is eagerly awaited, received, and animated by its power by the spirits or legions inhabiting the Sphere of that Element which matches the condition of that cardinal wind; and thus its dominion is felt in the air during that season. For example: when the **Eastern Angel** blows, who rules and breathes from the Eastern corner, the fiery spirits are accustomed to exult and be animated, and to run through the whole earth in their vigor, inflaming the air and transforming it into a fiery condition; hence the East Wind <note>original: "Eurus"</note> dries things out and burns vehemently. Moreover, the Leader of these fiery Legions is **Samael**; it is his role to rule the region of fire, inasmuch as he rains down those fiery influences from *Mars* which he received from the Sephirotic gate of *Geburah* <note>The Sephirah of "Strength" or "Severity" in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.</note>, over which presides the Name of God, *Elohim Gibbor* <note>Hebrew: "God of Might."</note>. This leader, however, is commanded by the Archangel **Michael**, and renders himself obedient to him.

And when **Egyn** blows—who is the Angel in whose power is the Northern axis—the earthly spirits (among whom are those called the *Bene Elohim* <note>Hebrew: "Sons of God."</note>) are animated, and they shall have dominion in the great sea. And then the Heaven or the Air shall be converted into an earthly nature. Now, the Prince of this Element is **Azael** (as the Kabbalists maintain), who derives his power from the Archangel governing the sphere of *Saturn*. He receives his influences—congealing, dry, and cold—from the lucid fountain of *Binah* <note>The Sephirah of "Understanding."</note> and hides them in the *Saturnine Globe*, from which they are later rained down and dispersed by the Northern winds into the aerial sea. Finally, this *Egyn*, who is the presiding officer of the North wind, is governed and either restrained or sent forth by the Archangel **Gabriel**, who is the Prince of the Sphere of the Moon.

Similarly, when **Amaymon** breathes—who is the cardinal Angel of the *South*—the spirits of the Element of air rejoice and are animated. The leader of such spirits or troops is **Mahazael**, whose power is partly from Mars and partly from Jupiter; however, in his *Jovial* <note>Jupiter-like; benevolent and expansive.</note> nature he does not harm but benefits creatures, just as in his *Martial* <note>Mars-like; aggressive or destructive.</note> condition he causes harm. Over both the aerial leader and that southern cardinal angel, the lord is **Noriel**, or **Uriel**, who either loosens or pulls back their reins as the will of God may be, whether for good or for evil; hence he brings forth either good or evil to creatures. Finally, the **Western Leader**, having power over that wind which by its breath refreshes the spirits of the element of Water, is called **Paymon**: whose Angelic Lord is **Raphael**. *And so it is with the others.*

By which it seems to be indicated that benevolent species of human nature are present everywhere, as well as malicious and malevolent ones.

Concerning the malevolent spirits and those adverse to the human race, we shall speak in our *History of Diseases*; but here, as the subject of this treatise requires, we shall discourse only upon those spirits leading to the paths of life and health.

In the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Large World" or the universe as a whole, reflecting the "Microcosm" of the human being.</note> we see rains, snows, winds, and other such meteorological phenomena serve the benefit of plants, cattle, and men themselves—all of which <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, often used in this period to denote the source of all being.</note> brings forth by means of his Angels from his treasures hidden in the air. For the treasures of God are those lights of *Wisdom* sent forth from the inner sanctuaries of the divine shrine, expanded everywhere into the aerial world according to his will, even for the sake of mortals.

For (as was declared before) the name *Jehovah* encompasses the entire <term>Sephirotic trunk</term> <note>A reference to the Sephirot, the ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalah, often depicted as a tree.</note>, whose branches are engaged both in severity and in mercy. Thus the Angel whom he sent before the Israelites to guide them on their journey was sometimes occupied with severity.

But truly, just as He made His angels winds and invisible spirits, so indeed He made His ministers a burning flame; these are they who are accustomed to carry out the aforementioned matters. # On the Super-celestial Origin of Life and Health.

We have dealt with this in the "Contest against Folly," or our "Response to Marin Mersenne"; <note>Reference to Robert Fludd's work *Sophiae cum Moria Certamen* (The Contest of Wisdom with Folly, 1629), written to defend his mystical philosophy against the attacks of the French scholar Marin Mersenne.</note> therefore, we do not intend to speak more on this subject here: except that we consider those men unfortunate who, in their ignorance, seem to utterly deny that humans have their own guardian angels. That fellow Mersenne is of such a sort; I warn him from the heart to repent, and to take back into his soul the words of <term>Arbatel</term> <note>Referring to the *Arbatel de Magia Veterum*, a 16th-century manual of spiritual magic that emphasizes piety and the role of Olympic spirits.</note> concerning the highest study of Wisdom, which were spoken not at all foolishly, to this effect: namely, *That one part of **Theosophy** <note>Divine wisdom or "God-knowledge."</note> is the knowledge of the Word of God and a life established according to it; another part is the knowledge of God's government through the **Angels**, whom Scripture calls "Watchers," as well as the understanding of the mysteries of Angels. In the same way, one part of **Cacosophy** <note>literally "evil wisdom" or false, ignorant philosophy.</note> is the contempt for the Word of God and living according to the will of the Devil; another is ignorance of God's government through the Angels; and a third is the contempt for the protection of the Angels: by which means men render themselves companions of Devils.* These are the words of Arbatel, and they come from the very veil of Truth.

We conclude, therefore, that human Health seems to proceed chiefly from the Spirit blowing from the cardinal points; and also that from this Spirit comes all generation and preservation. Hence the Prophet said: *Come, Spirit, from the four winds and breathe upon these slain, that they may live again, etc.* <note>original: "Spiritus veni à quatuor ventis & insuffla interfectos istos, vt reuiuiscant, &c." - Ezekiel 37:9</note> By this speech and the effect of that Invocation, he seems to prove that both the giving of life and the growth of the limbs, as well as the power of all generation and the mystical method of rising from the dead, proceed from that one Spirit blowing from the four winds; and even that all the Angels, in effect, are nothing but a single **Universal Spirit**, <note>original: "Spiritus Catholicus"</note> who works all things both in the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The Great World, or the universe.</note> and in the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The Little World, or the human being.</note>. Hence Job said:
<margin>Job 33:4</margin> <note>The original text mistakenly cites Job 23:4.</note>
*The Spirit of the strong God has made me, and the breath or inspiration of the Almighty has given me life.*

Furthermore, it should be observed that just as sterile clouds are gathered together in the great world by the Winds or the favorable and merciful Spirit, filled with the seeds of life and sweetness; so indeed the **Sperm** in the Microcosm (which is stored in its vessels for procreation) is perfected and adapted for generation by the life-giving Spirit of God acting centrally, and by the subtle airy or elementary part of the whole composite—and this by the inspiration of the most hidden Spirit gathered from the four "corners," as it were, of the Microcosmic Earth. But now let us proceed to the celestial reasoning of Life and Health in the manner of the common astrologers.

### CHAPTER I.

->*In which the principle of Astrological Life and Health is explained.*<-

---

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'V' containing a scene with a man in 17th-century attire standing in a landscape with a tree and distant hills.</image-desc>Just as in Arithmetic, we proceed from Unity into multiplicity: so indeed it happens in the formal progress of counting among men. However, it is certain that all counting is not (in effect) anything other than the multiform repetition of that same Unity; and consequently, it is contained by Unity. The matter stands in exactly the same way regarding the consideration of efficient causes <note>The "efficient cause" is the primary source of change or rest; for example, a carpenter is the efficient cause of a table.</note>: for some estimate and truly hold God as the <term>Monad</term> <note>original: "Monadem"; in Fludd’s Hermetic philosophy, this refers to the indivisible, singular source of all existence.</note> for the unique and sole agent in this world. Others say an Angel, or Angels, are the primary efficient causes; some place the Stars as the chief actors in **Fatality** <note>original: "Fatalitate"; referring to the unfolding of destiny or the preordained course of events governed by the heavens.</note>, saying that they primarily act upon lower things: such are those most skilled in Astrology. But the ancient Philosophers and Physicians establish the Elements and their forms as the efficient causes of things. From this it has arisen that men have arranged as many subordinate causes as there are almost sciences in the world. Yet, when the matter is considered a little more maturely, God, by means of His Wisdom, is the sole actor in this world, and none is with Him, as Isaiah testifies. And the Apostle says:
> *From Him, in Him, and through Him are all things.* <note>original: "Ab ipso, in ipso, & per ipsum sunt omnia"; a quotation of Romans 11:36, emphasizing God as the source and sustainer of all.</note>
Therefore, they err who say that an Angel or another creature does this or that: when rather God works all things in the Angel, and through the Angel, or another creature (as if through an <term>Instrument</term> <note>original: "Organon"; the Greek word for a tool or organ used to perform a task.</note>). For it is not the <term>lute</term> <note>original: "barbiton"; an ancient stringed instrument.</note> or the Lyre that makes music, but the Musician; nor even the Musician, but the Soul of the one playing; yet not even the Soul of the one playing, but the divine act, which is that central agent that moves the Spirit as if it were an immediate vehicle and provokes it; and the Spirit (incited by the divine ray) moves the body, and the body, with the Spirit moving it, strikes the string, and the string being struck makes the Organ or Instrument sound.

Therefore, in all that multiplication of causes, we find in truth nothing but a unique Essential agent, which is God Himself, who, insofar as He is in Himself unique and indivisible, is the sole actor and moving form in every worldly Instrument. For neither the spirit in man, nor the body, nor the string in the Instrument, nor the instrument itself can do more by themselves than material things destitute of form. By the same logic, without the ray of uncreated light, neither Angel, nor Star, nor wind, nor Element—which are indeed the Instruments of the one uniquely acting Divinity—can accomplish anything.

# On the Supercelestial Origin of Life and Health.

Therefore, we say that an Angel functions like the human spirit, in which the resident Divine Mind is observed to act immediately from its center. For **GOD** is said to act through the Angel as if through His instrument <note>original: "Organum"; here meaning a tool or biological instrument through which a higher power operates.</note>. In this same way, a Star is related to the human body, insofar as an Angel acts within it, with **GOD** inciting the action from the center, no differently than the Soul operates in and through the body; it is the internal principle of the mind itself. Thus, the Star acts upon the earth and all elemental things <note>original: "Elementata"; things composed of the four elements (earth, air, fire, water).</note>, much like a striking instrument <note>original: "pulsantis instrumentum"; likely a reference to a musical instrument or a clockwork mechanism.</note>, which elements then tend to produce the effects of their harmony in the open air (also like an instrument). From these things, it cannot be hidden from the Wise that God is the sole and unique Actor in nature and in natural things, to whom alone be praise and honor.

And yet, we will now speak according to the common manner, and like Astrologers and Physicians, we will imagine that the heavens and the stars are the sole actors upon lower things, so that we may deal with worldly matters in a worldly way.

<margin>Hippocrates, *On Fleshes*.</margin>
Hippocrates says: *It seems to me that I should say nothing concerning celestial and sublime things, except insofar as I shall demonstrate that men and all other animals that live and are generated on earth have their Principle and Origin from there; and that the Soul is from heaven; and that pain, sickness, death, and finally whatever good or evil is in man, proceeds from heaven, etc.* In this thread of discourse, that man—easily the Prince of the Pagan <note>original: "Ethnicorum"; referring to the pre-Christian Greek physicians.</note> Physicians—seems to recognize that the formal Author of lower things is the Heaven with its glowing fires. Indeed, he seems to not hesitate at all to establish it as the very source of life; although, as was declared before, the origin of that power is from a far more exalted fountain.

<margin>Ptolemy, *Centiloquy*, Discourse 9.</margin>
Furthermore, Ptolemy also committed to his writings that the "faces" <note>In astrology, a "face" (or decan) is a subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> of this elemental world are subject to the faces of heaven. And all Philosophers seem to agree on this: that higher things act upon lower things, and lower things are ruled by higher things. Similarly, they conclude that the lower world is contiguous with the superior bodies.

<margin>Reuchlin, *On the Art of the Kabbalah*, book 2.</margin>
And all Kabbalists agree on this (as mentioned before): that all lower things are representative of higher things, and that as it happens below, so it is acted above, etc. <note>This is a variation of the famous Hermetic maxim "As above, so below."</note>

<margin>Hermes, *Asclepius*, book 2.</margin>
For this reason, therefore, Hermes called *the Heaven a sensible **GOD*** <note>original: "Cælum sensibilem Deum"; a God that can be perceived by the physical senses.</note>, insofar as it is the administrator of all bodies, whose growth and decay are allotted to the Sun and the Moon, etc. But indeed, in a Christian manner, he himself concludes thus: *God, who is the maker of all, is the governor of the heavens, of the soul itself, and of all things that are in the world.* Thus he speaks. Wherefore he also says elsewhere: *Heaven itself is full of God, etc.*

<margin>Aristotle, *Meteorology*, Book 1.</margin>
But let us proceed in the common manner. Aristotle says: *That this world is almost continuous with the superior motions, so that its entire power is governed from there.* Wherefore I feel it must be concluded that the judgment of the Stars in the protection of Health <note>original: "Sanitatis tuitione"; the maintenance or defense of health.</note> is by no means to be entirely neglected; since that passage of Holy Scripture seems to argue for something more than just accidental illumination:

<margin>Deuteronomy 4.</margin>
->which is as follows: God made the celestial bodies for the service of all the Nations which are under heaven. But concerning this, we shall speak a little more clearly in the following.<-

### CHAPTER II.

->That the knowledge of Astrology is absolutely necessary for any true Physician.<-

From the previously cited passage of Hippocrates <note>Referring to the quote from *On Fleshes* on the preceding page.</note>, it is therefore right to conclude that the observation of the Stars is a primary requirement and is entirely necessary for a true Physician. This is so that he may not only judge the condition of an attacking disease, but also so that he might foresee with diligent caution what adversity might befall anyone's health. Consequently, he may skillfully anticipate a future evil that threatens health with danger, and hinder its malevolent effect. 

<margin>Haly</margin> <note>Likely Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer whose works were standard textbooks in the Renaissance.</note> This seems to be confirmed by Haly in a certain small preface placed before the *Works of Hippocrates*: *A Physician who is ignorant of Astronomy is like a blind man testing his way with a staff; miserably stumbling here and there at every phantom and empty appearance of good or evil, trembling like a fool, etc.*

By these words, he seems to denote how uncertain, inconsistent, and lacking the profession of Medicine is when the mystery of Astrology is ignored.

<margin>Ptolemy in the *Centiloquium*</margin> <note>The *Centiloquium* is a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Claudius Ptolemy.</note> Hence, Ptolemy (easily the Prince of Astrologers) brings forth these words: *The best professor of astrology can avert many effects of the stars when he is not ignorant of their natures, and has prepared himself diligently before their effects happen: And so it is in other matters.*

Furthermore, this also teaches the hours of <term>Election</term> <note>Electional astrology is the practice of determining the most auspicious moment to begin an action, such as performing surgery or administering a cure.</note>, in which medicines—both purgative and astringent—ought to be more suitably used for the human body. For very often, purgative medicines are given by a Physician ignorant of Astrology under an astringent <note>original: "astringente"; a contracting or binding influence that stops flow, the opposite of what a laxative/purgative should do.</note> Influence; for this reason, they rarely produce the expected effect. So also in "fluxes of the belly" <note>diarrhea or dysentery</note>, binding medicines fail to produce the effect expected by the physician while slippery and laxative Influences hold dominion. From this, it is observed that sometimes purgatives work more easily, and at other times they purge and evacuate with greater difficulty and in smaller quantities.

But concerning these things, we shall deal more copiously in the second Treatise of this Volume, where we will discuss Medicines.

### CHAPTER III.

->On the properties of the fixed Stars and their influences upon these lower things: and how they are accustomed to produce both diseases and health in turn.<-

That the fixed Stars scattered in the Firmament produce wonderful effects upon these lower things by means of their influences, we are taught first by that **polar** star, called **Alruckaba** <note>original: "Alruckaba"; an Arabic name for the star Polaris. Fludd uses it to show the star's specific "occult" or hidden influence over magnetism.</note> by the Egyptians. It possesses the nature of Saturn and Venus: as such, it is its nature to attract the Magnet to itself with an ardent affection, as the property of the mariner’s needle proves. For there is such a relationship between the Magnet <note>the lodestone</note> and iron that the magnet is observed to pull the iron strongly to itself by greedily desiring it. By this observation we are taught how strong is the operation of the higher things upon the lower; and also that those creatures upon which the said polar star acts by office—attributing to them a hidden life and being—are the Magnet among stones, and Iron among metals. And it is from here that Cecco d'Ascoli <note>original: "Cichus Esculanus"; a 13th-century Italian polymath and physician.</note>, where he speaks of the twelve signs of the Zodiac, affirms that each of them received its particular and special name from the nature and property of whatever animal it presides over: since the nature of one seems to harmonize with the nature of the other.

# On the Celestial Origin of Life and Health.

<margin>Reuchlin, 198.</margin> <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a German humanist and scholar of Hebrew and the Cabala.</note>
And <term>Moses the Arab</term> <note>original: "Moses Arabicus"; referring to the famous Jewish philosopher Maimonides.</note> says: that every living thing has a star from the heavens flowing into it, whose role is to preside over it; that is, to guard its health and preserve its very Essence, and this by divine command. For example: the stars existing in the sign of **Aries** <note>The Ram</note> pour their influences into the earthly ram; and the celestial **Scorpio** sends influences of life and Essence into the scorpions of the earth; and so it is with the rest, according to that axiom of the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Followers of a school of Jewish mysticism that influenced many Renaissance thinkers like Fludd.</note> previously mentioned: namely, *All inferior things represent the superior, and as it is done below, so it is driven above.* Likewise, <term>Hermes</term> <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary author of the Hermetic corpus.</note> says: that among stones, the star called **Aldebaran** (which is located at 25 degrees of **Taurus**) presides over the <term>Carbuncle</term> <note>A red gemstone, usually a garnet.</note>; and among plants, it presides over <term>Spurge</term> <note>original: "Tithimalli"; a genus of plants known for their milky sap.</note>; and so on for the rest. Finally, there is no herb, plant, stone, or any other lower mineral or animal which does not have a star that "strikes" it, as the Doctors of the Hebrews testify.

We say, therefore, that among such <term>fixed stars</term> <note>Stars that do not move relative to each other, unlike the "wandering stars" or planets.</note>, some are more favorable to the life and health of men, while others are adverse and more contrary. For example: those signs of the **Zodiac** which are the houses of **Jupiter** and **Venus** are most pleasing to human life. Such is the case with **Taurus**, from which the "sweet influences of the **Pleiades**" rain down, as **Job** testifies <note>Referring to Job 38:31, "Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades?"</note>. For this reason, and because of the happy connection made between the **Gemini**, this sign is also very beneficial to the human race, insofar as it emits a sweet moisture and moderately warm influences to inferior living beings. Similarly, **Libra** is also very favorable to life and health, because it pours moist and warm influences into lower things. So too **Pisces** liberally rains down salutary influences ascribed and sacred to the power of **Jupiter** upon lower things; and **Sagittarius** is also accustomed to benefit those with <term>phlegmatic temperaments</term> <note>One of the four "humors" or bodily fluids; a phlegmatic person was thought to be cool and moist.</note>.

It would indeed be very tedious to discuss all of these matters fully in this place; therefore, we do not wish to offer more here concerning the fixed stars that lead to life and health. However, as for the fixed stars that oppose human health, we shall say more about them in the second Treatise (God willing).

### CHAPTER I.

->*How inferior things are ruled by superior things, and that generation and health, as well as disease, corruption, and death, are caused by superior influences.*<-

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter H with intricate floral and scrollwork designs.</image-desc>

<margin>Poimandres 9.</margin> <note>Refers to the first book of the *Corpus Hermeticum*, a foundational text of Western esotericism attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note>
Hermes says that the revolution of the World, driving the generations of life, produces certain qualities; some infect the wicked and defile them, while others defend the good and purify them. This divine Instrument of the divine will was constructed primarily for this reason: so that, receiving all seeds from God and hiding them in its vast womb, it may produce all things by composing them, and again take all things away by dividing them. And like a skilled farmer, it prunes whatever is overly grown, so that they may live again at fixed intervals of time; nor is there anything to which the world does not grant life, being at once the place of life and also its teacher, etc. Hence, elsewhere he calls the world a "second God" <note>original: "mundum vocat secundum Deum"</note> insofar as it participates in the primary Divinity. From these things it seems to argue that divine nurseries are sown everywhere in the vast expanse of the world, and that through the planetary revolutions, they are ordained daily in composite creatures toward both generation and destruction, and various alterations are produced in the Elements.

Therefore in another place he says: "Behold the seven worlds placed below, built with wondrous adornment, completing eternity in their eternal order by their own course. Each is full of lights; yet there is in no way fire within them: for the friendship of contraries and the union of dissimilar things established a light illuminated by the act of God—the father of all good things, the Prince of the whole order, and the eternal Leader of the seven worlds." But the Sun and Moon are the Instruments of Divinity for the birth and death of things, for the increase and decrease of things, etc. <margin>Asclepius 2.</margin> <note>Another major text of the Hermetic corpus.</note> By the speech of this high priest <note>Hermes</note>, it is argued that the seven Planets and their <term>Intelligences</term> <note>The spiritual or angelic beings believed to guide the physical planets.</note> are ordained for the administration of the laws of both friendship and enmity, both of life or birth and of death or destruction in all things; and that the Sun and Moon are the primary instruments for performing that duty.

# CHAPTER II.
## On the properties of Jupiter.

Ptolemy and Galen (as reported by Julius Hyginus in the *Phenomena of Aratus* <note>Hyginus was a Roman mythographer who wrote a commentary on Aratus's astronomical poem, "Phenomena."</note>) said that out of the vast choir of stars, two are simply helpers, beneficent, and friends to nature: namely Jupiter and Venus; just as they also called two others, namely Saturn and Mars, corrupters, enemies to nature, and evildoers. Here, therefore, we speak of the beneficent ones in their order.

> Jupiter is the most merciful nurturer, protector, preserver, fruit-bearer, sower, hospitable, and beneficent sustainer of sublunary things, a healing and kind deity, and indeed the Father of all. Hence some wish to ascribe that name, namely Jupiter, to him because of that property of his. Jupiter (I say), as if "Helping Father" <note>original: "iuvās Pater"</note>; and *Zeus* from *Zoë* <note>original: "Zeus à Ζωὴ"</note>: that is, Life. From this it follows that in the month of birth where Jupiter is most powerful—namely the ninth—the infant is healthily brought forth into the light. The reason for this matter is gathered from the condition of that planet: for since it is in its constitution temperately hot and moist (which its position in the sky also seems to prove), indeed, it is located between cold Saturn and hot Mars. Thus, the cold and frozen Saturnine nature, dissolved by the heat of Mars, seems to fall into the moderate temperament of Jupiter. Therefore, it is said to have an airy disposition within itself; wherefore it has its influence especially on the air of the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "great world" or the universe as a whole, which reflects the "microcosm" of the human body.</note>, which it is accustomed to fill with the nurseries of life. This life is usually composed of the <term>innate heat</term> <note>original: "calido natiuo"; the internal heat believed to sustain biological life.</note> as the active agent and the <term>radical moisture</term> <note>original: "humido radicali"; the essential fluid that acts as fuel for the innate heat.</note> as the passive subject, from which, through the mediation of solar rays, both vital and natural spirits arise. For by the mediation of these things, every creature lives and breathes.

Furthermore, that auspicious planet Venus joins itself to this kind of union of life; hence Ficino <note>Marsilio Ficino (1433–1499), an influential Italian priest and scholar who sought to harmonize Neoplatonism with Christianity.</note> says (and not without wisdom) that the three Graces contributing to life are the Sun (☉), Jupiter (♃), and Venus (♀). But he makes Jupiter the middle of the twin Graces, and the one most suited to human life. Therefore it is also called the *Greater Fortune* <note>original: "Fortunium maius"</note>. This planet, therefore, having dominion through its influences over the air, renders it kind, moderately hot and moist, and very useful as the food of life, as will be more clearly explained in the description of the Sun. It is also said to have dominion over the blood in a creature, and is dedicated to the Liver; and from the biological faculties, it claims the "natural power" for itself. In quality, it is hot and moist.

But truly, this Royal Star is sometimes defiled by the worse planets having dominion in the sky, and is made an inciter of diseases (as will be said in the following Treatise), but this is beyond its nature and occurs only by accident.

# CHAPTER III.
## On Venus.

Cicero maintains that this star is called *Venus*, as if "coming benevolently" <note>original: "beneuole ueniens"</note> to all things; and by others it is called the genital and prolific star, being in its nature kind and beneficent to life and generation. For Astrologers believe that through this planet, while inferior bodies and substances are generated or nurtured, a gentle and dewy juice is supplied. Hence some wish that the nature of this planet agrees with an airy heat, as if excited by choler <note>One of the four humors, associated with heat and fire.</note>, and with a subtle and cold wateriness. From this it arises that it attracts toward pleasures and is occupied with soft and sweet things, tending more toward the outer surfaces than the center; unless its nature were restrained by the proximity of the Sun, or in the human...

...is not held back by the bridle of reason. Nevertheless, because of the temperament of her nature, Venus is a nurturer of innate moisture and is not at all opposed to innate heat. For this reason, she is frequently called the *Lesser Fortune* <note>original: "Fortunium minus"</note> by astrologers, and also *Nurturing* <note>original: "Alma"</note>, as some would have it, from the word for "nourishing."

We conclude, therefore, that the breath of Venus is moist, but without any excess, and possesses a small and temperate warmth. It is from this that the ancient poets—not without skill—imagined Venus to have been born from the foam of the sea, as if she were the Spirit of the Waters. This may be because the seeds of animals are foamy, or as Euripides argues, because those who are captured and overcome by Venus or Concupiscence <note>The desire for physical or worldly pleasure.</note> are of unsound mind. Thus, to this planet as well as to Jupiter, the Liver <note>original: "Hepar"</note> is attributed among the parts of the body, in which the concupiscible faculty resides. The seat of "quivered Cupid" (whose mother is Venus), as well as of titillations and appetites, is thought to be here by both Plato and Galen—without which no sensing animal can exist. Hence the poet wrote:

->The spleen makes us laugh, the liver compels us to love.<-
<note>original: "Splen ridere facit, cogit amare Iecur."</note>

Finally, she herself governs the genitals among the limbs, as the minister of pleasures. Among the senses, she presides over taste and smell, in which no one doubts that the delights of both the soul and the body are situated. Of the faculties, she claims that of appetite and the concupiscible power; of the humors, she claims sweet, tasteless, and natural phlegm <note>original: "pituita"</note>, which can be changed into blood and "cooked" by the body's innate heat.

By the disposition of nature, she renders people—by virtue of her temperament—joyful and happy in the company of men. They take delight in music and dancing, long to be adorned with flowers, and are by such a nature delicate. Although this star brings all these benefits to humanity by its benign nature, it can sometimes be "badly affected" by accident—that is, by the malevolent gaze of ill-intended planets dominating in the heavens. On such occasions, it is observed to produce diseased effects, as will be explained in the *following Treatise of this volume*.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*On the Planets which, in their healthy as well as unhealthy dispositions, act upon the animal body: and first, concerning the Sun, the Prince of the Heavens.*<-

<margin>Asclepius, 2.</margin>
The Sun and the Moon (says Hermes Trismegistus) are the instruments of Divinity for the birth and death of things, and for their growth and decay. And yet it is certain and proved by experience that the Sun, in its manifest disposition, is not an adversary to living things but a friend—the greatest of all other benevolent bodies in the heavens, as we shall soon most clearly prove. For although its temperament seems to agree with "red bile" <note>original: "cholera rubra"</note>, and consequently assumes a fiery quality, it is nonetheless quite temperate in its heat and dryness. Because of this moderate condition, it is favorable to the life of creatures, which consists of "radical moisture" <note>The essential fluid thought to sustain life in medieval medicine.</note> joined with heat. Indeed, its entire substance seems to be most full of a life-giving power, by means of which the celestial signs, the other fixed stars of the firmament, and the remaining planets, as well as all sublunary creatures, live, engage in generation, and enjoy their desired health. Therefore, Heraclitus did not break into this discourse without consideration: *If you take the Sun out of the world, what is our poor body if it lacks a soul? No pulsating vein is moved there; no judgment of sensing remains in it, no vital condition, nor any breath.*

And this is the reason why the Sun is called by some the *heart of heaven* <note>original: "cor cœli"</note>. For just as the living blood exists in the heart, moistening and watering the other members of the human body and infusing vital motion, so in the Sun there appears to be the vegetation and preservation of all things, both lower and higher. This is because it breathes life and heat into the lower things by its light—which is a simple act, turning all things toward itself with life-giving heat, permeating all Beings, and...
