# C H A P T E R I I I.

## Concerning the Method of thanksgiving <note>original: "congratulatoriæ," meaning prayers that offer "congratulations" or grateful acknowledgement of God's deeds</note> prayer in general. And then it moves toward more specific subjects.

I believe it is hidden from no righteous and pious person that prayers of thanksgiving for benefits received are necessary for any just man. For if this saying is appropriate among men—"If we call a man ungrateful to his fellow man, we have said the worst of all things"—then how much more is gratitude toward our God to be expected from us sinners, from whom we receive all necessary things out of His good grace? Do we not seek Him like perpetual beggars for our daily bread, without which we could not persist for even a moment of time? And for such a great benefit received, are no thanks to be returned by us to a God so gracious, merciful, and liberal? If, therefore, we recognize His grace and favor for the benefit received this time with a sincere mind and an upright heart, we shall undoubtedly find Him constant in His future benefits. On the other hand, if anyone is ungrateful and does not return thanks to his so well-deserving God, he must be considered the most ungrateful of all toward his Creator; God will then fail him in his necessity because of his ingratitude and will hide His face from him.

<margin>Exodus 15.</margin>
We find, therefore, that the holy ancient Fathers humbly returned thanks to Jehovah their God for every thing they received. For example: Moses and Miriam, with an oratorical song and a hymn of thanksgiving <note>original: "Hymno Eucharistico," using the Greek-derived term for thanksgiving</note> for the overturning of Pharaoh and the Egyptian army and their drowning in the sea; the three righteous men <note>referring to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego</note> for their preservation from the fiery furnace; David for his safety and various other benefits; Judith on account of the vic...

### BOOK I. CHAPTER I.
->*In which the general reasoning for preserving and protecting health through celestial observation is discussed.*<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'Q' featuring a seated figure holding a celestial sphere within a circular frame, decorated with foliate flourishes.</image-desc>Although every reason and root of both health and sickness depends on that celestial and super-celestial root; nevertheless, since the Creator ordained the heavens and the stars so that they might be moved by His immortal spirit in a natural order and preordained influence <note>original: "influxu," referring to the astrological belief that power "flows" from the stars into the physical world</note>, to dispose lower things both toward generation and preservation in a state of health, as well as toward corruption and death in an unnatural condition, it will not (in my opinion) be difficult for a wise Physician to correct and turn for the better those harmful influences that are foreseen and coming, which will descend at fixed times by an inevitable fate. Nevertheless, the expert Physician cannot provide this by his own art alone: or at least, the person who is still healthy does not wish to obey the command of a physician foretelling future evil, unless God—who is the sole actor of all things and in all people—directs the Physician by His good grace for the benefit and advantage of the one whom the Heavens threaten, and makes that person obedient to the Physician, and blesses the work of the Physician himself. For as God is unique and always the same: so indeed His immediate act is in the super-celestial places, and although in the celestial regions this power seems to be mediated <note>i.e., acting through intermediaries</note>, yet it is no less inseparable from its source than the portion of the soul in the chest is from that in the brain. Thus it is said, *God works all things and in all*, but in different organs. So He acts differently in the Empyrean Spirit <note>The highest, most "fiery" part of heaven</note> than in the Ethereal, and differently also in this or that Star, and yet the power of God is always the same and of one essence.

<margin>Asclepius 2. <note>A reference to the *Asclepius*, a core text of the Hermetic tradition.</note></margin>
These things being duly known, we see the reason why by some Pagans <note>original: "Ethnicis"</note>, the Heaven is esteemed as God: and also the Stars are held as Gods: yet in such a way, and with the same caution, that all these have their relation to the one Jove, or Jehovah, as if from Him these aforementioned creatures receive their divine essence and action. Hence *Hermes Trismegistus* <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, blending Egyptian and Greek wisdom</note> did not blush to say repeatedly that *Heaven is a sensible God, the administrator of all bodies, whose increases and decreases have been allotted to the Sun and Moon*, but nonetheless with that caution, that he recognized the Governor of the true heavens and of the soul itself, and of all things which are in the World, to be He who is also the Maker of all, God, etc.

By which he seems to argue, that both the first Monad <note>original: "Monas," referring to the ultimate Unity or the One from which all existence flows</note> is absolute God; so indeed the World and consequently the Heaven is called God in a relative sense, insofar as it participates in the divine nature, by means of which it operates such things in successive order

### CHAPTER II.

->How Health may be preserved against the malevolent influences of the Heavens through the proper knowledge of constitutions, and their application to the fixed and wandering stars.<-

---

Since the Worldly Elements themselves follow the positions of the celestial bodies, just as human humors are made to conform to the natures of those same Elements—and are refreshed by their influences no differently than human life is by its airy food—it follows from this that the Worldly Elements draw the powers of their lives from the stars in a different way than human elements do from the [Worldly] Elements. From this, therefore, we have confirmed that old axiom of the Philosophers: *That the higher things act upon the lower, and as it is above, so also it is below.* <note>The famous Hermetic maxim "As above, so below," suggesting a correspondence between the cosmos and the individual.</note> Thus, those more skilled in the Cabala <note>Referring to Kabbalistic traditions which linked mystical interpretation with natural philosophy</note> maintain that lower things are representative of higher things: namely, the humors of the Elements and the Elements of the stars.

Once these things are well-weighed, it will not be difficult for a skilled physician, through the knowledge of a constitution <term>complexion: the specific balance of humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—in an individual, which was thought to determine their physical and mental health</term>, to have knowledge of the Element primarily predominating in him, and consequently of the fixed star and planet that preside over him. If the Physician understands these things well and considers them properly, he will find it a matter of great importance to make the attacks of malevolent influences <note>original: "influxus," the astrological flow of power from the stars to the earth</note> weaker, to avoid their evils and threats, and to blunt their edge, so that they cannot have such great force against a healthy man,

so as to alter it from its state of health. For example: just as the element of fire, in a moderate degree, has power over natural bile <note>Original: *bilem seu choleram*. In this system of medicine, health was determined by the balance of four "humors" or fluids; bile (cholera) was associated with heat and dryness.</note>; so the Sun possesses authority over the moderate and tempered virtue of fire, just as Mars himself claims dominion over unnatural bile and intense fire.

Having understood this, we can very easily discern which planet or fixed star may be harmful to a person with a naturally choleric temperament—provided we have correctly observed the friendships and enmities of the planets. Once this is perceived, we can, through various means, prevent the malevolent attacks and influences of the planets and the evils of the zodiac signs that are opposed to this specific "complexion" <note>A person's "complexion" or temperament was their unique constitutional makeup of humors.</note>. For it is better and wiser to prevent a future evil than to try to drive away an evil that is currently afflicting and actively attacking the body.

Therefore, let us proceed quickly to the exact arrangement of the temperaments and the knowledge of their qualities.

### CHAPTER III.
#### On the description of the Choleric temperament: and of the Element of Fire and the Star ruling over it.

Cholera—that is, yellow, red, or rust-colored bile—is the most natural kind. Among the heavenly bodies, it is subject to Mars and the Sun; among the elements, it is subject to Fire. Therefore, in its constitution, it is temperately hot and dry. In this particular balance of humors, the Sun is the stronger influence, while Mars is the weaker. For where Mars obtains his dominion, there the bile most often exceeds the boundaries or limits of nature; it is then considered to be "contrary to nature," which is why it produces fevers and other such fiery diseases. 

However, where this natural bile holds dominion in a person's temperament from birth, there the head and hair are found to be very black (like a crow's). The blacker and more curly the hair is, the more bilious and dry the person seems to be. These people are endowed with a low forehead, brownish-colored ears, a slender and thin face, and black eyes (in whose gaze a great brightness is sometimes perceived). They have black eyebrows and a straight nose, though it may be slightly hooked. They have large lips, black beard hair, hard and slender cheeks, a thin neck, a slender and lean body of a brown color, thin and scrawny arms and hands, and long fingers, nails, and shins. Their tongue is either the color of verdigris <note>A greenish-blue pigment; here suggesting a sickly or bitter coating.</note> or partakes of a yellowish hue; finally, they are mostly characterized by yellowish urine and stool. 

The choleric person desires sexual intercourse much, but is capable of little because of his dryness, which causes a lack of seed. He does not sleep much and eats little. His voice is loud and sharp like a trumpet, and in every condition, the choleric person is prone to anger.

Furthermore, by his internal nature, he is argumentative, given to drinking, and very easily seized by drunkenness. In such a state, if his anger is provoked, he becomes furious and without restraint—behaving like a lion. He is a curser and a doer of evil, boastful and a braggart, exposing himself to danger as if it were nothing; he behaves in a stormy manner in such cases. He is easily governed by a woman, even though such intimacy may be harmful to him.

But if the bile is red and more yellowish, then the Moon and Venus have a share in that constellation, even though the Sun still claims dominion over it. Because of this, his condition agrees in many ways with the Phlegmatic <note>The "phlegmatic" temperament is the opposite of the choleric, being cold and moist.</note> person. It must be noted, however, that this kind of temperament is inwardly full, in the manner of a toad or a serpent; for this reason, it is imprinted everywhere with the spots and signs of serpents, for this type burns more intensely within than the aforementioned species.

We conclude, therefore, that Cholera is one of the four natural humors of the human body, by the power of which the attractive force <term>attractive force: the biological "virtue" or power of an organ to draw in the nourishment it needs from the blood</term> is sustained in its vigor. It is generated in the liver and has its seat in the gallbladder. It has its power—

### CHAPTER IV.

->*On the signs of the sanguine complexion or humor. What its constellation is, and to which Element it is subjected.*<-

The sanguine person <note>One dominated by the "blood" humor, traditionally thought to be cheerful, active, and amorous.</note> has a beautiful rose-red color, a handsome face with red, round, and plump cheeks, and lips that are rosy and thick. They have yellowish or beautifully brownish hair, and sometimes sparse hair on the beard and eyebrows of a single color; a broad forehead; rounded temples; reddish ears; and a straight nose. Their eyes are blackish-brown for a "brown-sanguine" type, or bluish-gray <note>Original: *glaucos*</note> for a "white-sanguine" type. They have beautiful and even teeth, a thick and fleshy neck, and skin stretched by fat. The body is corpulent and full of flesh, with arms and limbs adorned with fat; they have thick hands with blood visible under the fingernails, and feet and shins that are plump and not long. Their urine and stool are citron-colored, like gold or yellow amber.

Finally, the person born with this temperament enjoys a hot and moist constitution <note>Ancient medicine categorized the four humors by "qualities": Blood was considered Hot and Moist, like the air.</note>. Regarding their constellation, they usually claim Venus (♀) as their own; however, the brown-sanguine person, as well as the white one, participates more in Jupiter (♃). In lust, they desire much because of their heat, and are capable of much because of the abundance of their moisture. For their Element, they have Air: since Air has dominion over those of the sanguine type.

*Signs of the soul* of such a person are these: They are very devoted to sexual union, and they deeply love those with whom they couple. They are greatly carried away by every kind of pleasure, namely banquets, dancing, music, and songs. They are affable and gracious, and usually free from worry; they are very fertile and have a resonant voice.

And here it should be noted that the white-sanguine person is more changeable and inconstant than the brown one; and that Jupiter (♃) is a better planet than Venus (♀), though both are sanguine planets—one white, and the other brown and blackish.

But where the complexion is brown-sanguine or somewhat blackish, the face is brown mixed with redness; the hair inclines toward blackness, the forehead is full and plump, and the body is corpulent, as explained before.

The difference between a Jovial <note>Influenced by Jupiter (Jove)</note> and a Venereal <note>Influenced by Venus</note> nature is as follows: for one has ivory-colored hair, and the other has blackish hair, and this is true for every part of the body. By this reasoning, their mixture can be known: for the whitish-sanguine person has a mixture of Venus (♀) and the Moon (☽), or Jupiter (♃) and the Moon (☽); and the brown-sanguine person has a mixture with Venus (♀) and Mars (♂). However, as it seems to me, Jupiter (♃) mixes with Venus rather than others in this complexion: because those who are brown-sanguine are more beautiful than the white ones.

### CHAPTER V.

->*On the signs of the Phlegmatic complexion, or the pituita humor. What its constellation is, and to which Element it is subjected.*<-

The phlegmatic person <note>Dominated by the "phlegm" humor, associated with a cold, moist, and often calm or sluggish nature.</note> has a pale and whitish face that is somewhat plump, but not like that of the sanguine person. They have a well-proportioned face; thin, ivory-colored, and soft hair; and beard hair that turns toward redness—not much of it, but sparse. Similarly, there is not much hair in the eyebrows. They have a short nose, which is usually quite sharp in the front and broad in the back, and thick, pale lips.

[A person of this type has] a pale tongue; a thick and stout neck; soft and curly skin; the body whitening all over; blue-gray eyes; arms, hands, and nails as beautiful as those of the sanguine; a decent stature; sweet breath; pale excrement; and white urine tending toward thickness.

The constellation for these people is the Moon <note>Original: *Luna*</note>; hence they are moist and cold in their nature. For this reason, they are capable of much in Venus <note>Original: *Venere*; referring here to sexual intercourse or activity</note> due to the abundance of moist matter, yet they have little desire because of their cold nature, especially during the cold quarters of the Moon; however, in the hot quarters, their activity increases. This humor participates primarily in the element of Water. From the conditions of their soul, they are recognized thus: they are quite irascible and moved suddenly to anger, but they set aside their anger just as quickly; they are changeable and inconsistent in their works; and they are not particularly wise, since they are generous to everyone. They do not keep counsel when moved by anger. They are temperate and impatient about staying in one place, not remaining quiet with their servants for long; they love new inventions, sleep well, and many thoughts and imaginings occupy their brains. What they do, they do lightly and quickly, but they do not know how to keep what they have; they labor much with others and are of great piety, compassion, and good contemplation. The Moon is their mistress; and for this reason, they are "lunatics" <note>Originally *Lunatici*, meaning influenced by the moon, implying instability or mood swings</note> and inconsistent in their deeds. One moment they will laugh and rejoice, and soon they will be struck by sadness and stupidity. Their talent is perceived to be better in sudden situations.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*On the signs of the Melancholic humor: its constellation and Element.*<-

Those endowed from their birth with the melancholic humor have a leaden color, a fairly tall stature, large joints in every part of the body, and thick bones; a fairly broad face and skin with large grains, like a bull’s; much hair on the head, hard and dark in color, which will suddenly turn gray; large ears; large wrinkles on the forehead and face; drooping eyebrows with many long hairs, tending downward over the eyes; a dark and scowling expression, a contracted forehead, yellowish and ferociously staring eyes, a large nose, large lips, and large teeth like those of horses; the nose and lips are somewhat pale and poorly colored; they have a large mouth, from which they eat and devour much. The neck is curved like a horn; they have large hands and feet, long shins, and large knees. They are very sinewy and have large veins; in summer they smell like a goat; they are quite strong. They possess a tongue of a leaden color, and in build they are slender and thin. The constellation of this type is Saturn; therefore, this humor in its temperament <note>Original: *complexione*; refers to the specific balance of qualities</note> is cold and dry. A person of this condition has little appetite for the things of Venus <note>Referring to sexual desire</note>, because he is cold; and again, he is capable of little in the act itself, because he is dry. Therefore, in the sexual act, this is the worst of all humors.

Signs from the condition of the soul are these: they are rarely or never cheerful; they eat and drink much; they hold everyone in suspicion; they do not sleep much; they are men greedy for the world, deceivers, and possess no conscience; they trust no one; what they have, they hold onto firmly; they are quickly angered, even over nothing, and are slow to forgive. These are the most ingenious of all others, they do not live peacefully with a wife for long, and whatever they do is of long duration, for they are slow in working. They are very lofty in spirit and proud, and in governance, they are more excellent than the rest. Their master is Saturn.

### CHAPTER VII.

->*In which the friendship and enmity of the Planets among themselves is recounted, and how one must proceed in the preservation of health and in astrological reasoning.*<-

Astrologers <note>Original: *Mathematici*; in the seventeenth century, this term often referred to those who calculated planetary positions, including astrologers</note> have observed that there is both a great and evident friendship and enmity among the planets. For instance, there is a great hatred between Jupiter and Mars; just as, on the other hand, Saturn pursues Venus with ill-will. Therefore, since Jupiter and Venus are friends to the lives of creatures, both are called "Fortunes" <note>Original: *Fortunia*; referring to the Benefic planets which bring good luck or health</note>. Likewise, Saturn and Mars are enemies to life, and for that reason, they are called "Misfortunes" <note>Original: *Infortunia*; the Malefic planets which bring hardship or disease</note> and malevolent.

Furthermore, the Moon is an enemy to Mars and to Jupiter: insofar as her watery moisture is opposed to the fiery disposition of Mars, and her coldness is opposed to that airy heat of Jupiter.

Similarly, Saturn is an enemy to the Sun and Mars, with respect to his earthy coldness; and he is an enemy to Venus with respect to her heat. Yet, truly, the Moon is a friend [to Saturn]. And so it is among the others.

Once these things have been rightly considered, one must proceed in this manner: Once the complexion <note>The specific balance of "humors" or fluids in a person's body</note> and the predominating planet and sign are known, it can be very easily discerned to which infirmity that person is most inclined. For example: Choler <note>The yellow bile humor, associated with fire and heat</note>, when malevolently excited by a bad aspect from Mars, very easily ignites a fever and turns natural bile into something preternatural <note>Outside the normal course of nature, i.e., diseased</note>. So also, when the Sun rises in the summer time with the Dog Star <note>Sirius, referred to here as a "Martial Star" because of its heat</note>, it excites feverish imbalances in the blood, especially in a bilious complexion. For this reason, Galen <note>A famous Roman physician whose theories dominated medicine for centuries</note> holds that just as phlegmatic people feel better in the summer—because the coldness of their watery humor is repressed by the heat of the summer season, and by this reasoning their innate heat is more excited—so indeed Choleric people are known to feel better in the winter. This is because the excessive heat of their choler is tempered by the coldness of the season, and its dryness is restrained because of the abundance of the predominating moisture; thus, in that season, the radical moisture <note>The essential life-sustaining fluid within the body</note> exults more greatly.

<margin>☉</margin>
Hence it follows that if a wise Physician perceives that Mars will have great dominion in a certain Choleric Sign—for example, in Aries ♈, Leo ♌, or Sagittarius ♐—and that he regards the Sun or Moon with a malevolent aspect, then such attacks of Mars must be prevented. This is done with herbs or other medicines which are subjected to the enemy of Mars—namely, Jupiter. These medicines, both those that purge and those that alter the humors, should especially be gathered and prepared at a time when Mars is weak—being in his "fall" or "detriment" <note>Positions in the zodiac where a planet's influence is weakened</note>—and when Jupiter is in his domestic dignity or "exaltation" <note>Positions where a planet's influence is strongest</note>, preferably with Jupiter regarding Mars with a good aspect, if possible. For by this reasoning, medicines of the property of Jupiter, collected while he is in his power and exaltation, will be rendered more fit and stronger for repelling and resisting the malevolent attacks of a predominating Mars.

In such a case, the patient ought also to face North and West, and choose a bedroom situated in that quarter for his habitation until the dominion of Mars and that malevolent aspect have passed.

Furthermore, because Mars is an enemy to the Moon, her benevolent aspects and the medicines subjected to her—prepared while she remains in her exaltation—will be wonderfully beneficial. But if a healthy person is of a phlegmatic complexion, since his constellation is the Moon, and the Moon (both in the full moon and in the "moist mansions" <note>Specific segments of the lunar cycle associated with water</note>) makes the phlegm in that healthy person heavier and more malignant—especially if Saturn regards it with a malevolent aspect, or if Mars looks upon it and turns it into a putrid nature—then in the former case, the protections of a predominating Jupiter are requi-

**A.**
**The minor principal virtues are ministers and, as it were, handmaidens to the principal ones; and they are four, namely:**

> **The Attractive Virtue**: which is hot and dry in its temperament and is subject to Mars ♂ and the Sun ☉; it operates through straight fibers in the administration of:
> - **The Animal Faculty**: <note>In this context, "Animal" refers to the *Anima* or soul/mind, governing the nervous system.</note> these fibers are in the veins, arteries, nerves, membranes, and other parts, both fleshy and membranous.
> - **The Vital Faculty**: For when fibers of this sort in the substance of the heart are contracted, while the other types of fibers are relaxed, the heart is then dilated; and this movement is called **Diastole**. <note>The phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle relaxes and allows the chambers to fill with blood.</note>
> - **The Natural Faculty**: For these fibers, constituting the internal lining <term>tunic<gloss>a layer of tissue or membrane</gloss></term> of the stomach and intestines, perform the duty of drawing from the esophagus, as well as in the gall bladder, the mesenteric vessels, and other veins.

> **The Retentive Virtue**: which is cold and dry in temperament, and receives its influence from Saturn ♄.
> **The Concoctive Virtue**: <note>Also known as the "Digestive" virtue.</note> which consists in a hot and moist temperament; and Jupiter ♃ presides over this.
> **And these two operate through oblique fibers in the faculty of:**
> - **The Animal**: as above.
> - **The Vital**: for this species of fiber, implanted in the substance of the heart, produces by its action the rest between systole and diastole.
> - **The Natural**: namely, in the external lining of the stomach and intestines, and in the veins and gall bladder, etc., which perform both the retentive and digestive duties.

> **The Expulsive Virtue**: consisting in coldness and moisture; and its constellation is the Moon ☾.
> - **The Animal**: as before.
> - **The Vital**: for the transverse fibers of the heart, by contracting themselves, relax the straight ones, and in this way the heart is indeed contracted and pressed back; this is called **Systole**.
> - **The Natural**: and this species of fiber, holding and constituting the second or middle lining of the stomach and intestines, as well as in the gall bladder, kidneys, etc., provides the expulsive faculty within them.

Just as we have the subject of this distinction from the more skilled and trustworthy Philosophers and Physicians; for indeed Galen made ample mention of it in *On the Power that Dispenses our Body*, <note>Latin: *De virtute nostrum corpus dispensantem*</note> *On the Difference of Symptoms* (chapter 3), <note>Latin: *De symptomatum differentiis*</note> in his *Synopsis on the Pulse* (chapter 34), and in *On Natural Faculties*. <note>Latin: *De naturalibus facultatibus*</note> Likewise, Avicenna <note>A Persian physician (980–1037 AD) whose "Canon of Medicine" was a standard European textbook for centuries.</note> mentioned it in the first book, first doctrine, chapters 8 and 16, and again in chapter 3 and chapter 2. So indeed, regarding the constellations of these virtues, you will find Ptolemy himself speaking in the 86th proposition of the *Centiloquium*. <note>A collection of 100 astrological aphorisms attributed to the famous astronomer Ptolemy.</note> For there he seems to recognize that the Sun is the principle of the faculty of life; Mercury ☿ influences the natural faculty; Venus ♀ gives power to the animal faculty, the imagination, and the senses. Similarly, the beginning of the reductive or retentive faculty is allotted from Saturn ♄; he recognizes Jupiter ♃ as the ruler of the augmentative <note>Growth-related</note> faculty, and Mars ♂ as the ruler of the irascible <note>Related to anger or the "spirited" part of the soul</note> and attractive faculty. Venus ♀ he makes the source of the pleasurable and concupiscible <note>Desire-driven</note> faculty. Furthermore, both he and others ascribe the generative faculty to the influences of Venus, and the vital faculty to the Sun.

Of the humors produced in the natural virtue: Blood is ascribed to Jupiter; natural Choler <note>Yellow bile</note> to the Sun; and that "preternatural" choler to Mars (although some others attribute this humor to the Sun and Mars together). Phlegm is ascribed to the Moon; Melancholy <note>Black bile</note> to Saturn. For they confidently assert that the inferior things of the world depend upon the superior ones, as the passive depends upon the active; maintaining that the acts of the superiors upon the inferiors are performed by means of their influences.

Hence, they also maintain that the **attractive virtue** <term>attractive virtue<gloss>the biological faculty responsible for drawing nutrients into the body or specific organs</gloss></term>, which is temperately hot and dry, resides in the influence of the **Sun** ☉, and not in that of **Mars** ♂; for Mars is, in his own nature, for the most part corrupt. They ascribe the **digestive virtue** to the influences of **Jupiter** ♃, and the **retentive virtue** <note>the faculty that holds substances in place for processing</note> to **Saturn** ♄. Finally, they assign the **expulsive virtue** <note>the faculty responsible for eliminating waste</note> to the **Moon** ☽.

On this point, astrologers say in passing that the **Moon** ☽, among all the other planets, possesses more power and gives more through her influences than any of the others. This is because she is situated closer to us, and by grace of the moisture over which she predominates, she chiefly governs and disposes the humors in the human body. This is all the more true since she has influence over **Phlegm** <note>original: *phlegma* or *pituita*</note>; for phlegm is nothing other than semi-cooked blood, and blood is the prince of the humors. Similarly, **choler** <note>yellow bile</note> is nothing other than the foamy superfluity of the blood, just as phlegm is the watery excess, and **Melancholy** <note>black bile</note> is the dreggy and earthy excess. Therefore, it follows of necessity that the **Moon** ☽ must be most powerful by reason of her influx upon the human body and every humoral thing in the whole world.

Furthermore, it is worth observing that, just as in the ethereal field two planets are numbered which, by themselves, produce no influence (or at least no great one) for the utility and continuation of life—namely **Saturn** ♄ and **Mars** ♂—so too in the body there are noted to be members which contribute very little by themselves to the continuation of life. Instead, they act only "by accident" <note>indirectly or secondary to the main function</note> toward its health. For example, the **gallbladder** <note>original: *cista fellis*</note> receives and attracts to itself burnt choler, so that by this means the remaining members are not inflamed beyond the laws of nature or reduced to a feverish imbalance. Likewise, the **Spleen** <note>original: *splen* or *lien*</note> is a vessel or storehouse ordained for receiving dreggy and melancholic blood. Hence it is that just as **Mars** ♂ has dominion over the gallbladder, so does **Saturn** ♄ over the spleen.

But now, to return to the purpose and turn the use of these constellations—regarding the four aforementioned virtues—toward the preservation of health: we say that the **attractive virtue** (which consists in heat and dryness) ought to be strengthened and comforted when a similar virtue reigns in heaven. For example, when the **Moon** ☽ is in a hot and dry sign, such as **Aries** ♈ or **Sagittarius** ♐. However, one should avoid **Leo** ♌, which is a sign of the Zodiac that is too strong; it has influence over the human heart and consequently the stomach. Therefore, its power is so strong that **Leo** ♌ should not be chosen for medical works, whether the Moon is in it or in the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant<gloss>the degree of the Zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a specific time</gloss></term>; it should not be used for administering laxatives, composing a medicinal mixture <note>original: *confectionis*</note>, or for bloodletting.

For this reason, medicinal mixtures for this work are better made when the Moon is in **Aries** ♈ or **Sagittarius** ♐, and not in **Leo** ♌. But indeed, if one must hasten to fortify and stabilize the **attractive virtue**—or prevent its future weakening—due to a sudden urgent necessity, or if one must cure it when it is already weakened and cannot wait for the presence of the **Moon** ☽ in **Aries** ♈ or **Sagittarius** ♐, let them at least choose a time in which the **Ascendant** of the heavens will be **Aries** ♈ or **Sagittarius** ♐. In this way, the "upper root" <note>the stars</note> may be able to comfort the "lower root" <note>the human body</note>. Similarly, he who wishes to corroborate the **retentive faculty** against a present or future danger shall wait for the time when the **Moon** ☽ enters or is found in a cold and dry sign; for example, when she is in **Taurus** ♉ or **Virgo** ♍, and not in **Capricorn** ♑, as that is a retrograde sign <note>The author likely refers to Capricorn being the "detriment" or "fall" of certain planets, or its association with the winter solstice, rather than the sign itself being retrograde</note>. In this time, therefore, to protect the **retentive faculty** (which the physician suspects is at risk) or to restore it if already weakened, medicinal mixtures and other medicines that serve to strengthen the retentive faculty should be prepared and compounded by the physician or pharmacist.

Furthermore, in my opinion, herbs or plants are to be collected at such a time as they contribute to these kinds of effects. However, where a failure or decrease of the future **concoctive** <note>digestive</note> or **digestive virtue** is foreseen, or a present danger hangs over it, let the Moon be in a hot and moist sign; for example, in **Gemini** ♊, the first half of **Libra** ♎, or **Sagittarius** ♐, when either confections or other medicines...

For that old axiom is well-worn and proven: *United strength is stronger* <note>original: *Vis unita fortior*</note>. This is all the more true because Heaven is the **Male** and the active force, while this lower world is the **female** and the passive recipient. Therefore, if we wish to make this or that impression in wax, it is fitting to choose specifically according to the nature of the thing we wish to imprint. By all means, then, the contrary influences of the Heavens must be fled and avoided; for I ask you, which physician skilled in **Astrology** would attempt to stop a looseness of the bowels with "slippery" things, or mitigate the heat of a burning fever with hot things? Who would try to soften a stomach that is too hard with styptic and constricting things, or aid digestion with things adverse to it, or attempt to attract with things naturally cold and moist?

Since, therefore, every thing is fortified by its own like, one must wait for a constellation to aid a failing virtue, and that constellation must always be of the same nature as the thing to which it must bring help. For like rejoices in its like and is refreshed by it.

Furthermore, we advise the skilled physician by no means to neglect the **Mansions of the Moon** <term>Mansions of the Moon<gloss>28 divisions of the lunar cycle, each thought to have a specific medical or magical influence</gloss></term>, since the Moon in a hot and dry mansion would contribute more to the **attractive virtue**; in a cold and dry one, to the **retentive**; in a hot and moist one, to the **digestive**; and in a cold and moist one, to the **expulsive**. For he will find that the degrees themselves vary in nature within the same sign, as is explained in the Table of the Mansions of the Moon in the section of the Second Treatise concerning **Astrological Curing**.

the business is more favorable when the **Moon** ☽ is more free from all impediments and has a good **aspect** <term>aspect<gloss>The geometric angle between planets that determines their astrological influence</gloss></term> with **Jupiter** ♃ or **Venus** ♀. In this case, the natures of the signs of the Zodiac must also be observed: for when the Moon ☽ is in the **sanguine**, **phlegmatic**, and **airy** signs, it will be good, provided other things do not hinder it. Furthermore, the four quarters of the **Moon** ☽ are not to be neglected in such a case. For in its *first* quarter, which extends from **Aries** ♈ to the first part of **Gemini** ♊, **bloodletting** <note>original: *sanguinis missio*</note> is most suitable for young people. In the *second* quarter, which is from the start of **Gemini** ♊ up to **Leo** ♌, blood is more appropriately drawn in the prime of manhood. In the *third*, which is from **Leo** ♌ to the second part of **Sagittarius** ♐, blood should be drawn from a man of mature age <note>original: *medicæ ætatis*; literally "medical age," referring to middle age or the years of full physical maturity</note>: but truly, where a great necessity urges, a vein may be opened in the elderly from the second part of **Sagittarius** ♐ to **Aries** ♈.

And although these precepts are not to be so strictly observed that they cannot be changed when necessity compels; nevertheless, because the **Moon** ☽, by respect of the constancy of her influence and the closeness of her nature, is most familiar with earthly things: therefore, the human age is also ordered according to the disposition of her own age <note>The "age" of the Moon refers to its phase in the lunar cycle</note>, and for that reason, her ages most closely agree with those living beings.

But truly we say that **bloodletting** is prohibited by the laws of **Astrology** when the **Moon** ☽ is in **Leo** ♌ with the **Dragon’s Head** <term>Dragon’s Head<gloss>The North Node of the Moon (☊), considered a point of amplification or disruption</term>, and that for two days before or after. Similarly, a vein is not conveniently cut for the space of one natural day when the **Moon** ☾ is in **Taurus** ♉ with **Saturn** ♄, the **Sun** ☉, and **Mars** ♂.

But since we have explained the exact condition of the **Moon** in **Phlebotomy** <term>Phlebotomy<gloss>The surgical opening of a vein to withdraw blood for therapeutic purposes</gloss></term> more clearly and lucidly in that *Discourse on Phlebotomy* in the following Treatise, we will not say more about it in this place.

Plainly the same reasoning must be held in the astrological **administration of medicines**: for the moist signs, namely **Cancer** ♋, **Scorpio** ♏, and **Pisces** ♓, are observed to be more favorable for exciting the purgative or **expulsive faculty**. If, therefore, a good and strong **Moon** ☽ passes through these, she will perform her duty in this work: the bowels (I say) will be rendered more **lubricous** <note>original: *lubricior*; slippery or loosened</note>, and the **Moon** ☾, because of this moist disposition of hers, will reject more waste products. She will also perform the very same thing in the **airy signs**, **Gemini** ♊, **Libra** ♎, and **Aquarius** ♒. Indeed, in these, she herself thins the waste products even more.

But truly, Astrological Physicians especially beware of **Leo** ♌, because that sign holds its powers in the heart and the stomach. Therefore, when the **Moon** ☽ is in **Leo** ♌, or when that sign is **ascending** <term>ascending<gloss>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</gloss></term>, a purgative medicine will not work well, because it will be as nauseating to the stomach as the bowels will be found less slippery on account of the dryness of **Leo** ♌.

It will also be a matter of no small importance if, in prescribing medicines, that hour is chosen in which a favorable sign is ascending, and whose ruling planet is positioned **below the earth**. This is the reason why medicines of this sort usually perform better and are observed with greater utility in the Spring and Autumn seasons than they usually are in either Summer or Winter.

Here also we consider it worthy of observation that the **Moon** ☾ passing through **Cancer** ♋ and regarding **Venus** ♀ by **Trine** △ or **Sextile** ⚹ <term>Trine or Sextile<gloss>Harmonious astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees, respectively</gloss></term> strengthens the expulsive virtue, by which **phlegm** is most easily secreted with an **electuary** <term>electuary<gloss>A medicinal paste made by mixing powder with honey or syrup</gloss></term>. If, however, she regards **Jupiter** ♃, she draws out **melancholy**. But truly the **Moon** ☾ being in **Scorpio** ♏ and regarding **Venus** ♀ through a **Trine** △ or **Sextile** ⚹ expels **choler** <note>original: *cholera*; yellow bile</note> with potions. But if she is joined with **Jupiter** ♃ in the same aspects, she assists in the secretion of the **Melancholic humor**.

Similarly, when the **Moon** is in the sign of **Pisces** ♓ and regarding **Venus** ♀ through a **Trine** △ or **Sextile** ⚹, the **choleric humor** is purged more easily and with good success by pills.

But if she regards the **Sun** ☉ and **Mars** ♂, **Melancholy** is better driven downward by pills. Finally, it must be known that the choleric nature of **Leo** ♌ is better excreted by the virtue of **Venus** ♀: just as that Melancholic nature of **Saturn** is excreted by the heat and moisture of **Jupiter** ♃: and so on in the others.

### On the heavenly method for preserving health.

The procedure is more favorable when the **Moon** <term>☾</term> is more free from all hindrances and has a good aspect with **Jupiter** <term>♃</term> or **Venus** <term>♀</term> <note>aspects are the angles planets make to each other, influencing their power</note>. The natures of the Zodiac signs must also be observed in this case: for with the **Moon** existing in the sanguine <note>associated with blood and air</note>, phlegmatic <note>associated with water</note>, and aerial signs, it will be good, provided other things do not stand in the way; and also in **Cancer** <term>♋</term>. The quarters of the **Moon** in such a case are not to be disregarded. For in its *first* quarter, which extends from **Aries** <term>♈</term> to the first part of **Gemini** <term> Gemini ♊</term>, the letting of blood <note>original: *sanguinis missio*</note> is most suitable for youths. In the *second* quarter, which is from the first part of **Gemini** to **Leo** <term>♌</term>, blood is more properly drawn in the age of manhood. In the *third* quarter, which is from **Leo** to the second part of **Sagittarius** <term>♐</term>, blood should be drawn from a person of mature age <note>original: *medica ætatis*, literally "medical age"</note>; but indeed, where a great necessity urges, a vein may be opened in the elderly from the second part of **Sagittarius** to **Aries**.

And although these precepts are not to be so strictly observed that they cannot be changed when necessity compels; nevertheless, because the Moon—with respect to the constancy of its influence and the proximity of its nature—is most familiar with earthly things: therefore, the human age is also ordered according to the disposition of the Moon's age, and for this reason the Moon's phases most closely agree with those living beings.

But indeed, we say that *bloodletting* is prohibited by astrological laws when the **Moon** is in **Aries** with the **Sun** <term>☉</term>, and that for two days before or after. Similarly, the **Moon** in **Taurus** <term>♉</term> with **Saturn** <term>♄</term> passing through is not good; likewise it is not good in **Gemini** with the **Sun**, **Saturn**, and **Mars** <term>♂</term>, specifically for a space of 12 hours before or after. Similarly, a vein is not conveniently cut for the space of one natural day when the **Moon** is in **Leo** with **Saturn**, the **Sun**, and **Mars**.

But since we have explained the exact condition of the Moon in phlebotomy more clearly and lucidly in that *Discourse on Phlebotomy which follows this treatise*, we will not say more about it in this place.

Plainly the same reasoning must be held in the astrological *administration of medicines*: for the moist signs—namely **Cancer**, **Scorpio** <term>♏</term>, and **Pisces** <term>♓</term>—are observed to be more favorable for exciting the purgative or expulsive faculty. If, therefore, the **Moon** passes through these signs, being good and strong, it will perform its duty in this work: the bowels (I say) will be rendered more slippery, and the **Moon**, on account of this moist disposition of hers, will reject more waste. She will also provide the same effect in the aerial signs **Gemini**, **Libra** <term>♎</term>, and **Aquarius** <term>♒</term>. Indeed, in these signs, she thins out the waste products even more.

But the astrological physicians especially guard against the **Dragon's Head** <term>☊</term> <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, because it has its power in the heart and the stomach. Wherefore, when the **Moon** is in **Leo**, or when that sign is ascending, a purgative medicine will not work well, because it will be as nauseating <note>original: *fastidiosum*</note> to the stomach as the bowels will be found less slippery due to the dryness of the **Dragon's Head**.

It will also be a matter of no small importance if, in the offering of medicines, that hour is chosen in which a favorable sign is ascending, and whose planet is positioned below the earth. This is the reason that medicines of this sort usually provide more, and are observed with greater utility in the spring and autumn, than they usually are in summer or winter.

Here we also consider it worthy of observation that the **Moon** passing through **Cancer** and regarding **Venus** by a **trine** <term>△</term> or **sextile** <term>✶</term> aspect strengthens the expulsive power, by which phlegm is most easily separated with an electuary <note>a medicinal paste made with honey or syrup</note>. If, however, she looks upon **Jupiter**, she draws out melancholy <note>black bile</note>. But indeed, the **Moon** being in **Scorpio** and looking toward **Venus** by a **trine** or **sextile** expels choler <note>yellow bile</note> through potions. But if she is joined with **Jupiter** in the same aspects, she assists in the secretion of the melancholic humor.

Similarly, when the **Moon** is waxing in the sign of **Pisces** and looking toward **Venus** through a **trine** or **sextile**, the choleric humor is purged more easily and with good success by pills.

But if she looks toward the **Sun** and **Mars**, melancholy is better driven downward by pills. Finally, it must be known that the choleric nature of **Mars** is better excreted by the power of **Venus**; just as that melancholic nature of **Saturn** is excreted by the hot and moist nature of **Jupiter**: and so it is with the rest.

But since we have spoken more fully about the timing for choosing purgative medicines <note>original: "medicamentorum purgantium"</note> in the following volume, where we treated medicines in general, we shall not speak further of these matters in this place.

But now we shall come to the favorable times and constellations for baths and the washing of bodies.

If anyone wishes to wash in a bath for the sake of cleansing themselves from uncleanness or stench, I advise that they first see whether the **Moon** <term>☾</term> is traveling through **Gemini** <term>♊︎</term> or **Pisces** <term>♓︎</term>, and if **Venus** <term>♀</term> applies herself with a benevolent aspect. For such a time will be most excellently adapted to a business of that kind.

But if a healthy person wishes to wash themselves or refresh themselves in a bath because of a fear of some imbalance <note>original: "intemperiei," referring to an imbalance of the four bodily humors</note> which might happen to them, it must first be seen whether that future imbalance is likely to arise from dryness, or humidity, or some other humor. For if drying medicines are required for such a future disease—for example, where paralysis or dropsy <note>original: "hydropsis," a condition of swelling caused by excess fluid</note> threatens—it will be necessary to wait for that time in which the **Moon** <term>☾</term> inhabits some fire sign, and has a suitable aspect or radiation with **Mars** <term>♂</term> and the **Sun** <term>☉</term> being well-disposed and fortunate.

If, however, the future disease requires moistening medicines, observe the time in which the **Moon** <term>☾</term> passes through some humid sign, and regards **Venus** <term>♀</term> and **Jupiter** <term>♃</term> with some favorable aspect. Such conditions (I say) and such precepts a Physician ought to observe and follow if he advises a healthy person to enter the baths for the precaution of some future disease.

Finally, in the trimming <note>original: "præfectione," a finishing or grooming</note> of the hair and nails, it is a matter of the greatest importance to gather the times of the **Moon** and the heavenly constellations through which she passes, so that by observing them rightly, such superfluities of nature may grow more slowly or more quickly in a healthy person. More slowly (I say) when the strength of the healthy is weakened by their prompt increase, and they are even rendered more slender; as I myself observed in a certain most noble woman, whose hair multiplied so much in length and abundance that her strength was greatly cast down by the sheer mass of it, and her face, along with her whole body, was consumed by an unbecoming thinness. This indeed happened not only from natural inclination, but perhaps because the hair was trimmed in an evil hour and during the waxing of the **Moon**. For when they were later trimmed and shortened in a well-chosen hour, they did not grow so suddenly.

But truly, on the other hand, when baldness is present, or where the hair is thin, one must choose a time for cutting or a constellation in which they may afterwards grow in greater abundance. In the former case, therefore, the hair should be cut while the **Moon** is waning and existing in **Capricorn** <term>♑︎</term>.

Furthermore, if you wish to prohibit a more exuberant growth of hair, let their trimming be instituted under the signs of **Cancer** <term>♋︎</term>, **Virgo** <term>♍︎</term>, or **Pisces** <term>♓︎</term>, with a favorable aspect nonetheless accompanying. Moreover, where the cutting of hair is done at such a time, they will grow back later and be preserved from rot.

But indeed in the other case, where the hair is to be nourished for the sake of adornment, let their trimming be done while the **Moon** <term>☾</term> is waxing and in a "hairy sign" <note>constellations traditionally associated with hair growth</note>; such are **Gemini** <term> Gemini ♊︎</term>, **Virgo** <term>♍︎</term>, and **Libra** <term>♎︎</term>, with a good aspect existing between her and **Venus** <term>♀</term> and **Jupiter** <term>♃</term>.

Finally, in the trimming of the nails, this is to be observed: so that they do not grow back so suddenly, some are accustomed to shorten them during the waning of the **Moon**. Some, however, for the better strengthening of the nails after cutting, and to prevent them from falling into the affliction of abscesses <note>original: "Apostematum," inflammatory swellings or sores</note>, are accustomed to cut them while the **Moon** <term>☾</term> is waxing and has her station in the houses of **Venus** <term>♀</term> and the **Sun** <term>☉</term> <note>the "houses" are the zodiac signs ruled by or associated with those planets</note>.

### CHAPTER X.

#### *On the selection of months and days for matters pertaining to health.*

Indeed, the selection of months and days in this matter is not frivolous or vain, since we find even the most holy scriptures inclined toward this purpose in some way: namely, that one month, day, or hour of the year is more unlucky or less favorable for this or that than another. Hence Christ says: *My time has not yet come*. <note>original: "Nondum venit tempus meum"</note> And elsewhere: *His hour had not yet come*. And the Apostle says: *that you may be able to resist the attacks of the Devil on the evil day*. <margin>Job 7:8, 8:26 <note>These likely refer to the Gospel of John, despite the label "Job."</note>; Ephesians 6:12; Ecclesiastes 7:14.</margin> And the Wise Man says: *In the good day enjoy good things, and beware the evil day*. For God made both this and that, so that man may not find just complaints against Him. By these examples it is evident, and confirmed by the tested doctrine of ancient wisdom, that times are found to be as lucky as they are unlucky for carrying out this or that in the world.

Therefore, the observation of the Ancients in many things, and especially in the preservation of health <note>original: "sanitatis tuitione"</note>, is that one month differs from another, and within that, one day from another; and within a day, one hour may be more unfortunate than another. Hence, taught by experience, they maintain that in the month of:

*January:* Drinking white wine is suitable. Bloodletting <term>phlebotomia</term> is forbidden, especially on its dangerous days: which are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 15th, 19th, and 20th.

*February:* They forbid the release of blood in the vein of the thumb, nor (unless necessity <note>original: "Necessitas"</note> urges) should bloodletting be performed on its dangerous days, which are the 12th and 29th.

*March:* Eat figs, raisins, and other sweet foods and drinks. The 17th day is considered bad.

*April:* Bloodletting is suitable: especially in the right arm, and particularly where weakness of vision is feared. Bloodletting on the third day is suitable for a headache. In this month, let the food be fresh and warm.

*May:* Rise at daybreak; use warm food and drink. Do not eat the feet or brains of animals. Do not perform bloodletting on dangerous days: which are the 7th, 15th, 16th, and 20th. However, it is suitable on the 4th, 5th, or 6th, and at the end of the month. Bloodletting may be performed in either arm to either prevent or drive away illness.

*June:* Every day on an empty stomach drink a good draught of cold water, and be moderate in eating. Abstain, if you can, from bloodletting: and especially on the 7th day, which is dangerous.

*July:* Abstain from sexual intercourse <note>original: "coitu"</note>; because the humors <note>The "humors" were the four vital fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—thought to control health.</note> rise to the brain. Abstain from bloodletting, and especially on the 15th and 16th days, which are called malevolent.

*August:* Do not lose blood on the dangerous days: which are the 19th and 20th.

*September:* Ripe fruit is helpful: and the 17th day is most suitable for bloodletting to treat dropsy <note>original: "Hydrope," an accumulation of fluid in the body</note>, fever, or paralysis.

*October:* Mead <note>original: "Mulsum," a mixture of wine and honey</note> and wine are suitable. Bloodletting is not as beneficial: especially on the 6th day, which is dangerous.

*November:* Beware of these days, the 15th and 19th, on which you should not enter hot baths.

*December:* Eat warm foods. Let bloodletting be performed if necessity compels it. Its dangerous days are two: the 2nd and 17th.

And let these things suffice for us regarding conjectural matters of this kind in astrology, which especially lead to the preservation of health and the restoration of a healthy body.

Now indeed we shall proceed to a more certain business in astrology, which shows the method and reason by which a skilled physician can better and more easily penetrate the inner workings of a healthy nature, and think more rightly about preventing diseases that may occur in the future.

The choice of months and days in this matter is by no means frivolous or empty, since we find the Sacred Scriptures themselves somewhat inclined toward this purpose: namely, that every month, day, and hour may be more unlucky than another, or less propitious for this or that task. From these things it is evident, and confirmed by the experienced doctrine of ancient wisdom, that times are found to be both favorable and unfavorable for carrying out various things in the world.

Therefore, it was the observation of the Ancients in many matters, and especially in the protection of health, that one month is different from another; and within that month, one day from another; and within the day, one hour may be more unhappy than another. Hence, taught by experience, they maintain that:

*In the month of January:* The drinking of white wine is suitable. <term>Phlebotomy</term> <note>The medical practice of bloodletting, intended to balance the body's humors.</note> is forbidden, especially on its dangerous days, which are: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 15, 19, 20.

*In March:* Eat figs, raisins, and other sweet foods and drinks. The 17th day is considered bad.

*In April:* Bloodletting is suitable, especially in the right arm, and particularly where a weakness of sight is feared. Phlebotomy on the third day is good for a headache. In this month, let the food be fresh and warm.

*In May:* Rise at daybreak; use warm foods and drink. Do not eat the feet or brains of animals. Let no bloodletting be done on the dangerous days, which are the 7th, 15, 16, and 20th. But on the 4th, 5th, or 6th days, and at the end of the month, it is favorable. Phlebotomy may be performed in either arm to either prevent or drive away illness.

*In June:* Every day on an empty stomach, drink a good draught of cold water, and be moderate in eating. Abstain, if you can, from bloodletting—especially on the 7th day, which is dangerous.

*In July:* Abstain from sexual intercourse, because the humors rise to the brain. Abstain from bloodletting, especially on the 15th and 16th days, which are called malevolent.

*In August:* Do not lose blood on the dangerous days, which are the 19th and 20th.

*In September:* Ripe fruit is helpful; and the 17th day is most suitable for bloodletting for <term>dropsy</term> <note>original: "Hydrope," an old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid.</note>, fever, or <term>paralysis</term>.

*In November:* Beware of these days, the 15th and 19th, on which you should not enter hot baths.

*In December:* Eat warm foods. Let bloodletting be done only if necessity compels it. Its dangerous days are two: the 2nd and 17th.

### CHAPTER I.
->*How, once the revelation of a Birth is known, anyone skilled in Astrology may easily prevent future health evils.*<-

<margin>Book 5 of the Centiloquium.</margin>
<note>The Centiloquium is a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Ptolemy, though now believed to be by a later author.</note>
Although we do not say that what we propose here arises from necessity <note>The author is likely distancing himself from "fatalistic" astrology, which suggests the stars force human actions, favoring instead the idea that stars "incline" but do not "compel."</note>, nevertheless, to set it forth according to the course of Nature is indeed quite probable. Hence Ptolemy, that skilled and wise Astrologer, says: *much evil can be hindered, which is ordained to happen through the course of the stars, if one understands their disposition beforehand.* Once these things are known by him, it will not be difficult to prevent the evil which indeed looms through the constellation of one's **Birth** <note>original: "Natiuitatis"</note>; thus verifying that well-worn axiom, *The wise man will rule the stars.* <note>original: "Sapiens dõminabitur astris." This was a popular medieval and Renaissance motto suggesting that through reason and foresight, humans can overcome celestial influences.</note> For example: If a person is healthy by nature but, from the disposition of their constellation, is apt to fall into some hot and dry or bilious <term>bilious: related to yellow bile, one of the four "humors" believed to cause heat and irritability in the body</term> infirmity, a shrewd physician in this case can meet this evil by administering alterative <term>alterantia: medicines intended to gradually alter the body’s condition, usually to restore balance to the humors</term> medicines while the subject is still healthy. The effect of these medicines is to cool and moisten: these are mostly to be applied at that time when the Moon is in its moist and cold quarter <note>the phase of the moon associated with these qualities</note>, and in such a mansion <note>a "lunar mansion" is one of the 28 divisions of the sky the moon passes through</note>, or at least while the Moon is migrating through and existing in one of the cold signs. The healthy person ought to use such medicines for a good span of time before the evil period in which such danger is threatened: for in this way, the malevolent effect of the future constellation will either be totally annihilated, or at least its influence will be wonderfully mitigated and weakened.

### CHAPTER III.
->*What must be done when the hour and degree of birth are not known.*<-

In such a case, according to the teachings of Ptolemy in the *Quadripartitum*; <note>original: "Quadripartito." This refers to Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational four-book text of Western astrology.</note> one must judge and operate by a conjecture of the hour of life and the minute, and this as certainly as we are able: which we shall indeed perform based on the uncertain hour.

Arrange the celestial houses as perfectly as possible, and let the planets be placed in them, as is the custom of the art. Then I would have you look at which planet is strongest in the figure made upon the place of the conjunction [☌] <term>conjunction: when two celestial bodies appear in the same place in the sky</term> of the luminaries <note>The "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.</note>, or the opposition [☍] <term>opposition: when two celestial bodies are 180 degrees apart</term> occurring immediately before the Birth. Once this planet of greater strength is found, consider its place in the presupposed Chart of Birth: and note how many degrees and minutes in the Sign in which it was at the time of that birth it has traversed. Then take this as your foundation: namely, that the planet which has greater strength in the hour of conjunction [☌] or opposition [☍] ought to be placed and expressed in the same degree of the said Sign in which the presupposed birth was; in whatever degrees it was found in any sign. 

For example: The conjunction [☌] of the luminaries immediately preceding the birth might be in the 4th degree of Leo [♌]. Jupiter [♃], however, is there at the place of conjunction with the greatest power, and consequently, is the Lord. Then you must look at how many degrees Jupiter has traveled in the Sign in which it was found at the hour of birth; as if it had made 6 degrees and 2 minutes of Leo [♌], then Jupiter is at the end of the 7th degree of Leo [♌] at the hour of birth. You will take this as your foundation: that the planet which is stronger than the others in the place of the Sun [☉] at the hour of conjunction is at the 7th degree of the Sign at the hour of birth—in the sign of the hour of birth, and not the hour of conjunction or opposition, but of the birth: and this will be the first foundation.

The second foundation of the investigation of the true degree of the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> of any Birth is this: Observe the Figure or Celestial Chart made by conjecture to find the Ascendant of the Birth, and then seek in what place of the Heaven the planet is which has the greater virtue in the Heaven at the place of the conjunction [☌] and the hour of the conjunction, and to which of the two angles—that is, whether to the Ascendant or to the Midheaven [Medii Coeli] <term>Midheaven: the highest point in the sky at the time of birth</term>—that planet is closer. 

(For example: if the Moon [☾] is found through the presupposed Figure to be closer to the angle of the 10th house, then the 7th degree of the presupposed sign is the beginning of the 10th house. And if the Planet at the hour of birth is closer to the angle of the Ascendant, then the entire figure ought to be formed in such a way: that the 7th degree of the presupposed sign should be the Ascendant; and so from the 30 degrees of any Sign which were at the beginning of the work, whether due to a defect of the clock, or due to the negligence of those who ought to have observed the true minute of the hour at Birth.) And through this way is known and found without doubt the proper degree through the strength of the place of conjunction [☌] or opposition [☍] and through the proximity of the Planet to the two said angles at the hour of Birth.

### CHAPTER I.

->*How, once the revelation of a birth is known, someone skilled in astrology may easily prevent future health problems.*<-

<margin>Book 5 of the *Centiloquium*</margin>
<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'Q' featuring leafy vines and floral patterns.</image-desc>Although we do not say that what we propose here arises from absolute necessity, it is nevertheless very probable when put forward according to the course of Nature. Hence, Ptolemy, that skilled and wise astrologer, says that much evil can be prevented which is ordained to happen through the course of the stars, if one understands their disposition beforehand. For once those things are known by him, it will not be difficult to anticipate the evil which truly threatens through the constellation of one's birth; thus verifying that well-worn axiom: *The wise man shall rule the stars.* <note>original: "Sapiens dominabitur astris." This was a popular medieval and Renaissance maxim suggesting that while stars influence the physical body, a person using reason and medical knowledge can overcome their fate.</note> For example: if someone is healthy by nature and yet, from the arrangement of their birth constellation, is prone to fall into some "hot and dry" or bilious <note>Relating to yellow bile, one of the four humors; associated with a fiery, irritable, or feverish temperament.</note> infirmity, a shrewd physician can meet this evil in such a case. While the person is still healthy, the doctor can administer altering medicines whose nature is to cool and moisten. These should mostly be used at the time when the Moon [☾] is in its moist and cold quarter and in such a "mansion" <term>mansion: one of the 28 divisions of the lunar orbit, used to determine the best timing for medical treatments</term>, or at least while she is traveling through and located in one of the cold signs. The healthy person ought to use such medicines for a good length of time before the period of illness that is threatened; for in this way, the malevolent effect of the future constellation will either be totally wiped out or, at the very least, its influence will be wonderfully softened and weakened.

### CHAPTER II.

->*What a "Birth Revolution" is: And once it is first known, what must be done afterward.*<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'I' with decorative foliage.</image-desc>First, therefore, so that we may reach the perfection of this knowledge and science, we must know what a "Birth Revolution" <term>Birth Revolution: known today as a Solar Return, this is a chart cast for the exact moment the Sun returns to the exact position it held at the moment of birth</term> is, and how it is correctly understood by the astrologer. We must observe the degree of the sign or the line of the Ecliptic where the Sun [☉] was located at the hour of birth; indeed, if possible, the very minute of time in which the infant was born. For example: an infant is born with the Sun being in the fourth degree of Leo [♌] with certain minutes of that same degree; then the place in which the Sun is found will be called the "degree of birth," not only at the child's delivery, but also through the entire span of his life. Therefore, when the Sun reaches that same 4th degree of Leo [♌] with its minutes in the following year, that is called the "Revolution" of that birth. And so it goes for each successively following year, during...

### CHAPTER III.

### *What must be done when the hour and degree of birth are not known.*

**I**n such a case, according to the teachings of Ptolemy in the *Tetrabiblos* <note>original: "Quadripartito". This is the foundational text of Western astrology written by Claudius Ptolemy in the 2nd century.</note>, one must judge and work by estimating the hour of life and the minutes, and this as accurately as we can; which indeed we shall perform upon an uncertain hour as follows:

Arrange the celestial houses as perfectly as possible, and let the planets be placed in them according to the rules of the art. Then I would have you look at which planet is strongest in the figure made for the place of the conjunction [☌] <note>When two planets appear in the same spot in the sky.</note> of the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>, or the opposition [☍] <note>When two planets are 180 degrees apart.</note> occurring immediately before the birth. Having found this planet of greater strength, consider its place in the assumed birth chart: and note how many degrees and minutes it has traversed in the Sign in which it is at that time of birth. Then take this as your foundation: namely, that the planet which has greater strength at the hour of conjunction or opposition should be placed and expressed in the same degree of the said Sign in which the assumed birth occurred, in whatever degrees it was found in any sign.

For example: the conjunction of the luminaries immediately preceding the birth might be in the 4th degree of Jupiter [♃] <note>Refers to a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by Jupiter.</note>. Mars [♂], however, is in that place of conjunction and has the greatest power; consequently, he is the Lord <note>The ruling planet of that specific point in the zodiac.</note>. Then you must look at how many degrees Mars has traveled in the Sign where he is found at the hour of birth; for instance, if he has reached 6 degrees and 2 minutes of Leo [♌], then Mars is at the end of the 7th degree of Leo at the birth hour. You will take this as your basis: that the planet which is stronger than the others at the place of the Sun at the hour of Mars [the ruler] is in the 7th degree of the Sign where it resides at the hour of birth—not at the hour of conjunction or opposition, but at the birth itself; and this will be the first foundation.

*The second foundation for investigating the true degree of the Ascendant of any birth is as follows.* Observe the figure or celestial chart made by estimation to find the birth Ascendant, and then seek where in the heavens that planet is which has the greater virtue in the place of conjunction and the hour of Mars [the ruler], and to which of the two angles it is closer—that is, the Ascendant or the Midheaven <note>original: "medij Cœli". The highest point of the chart, representing one's status or the south.</note>. (For example: If Mars is found through the assumed chart to be closer to the angle of the 10th house [the Midheaven], then the 7th degree of the assumed sign is the beginning of the 10th house.) And if the planet at the hour of birth is closer to the angle of the Ascendant, then the whole figure must be formed in such a way that the 7th degree of the assumed sign becomes the Ascendant. Thus, one corrects the 30 degrees of any Sign that were at the start of the work, whether due to a failure of the clock or the negligence of those who ought to have observed the true minute of the hour at the birth. And by this way, the proper degree is known and found without doubt through the strength of the place of conjunction or opposition, and by the proximity of the planet to the two said angles at the hour of birth.

But to make the explanation of this matter even clearer, we shall place this example before your eyes.

A child was born on the 27th of February, on the day and hour of Venus [♀], which was on the 27th of February in the hour of Jupiter [♃]. <note>This identifies the planetary rulers of the day and specific hour of birth, a standard way of tracking time before mechanical clocks were reliable.</note> Let it be that the figure of the conjunction of the Sun [☉] and Moon [☾] immediately preceding this birth was in Pisces [♓] at 15 degrees and 16 minutes, and that Venus has the greatest strength there—namely, by Triplicity and Exaltation <note>Technical terms for a planet's dignity or "strength" based on its zodiacal position.</note> in the place of the conjunction. And at the previously assumed hour of birth, Venus was at 2 degrees and 12 minutes of Aquarius [♒], which is in the 3rd degree of Aquarius, near...

### CHAPTER IV.

->In which the judgment, or the method of preventing future evils through the true observation of the birth hour, is discussed.<-

Once the health of the person born is known in this way, and the degree of the Ascendant <note>The sign and degree rising on the eastern horizon at birth, considered the most important point for physical health.</note> is thus found, and the other planets are duly arranged in their houses, a most fitting preparation will have been made for foreseeing and acting in advance against many troubles in the annual revolution <note>Also known as a Solar Return, this is a chart cast for the exact moment the Sun returns to its birth position each year to predict that year's events.</note> which may hinder the health of the subject. For example: if eclipses of the Sun [☉] and Moon [☽] occurred at the degree of the Ascendant at birth, or near it—that is, not distant from it by more than 2 or 3 degrees—before the person’s birth, it suggests that some danger will happen within the space of half a year or sooner.

And that malevolent event, whether it be a disease or some other accident, will be greater and more dangerous if the eclipse occurs exactly in the angle of the Ascendant within the number of degrees mentioned above. And if the promised evil happens after those degrees, the event will not be so dangerous, but the person will nonetheless be in peril. The same is to be understood regarding Mars [♂] and Saturn [♄]: yet these would not bring such great harm if they were at the degree of the Ascendant, or near it, at the same time in the years of the revolution. And they will be all the more dangerous the more they are unfortunate, retrograde, or combust <note>original: "combusti". A planet is "combust" when it is too close to the Sun, which was thought to "burn up" or weaken its influence.</note>.

But indeed, to begin the discourse on diseases future to the subject: once the birth and the degree of the Ascendant are found and arranged in a Figure <note>An astrological chart or diagram.</note> in the usual manner, and the figure is adorned with the presence of the planets, the dispositions of the 6th and 8th Houses <note>In medical astrology, the 6th house governs illness and daily labor, while the 8th governs death, crisis, and surgery.</note> must be diligently observed. It must be seen in what place their Lords <note>The "Lord" is the planet that rules the zodiac sign found on the cusp (entrance) of a house.</note> are, and whether they are strong, and if they regard the Moon or the malevolent planets with a malevolent aspect—namely a square [□] or opposition [☍]. You must seek diligently if they make an unfortunate application <note>An "application" occurs when a faster-moving planet approaches an aspect with a slower one, indicating an event about to happen.</note> with the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Lord of the subject's life. Above all, it must be inquired in which quarter of the year, and then in which month, week, day, and hour the greatest danger will loom in the year of revolution. For through a diligent inquiry of this kind, one skilled in Astrological Medicine <note>original: "Medicinę Astrologicę".</note> is accustomed to predicting the time of future evil. Furthermore, the place or member of the body threatened, and the nature of the future disease, will be very easily recognized by observing the nature of the sign of the house in which the planet that is the Lord of the 6th is found; that sign will indicate the member to be affected by the evil, just as the sign occupying the 6th house will declare the quality and condition of the foreseen disease.

As for which member in the human body each sign in the Zodiac claims for itself, as well as the conditions of said signs and what diseases they are accustomed to produce in the human body, we shall speak most fully in the following Treatise, where the celestial cause of diseases will be discussed.

It should be noted in passing that the more "testimonies" <note>Pieces of astrological evidence or indicators.</note> of health found in the birth or the revolution, the fewer diseases you will judge the subject to be liable to; the more testimonies of infirmity, the more diseases. And it very often happens that Saturn [♄] or Mars [♂] is the author of the diseases, either individually or both together. For example: if one of them is the Lord in the revolution or the birth, either of the Horoscope <note>The Ascendant.</note> or the 6th house.

Nor indeed should it escape the skilled Physician that the remaining planets besides Saturn [♄] and Mars [♂] are said to be afflicted in two ways: namely by their own weakness or by malignant rays...
